【8】**Atherosclerotic narrowing： This diagnosis would be unlikcly in a young patient and would not be expected to cause the symptoms mentioned above. 【12】**KEY FACTS**

【13】**_CLINICAL_**

【14】**◆IDissections cause approximately 1% to 2% of all strokes in the general population but between 5% and 20% of strokes among patients <40 years old.**

【15】**◆Dissection can occur after trauma， on a spontaneous basis， or after movements of the head or neck that are generally considered benign (“trivial trauma”).**

【16】**Headache or neckache is present in about 75% of patients. Oculosympathetic paresis (Horner’s syn-drome) is commonly seen in ICA dissection.**

【17】**Transient ischemic attacks and completed strokes occur in a minority of patients.**

【18】**_◆Subarachnoid hemorrhage can accompany intracranial_ dissections，**

**◆The most common sites are the cervical portion of the ICA (within a few centimeters of the carotid bifurca-|删除0换行|tion) and the vertebral artery at the level of the C1-2vertebral bodies.**

【20】**Anticoagulation for a period of a few months is usu-ally performed when subarachnoid hemorrhage is not present.**

【21】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【22】**◆The most common finding at catheter angiography is a site of smooth or irregular narrowing extending over a few centimeters in length. Other catheter angiography findings can include pseudoaneurysm formation， arter-ial occlusion， and， less commonly， an intimal flap. A double-lumen appearance is rarc.**

【23】**The typical MRI finding is a narrowed arterial lumen(flow void) with an adjacent crescentic area of abnor-mal signal (usually hyperintense on Tl-and T2-weighted images).**

【24】**At MR angiography， a narrowed arterial signal column， frequently with an adjacent region of hyperintense sig-nal aligned parallel to the artery， can often be seen.**

【25】**◆Diagnostic features at ultrasonography include an echogenic intimal flap (the most specific sign， but present in only a minority of cases) and echogenic thrombus.**

【26】**_◆_ CT is not usually performed to establish the diagnosis， but contrast-enhanced CT can demonstrate a nar-rowed arterial lumen with an eccentric region of mural thickening.**

【27】**◆Resolution or significant improvement at the time of a repeat imaging study performed a few weeks later is seen in about 80% of treated cases.**

【33】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【34】**◆Meningioma： This might be considered because the lesion is extra-axial and denscly contrast-enhances. However， this diagnosis would not account for the abnormal signal in both temporal lobes.**

【35】**Craniopharyngioma： This diagnosis might be consid-ered because a portion of the mass extends into the suprasellar cistern. However， craniopharyngiomas are typically cystic， often calcified， and do not generally diffusely contrast-enhance.**

【36】**◆Epidermoid cyst： This diagnosis might be considered because of the extra-axial suprasellar location of the lesion. However， epidermoids usually appear moder-ately hyperintense on T2-weighted images and do not contrast-cnhancc.**

【37】**Pituitary adenoma： On Figure 6-22B， the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland is seen between the two internal carotid arteries (ICAs). The lesion is clearly separate from the pituitary gland.**

【38】**◆**

【39】**Aneurysm： This diagnosis should be considered when a mass lesion is seen in the region of the circle of Willis. A widc rangc of signal intensities can be seen due to slow blood flow within an aneurysm or partial or complete thrombosis. Therefore， the fact that a nor-mal flow void is not present in the lesion by no means excludes this diagnosis. The abnormal signal seen in the temporal lobes is a clue to the correct diagnosis. This signal is due to pulsation artifact in the phase-encoding direction produced by flow within the mass， which is an aneurysm.**

【40】**DIAGNOSIS： Giant aneurysm.**

【41】**◆ KEY FACTS**

【42】**_CLINICAL_**

【43】**◆Giant aneurysms are >25 mm in diametcr and account for approximately 5% of all intracranial aneurysms.**

【44】**Presentation usually is in the fourth through sixth decadcs. Giant aneurysms typically become sympto-matic due to mass effect on adjacent intracranial struc-tures (which may raise clinical suspicion of a neoplasm) rather than aneurysmal rupture.**

【45】**Giant intracranial aneurysms are associated with sub-stantial neurologic morbidity or death within 5 years of diagnosis if untreated.**

【46】**The optimal treatment options include (1) clipping of the neck of the aneurysm with preservation of the par-ent vessel， or (2) endovascular occlusion of the aneurysm by balloons or embolic coils. Less optimally， carotid artery ligation or wrapping of the aneurysm is performed in the uncommon instance in which the aneurysm cannot be treated definitively.**

【47】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【48】**◆About half of giant aneurysms involve the ICA and its distal branches. The most common sites in the carotid circulation are near the origin of the ophthalmic artery， ICA bifurcation， and cavernous segment of the ICA. The most freouent sites in the vertebrobasilar system are at the tip of the basilar artery， junction of the basilar and superior cerebellar arteries， and vertebrobasilar junction.**

【49】**◆At catheter angiography， partially thrombosed giant aneurysms often appear smaller than their actual size， which can be more accurately defined by CT and MRI.**

【50】**◆The CT and MRI appearance of a giant aneurysm can be mistaken for a tumor. In particular， giant ancurysms in the parasellar region and at other sites near the skull base can be mistaken for a meningioma. It is impor-tant to consider this entity in the differential diagnosis of masses in these regions if inadvertent biopsy or improper surgery is to be avoided.**

【51】**On noncontrast CT， ancurysms appcar as roundcd or oval masses that are relatively isodense or， frequently， hyperdense relative to adjacent brain tissue. Partially thrombosed aneurysms often have a hyperintense cres-centic rim. Occasionally， the rim of an aneurysm can be seen to be calcified. Following contrast administra-tion， nonthrombosed aneurysis densely and homoge-neously contrast-enhance， while generally only the patent lumen of partially thrombosed aneurysms densely contrast-enhances.**

【52】**◆On MRI， a nonthrombosed aneurysm is seen as an oval or spherical extra-axial region of absent signal(flow void)， continuous with a vessel. Partially thrombed aneurysms typically have a laminated appear-ance， due to layers of hemorrhage of different age. Occasionally， a thin circumferential region of abnormal perianeurysmal signal duc to chronic hemorrhagic products can be seen.**

【53】**◆An important clue that a mass lesion secn on MRI is an ancurysm is a band of pulsation artifact extending from thc aneurysm into adjacent tissues along the phase-encoding axis. This artifact is often increased after administration of contrast material .**

This mass has grown superiorly， expanding the infundibular orifice of the diaphragma sella， producing a bilobed appcarancc.**

【69】**DIAGNOSIS： Pituitary macroadenoma.**

【70】**KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【71】**◆Adenomas are the most common neoplasm of the pituitary gland and arisc in the adenohypophysis (ante-rior lobe of the pituitary gland). They comprise 10% to15% of all intracranial tumors.**

【72】**◆1Many hormonally active pituitary adenomas become clinically apparent whilc small. Three-fourths of all adenomas present with signs and symptoms related to hormonal overproduction.**

**Many nonfunctioning tumors grow to largc size before producing symptoms. Onc-fourth of all adenomas pre-sent with symptoms due to mass effect-e.g.， headache，|删除0换行|visual field defects， cranial nerve palsies， and cerc-brospinal fluid (CSF) rhinorrhea due to sellar erosion**

【74】**◆Hormonally active adenomas may secrete prolactin， thyroid-stimulating hormone， growth hormone， adrenocorticotropic hormone， follicle-stimulating hor-monc， and luteinizing hormone， alone or in various combinations. Hormonally inactive adenonas have been termed “null cell” adenomas or oncocytomas.**

【75】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【76】**◆Unless contraindicated， MRI is generally considered the first-linc imaging study for detection of pituitary adenomas.**

【77】**◆During the evalutation of the lesion of the sellar/juxtasel-lar region， thc radiologist’s role is to establish the center of the lesion and its relationship to adjacent structures. Rclevant fcatures include the relation to the optic struc-tures， course and caliber of the cavernous segment of the ICAs， and whether the cavernous sinuses are invadcd.**

【78】**_◆_ Pituitary adenomas can be diagnosed on any MRI pulse sequence， but contrast-enhanccd Tl-weighted images in the coronal plane are probably the technique that is most widely accepted. Nonetheless， they can be detected on noncontrast Tl-weighted images as a hypointense region and in 30% to 50% of cascs as a hyperintense lesion on T2-weighted images. The latter finding is more common in macroadenomas.**

【79】**MRI is optimally performed within a few minutes of contrast infusion. Microadenomas contrast-enhance less rapidly than the normal pituitary tissue in that time period and appear relatively hypointensc to the normal gland. Further delay in imaging can lead to false-negative studies， because over many minutes， the lesion contrast-enhances to the same degree as normal pituitary tissue.**

【80】**◆ Macroadenomas are typically isointense to gray matter on all pulse sequences and intensely contrast-enhance， often in an inhomogeneous manner.**

【81】**Complicated adcnomas can havc calcification， hemor-rhage， cyst formation， and necrosis and will display corresponding focal signal changes. These features are more common following medical treatment.**

【82】**If MRI is unavailable or contraindicated， adenomas can be detected on contrast-enhanced CT imaging using thin-section axial and coronal images.**

【83】**◆Incidental macroadenomas of moderate size can casily be missed on routine axial CT images of the brain (i.e.， CT studies not specifically performed to assess the pitu-itary gland). Enlargement of the sella turcica on the lat-eral scout topogram can be the only indication that a macroadenoma is present in a routine brain CT study.**

【13】**_Melanocvtic Nevus on the Genitalia_**

【14】**_ofYoung Women_**

【15】**ELANOCYTIC nevi andmalignant melano-**

【16】rrassituated1on the genitalia of womenhave numeroushistologic features in common， such as nests of melanocytes tthat vary in size and shape (many of which are irregular) and tend to confluence， melanocytes that have abundant pale-staining cytoplasm， and multinucleated melano-cytes within the epidermis. Both lesions may be broad， have horizontal extension of nests of melanocytes within the epidermis beyond the dermal component of the lesion， involve epithelial structures of adnexa， and have inflammatory-cell infiltrates with numerous melanophages in the dermis. The most important features that enable differentiation of melanocytic nevi from malignant melanomas on the female genitalia are the propensity of nevi to be mostly symmetric and well circumscribed， to have nests of me-anocytes mostly at the dermo-epidermal junction， and to have typical nevus cells in the dermis. None of these features is seen in malignant melanomas on the female genitalia.

【17】Melanocytic nevi on the vulva of youngwomen are usually deeply pig-mented， may be flat or raised， and have no clinical characteristics of malig-nant melanomas except that， rarely， they may be large， i.e. about 1.0 cm in diameter. Histologically， however， such nevi have some architectural and cytologic features in common with malignant melanomas. The melanocytes in the epidermis are not always those usually found in junctional or com-pound nevi， but may be pagetoid， that is， they have abundant pale-staining cytoplasm. In such nevi， unlike lesions of malignant melanomas， the nuclei of the pagetoid cells are not atypical. As in malignant melanomas， the nests of melanocytes within the epidermis vary， sometimes markedly， in size and shape and tend strikingly to confluence. Unlike malignant melanomas， however， virtually all of the nests of melanocytes in melanocytic nevi are at the dermo-epidermal junction. In some instances， a few single melanocytes may be scattered randomly like “birdshot"or “buckshot"at all levels of the epidermis in a pattern similar to that commonly seen in malignant mela-nomas. In most instances， however， most melanocytes within the epidermis of these nevi are arranged in nests that are situated at the dermo-epidermal junction. Unlike malignant melanomas on the vulva， such nevi are usually associated with typical nevus cells in the dermis.

【18】Pigmented lesions on the vulva are not common. Melanocytic nevi are ally encountered in young rather than older women. Most patienSare younger than 30 years， and some are preadolescent. These benign lesions are usually small， and rarely are thought clinically to be malignant melanomas. Malignant melanomas on the vulva are clinically broad， irregular lesions；

【19】histologically， they have the same characteristics as malignant melanomas on other anatomic sites， i.e.， they tend to be more than 6 mm in breadth， are poorly circumscribed， are asymmetric， and have atypical melanocytes arranged as single units and as nests at all levels of the epidermis. The atypical melanoctyes in malignant melanomas often extend far down the epithelial structures of adnexa and， like the situation in the epidermis， those arranged as solitary units may predominate over those in nests in some foci. When neoplastic melanocytes of malignant melanoma descend into the der-mis， they do not become progressively smaller， but are about the same size as the melanocytes in the epidermis and the upper part of the dermis.

【20】Melanosis of the vilva may be indistinguishable from malignant mela-noma clinically， but the two are easily differentiated histologically by the absence in melanosis of atypical melanocytes， nests of melanocytes within the epidermis， and melanocytes above the basal layer.

【21】In all of the many melanocytic nevi on the genitalia of young women that we have studied， the unusual histologic features were found solely in the epidermis. The changes in the dermis were typical of melanocytic nevi. Even if the pathologist were uncertain that the changes in the epidermis were those of a nevus， the potentially serious pathologic process would be confined wholly within the epidermis， i.e.， malignant melanoma in situ， and would therefore pose no biologic threat to the patient. Vulvectomy and lymph node dissection might be proper procedures for malignant mela-noma of the vulva， but they are surely not appropriate for malignant mela-noma that involves the dermis of the vulva， but they are surely not appropri-ate for malignant melanoma in situ， let alone wholly benign junctional or compound nevi that have some unusual features in the epidermis. If the criteria enumerated previously are employed， the pathologist will almost always be able to come to the correct diagnosis. If there is doubt， another opinion should be sought. If there is still uncertainty， the melanocytic lesion should be completely， but conservatively， excised.

Both lesions may be broad， have horizontal extension of nests of melanocytes within the epidermis beyond the dermal component of the lesion， involve epithelial structures of adnexa， and have inflammatory-cell infiltrates with numerous melanophages in the dermis. The most important features that enable differentiation of melanocytic nevi from malignant melanomas on the female genitalia are the propensity of nevi to be mostly symmetric and well circumscribed， to have nests of me-anocytes mostly at the dermo-epidermal junction， and to have typical nevus cells in the dermis. None of these features is seen in malignant melanomas on the female genitalia.

【17】Melanocytic nevi on the vulva of youngwomen are usually deeply pig-mented， may be flat or raised， and have no clinical characteristics of malig-nant melanomas except that， rarely， they may be large， i.e. about 1.0 cm in diameter. Histologically， however， such nevi have some architectural and cytologic features in common with malignant melanomas. The melanocytes in the epidermis are not always those usually found in junctional or com-pound nevi， but may be pagetoid， that is， they have abundant pale-staining cytoplasm. In such nevi， unlike lesions of malignant melanomas， the nuclei of the pagetoid cells are not atypical. As in malignant melanomas， the nests of melanocytes within the epidermis vary， sometimes markedly， in size and shape and tend strikingly to confluence. Unlike malignant melanomas， however， virtually all of the nests of melanocytes in melanocytic nevi are at the dermo-epidermal junction. In some instances， a few single melanocytes may be scattered randomly like “birdshot"or “buckshot"at all levels of the epidermis in a pattern similar to that commonly seen in malignant mela-nomas. In most instances， however， most melanocytes within the epidermis of these nevi are arranged in nests that are situated at the dermo-epidermal junction. Unlike malignant melanomas on the vulva， such nevi are usually associated with typical nevus cells in the dermis.

【18】Pigmented lesions on the vulva are not common. Melanocytic nevi are ally encountered in young rather than older women. Most patienSare younger than 30 years， and some are preadolescent. These benign lesions are usually small， and rarely are thought clinically to be malignant melanomas. Malignant melanomas on the vulva are clinically broad， irregular lesions；

【19】histologically， they have the same characteristics as malignant melanomas on other anatomic sites， i.e.， they tend to be more than 6 mm in breadth， are poorly circumscribed， are asymmetric， and have atypical melanocytes arranged as single units and as nests at all levels of the epidermis. The atypical melanoctyes in malignant melanomas often extend far down the epithelial structures of adnexa and， like the situation in the epidermis， those arranged as solitary units may predominate over those in nests in some foci. When neoplastic melanocytes of malignant melanoma descend into the der-mis， they do not become progressively smaller， but are about the same size as the melanocytes in the epidermis and the upper part of the dermis.

【20】Melanosis of the vilva may be indistinguishable from malignant mela-noma clinically， but the two are easily differentiated histologically by the absence in melanosis of atypical melanocytes， nests of melanocytes within the epidermis， and melanocytes above the basal layer.

【21】In all of the many melanocytic nevi on the genitalia of young women that we have studied， the unusual histologic features were found solely in the epidermis. The changes in the dermis were typical of melanocytic nevi. Even if the pathologist were uncertain that the changes in the epidermis were those of a nevus， the potentially serious pathologic process would be confined wholly within the epidermis， i.e.， malignant melanoma in situ， and would therefore pose no biologic threat to the patient. Vulvectomy and lymph node dissection might be proper procedures for malignant mela-noma of the vulva， but they are surely not appropriate for malignant mela-noma that involves the dermis of the vulva， but they are surely not appropri-ate for malignant melanoma in situ， let alone wholly benign junctional or compound nevi that have some unusual features in the epidermis. If the criteria enumerated previously are employed， the pathologist will almost always be able to come to the correct diagnosis. If there is doubt， another opinion should be sought. If there is still uncertainty， the melanocytic lesion should be completely， but conservatively， excised.

【53】UNCTIONAL melanocytic nevi and malignant mela-nomas in situ that occur on the palms or soles have numerous histologic features in common. Both melanocytic lesions are confined to a hyper-pigmented epidermis and consist of melanocytes of varying shapes， i.e.， dendritic， spindled， or round. In both conditions， there are increased num-bers of melanocytes arranged as solitary units above the dermo-epidermal junction， there are nests of melanocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction that often vary in size and shape and tend to confluence， and some of the nests may be situated above the dermo-epidermal junction. Solitary melano-cytes and nests of melanocytes may involve acrosyringia. Abundant melanin and some melanocytes are often present in the cornified layer of both junc-tional nevi and malignant melanomas in situ on palms and soles.

【54】In junctional nevi， nests of melanocytes predominate and are mostly at the dermo-epidermal junction； there is no cytologic atypia， although some of the melanocytes may have abundant cytoplasm； most importantly， the lesions are small---usually between 2 and 4 mm in diameter. Clinically， the lesions are small， symmetric， well circumscribed， and uniform in brown color. These acral melanocytic nevi are unusual histopathologically and dif-fer from junctional nevi on other anatomic sites in several ways： there is an increased number of single melanocytes at all levels of the epidermis， in-cluding the cornified layer； the nests of melanocytes tend to confluence； nests of melanocytes may be present within upper portions of eccrine ducts； and there are deposits of melanin， as well as clumps of melanocytes， in the cornified layer.

【55】By applying the aforementioned criteria， differentiation between junc-tional nevi and malignant melanoma in situ on volar skin is easily accom-plished. The major pitfall that leads to an erroneous diagnosis of a benign junctional melanocytic nevus on volar skin as a malignant melanoma is misinterpretation of the scatter of melanocytes at all levels of the epidermis.

A malignant melanoma in situ is the earliest recognizable stage of malignant melanoma， a time in which the pathologic process is confined wholly to the epidermis and epithelial structures of adnexa. Just as in malig-nant melanomas in situ on other anatomic sites， the clinical lesions on the palms and soles are asymmetric， poorly circumscribed， and variegated in shades of brown. Because malignant melanomas in situ are confined wholly to the epidermis and epithelial structures of adnexa， they pose no biologic threat to the patient， i.e.， they do not metastasize. If， however， enough melanocytes reach the dermis， metastases may occur. There is one circum|删除0换行|stance， however， in which a malignant melanoma that is apparently in situ by histologic criteria may actually be associated with metastases， namely， when the melanoma has undergone partial regression， a process that occurs in the papillary dermis. In some instances， neoplastic melanocytes of malig-nant melanoma move from the epidermis into the papillary dermis， where they are destroyed by lymphocytes. Residual changes of such a process are melanophages and telangiectases in a papillary dermis that is thickened by altered collagen； these are signs ofregression. Therefore， a patient may have signs of regression in a lesion in which there is also evidence only of malig-nant melanoma in situ. Such a patient may be at risk for metastases， be-cause regression is an indubitable marker of neoplastic melanocytes having entered the dermis from where they may be carried by vascular channels to distant sites. The actual factors that enable neoplastic cells to metastasize are not yet known.

【57】One important clue to the diagnosis of evolving malignant melanoma in situ on palms and soles is the recognition of increased numbers of den-dritic melanocytes. At one very early stage of its evolution， when there are increased numbers of melanocytes arranged as solitary units and before there is any nesting of the melanocytes， malignant melanoma on the palms and soles is characterized by melanocytes that are strikingly dendritic. Once nests of melanocytes form， the melanocytes lose their remarkable dendrites. The presence of dendritic melanocytes is not specific for malignant mela-nomas on palms and soles， because they may be detected in malignant melanomas in situ on any site. Neither are dendritic melanocytes specific for malignant melanomas， because they may be seen in simple lentigines， mel-anosis of the genitalia， and in melanocytic nevi of all kinds， especially in the dermis of blue nevi.

【58】The term “in situ” is used here to describe the stages of evolution of malignant melanoma during which all of the melanocytes are confined to the site of origin of cutaneous malignant melanomas， namely， the epidermis and epithelial structures of adnexa.

【87】mas that persist (recur) after incomplete surgical excision have many histo-logic similarities. Both may be asymmetric， have increased numbers of me-lanocytes arranged as solitary units and in nests within the epidermis and far down the epithelial structures of adnexa， some variation in size and shape of the nests of melanocytes， some tendency to confluence of some of the nests， some scatter of melanocytes above the dermo-epidermal junction， some atypia of the melanocytic nuclei， some variability in shape (oval， small round， and large round) of the melanocytes， epidermal hyperpigmentation， scars in the upper portion of dermis， nests of melanocytes not only within the epidermis but sometimes in the scarred dermis， and clefts sometimes between the scar in the dermis and the epidermis. Histologic differentiation and precise diagnosis of these two processes of very different biologic poten-tials is accomplished primarily by attention to their different architectural patterns. A persistent melanocytic nevus is sharply circumscribed at its lat-eral borders， the melanocytes are mostly in nests that are situated mostly at the dermo-epidermal junction， and there may be residual nevus cells be-neath the scar in the upper or middle parts of the dermis. Persistent malig-nant melanoma， in contrast， is poorly circumscribed， has nests of melano-cytes above the dermo-epidermal junction， and practically never has cells of a nevus beneath the scar. Recognition of the architectural patterns is crucial if the pathologist is to arrive at the correct diagnosis.

【89】Ihe phenomenon of a melanocytic nevus persisting after partial surgi-cal excision has been termedCEpseudomelanoma” lo alert pathologists to the pitfall of overdiagnosing these benign lesions as malignant melanoma. Per-sistent melanocytic nevi usually appear on the upper parts of the bodies of young adults within a few weeks after partial removal by shave excision and light electrodesiccation of an intradermal， or sometimes a compound， nevus. The persistent melanocytic nevus appears as a small， variegated， brownish macule-patch or papule-plaque with irregular borders， features similar to those of malignant melanoma. A scar from previous surgery is sometimes recognizable.

**The persistence of a pigmented nevus after surgery is seen quickly， the regrowth being apparent within but a few weeks. Little change is then|删除0换行|noticeable over the ensuing months， unlike the gradual evolution that occurs in a persistent malignant melanoma. The original melanocytic nevus is gen-erally intradermal and it may be either congenital or acquired， but the nevus that persists is usually wholly junctional. In some lesions， however， nests of nevus cells may be present in a scarred dermis. Remnants of the original intradermal nevus are often found in the dermis beneath the super-ficial scar and are helpful clues to the proper histologic diagnosis. The diag-nosis of a persistent nevus may still be made with confidence， however， even in the absence of residual nevus cells within the dermis， by finding charac-teristic changes within the epidermis and a scar in the dermis.**

【91】**Malignant melanoma may also persist after incomplete surgical exci-sion and must be differentiated histologically from a persistent nevus. In the case ofPpersistent malignant melanoma， however， the melanocytes tend to be much more atypical than those in persistent nevi， and they tend to be scattered throughout all layers of the epidermis， including the stratum cor-neum. In addition， mitotic figures are sometimes present and nucleoli are lare and eosinophilic. Solar elastosis may also be prominent in persistent melanoma， whereas solar clastosis is unusual in the dermis of persistent nevi because the patients are usually under 30 years of age.**

【0】ggravates the pain. Depending on the severity of the peritonitis and the prior cardiovascular status of the patient， hypotension， tachycardia， pallor， and sweating may also be present. Younger， healthier patients are relatively resistant to hypotension but easily experience tachycardia. In contrast， older patients with a decreased cardiovascular reserve more readily become hypotensive. The presence of cardiac disease may impair the development of tachycardia.

【1】**Appendicitis**

【2】Patients with acute appendicitis almost always have tenderness over the inflamed appendix， often with involuntary guarding， as well as rebound tenderness over McBurney point. Classically， a disproportionate rise in the pulse rate occurs with respect to the severity of fever. Too much emphasis on pain and tenderness and too little attention to the duration of symptoms and objective signs of inflammation may lead to negative exploration results in patients with suspected appendicitis.

【3】**Cholecystitis**

【4】Guarding in the RUQ and tenderness on palpation and percussion suggest cholecystitis. When gallbladder disease is suspected in patients with RUQ pain， the examiner should begin palpation very gently in other parts of the abdomen and end gently over the gallbladder. The goal of this careful palpation is detection of an enlarged (hydrops) gallbladder. An enlarged gallbladder may not be detected by deep palpation or percussion because such aggressive examination may result in involuntary guarding， which prevents detection of the enlarged gallbladder.

【5】**Peptic Ulcer**

【6】Patients with symptoms of peptic ulcer disease may show no abnormal physical findings except pain on gentle percussion over the midepigastrium or duodenal sweep. When peritonitis develops in patients with peptic ulcer disease， it is secondary to perforation of the involved viscus. If the viscus penetrates anteriorly， extreme rigidity of the abdominal wall results. If the viscus penetrates posteriorly， back pain is a major symptom and the symptoms of peritonitis are minimal. In the early stages of a penetrating or perforated peptic ulcer， bowel sounds may be increased or normal， but as the condition progresses， bowel sounds become diminished or absent.

【7】**Intestinal Obstruction**

【8】Auscultation of the abdomen may help the physician to diagnose obstruction. Classically， rushes of high-pitched， tinkling peristalsis are heard. These rushes are often associated with recurring crampy， colicky pain. The physician must listen for a succussion splash in all patients who complain of vomiting. This examination requires the examiner to place the stethoscope over the stomach and to shake the abdomen gently. A succussion splash may be heard over a stomach that is dilated or distended with air and fluid. This finding is normal in infants and adults immediately after eating. By 30 minutes after eating， the sound should not be heard unless an obstruction exists with an air-fluid level. Impaired gastric emptying occurs most often in patients with pyloric obstruction (congenital or acquired)； it also occurs in patients with gastric tumors or gastric atony. Atonic gastric dilatation is most frequently seen in postoperative patients and in patients who have severe hyperkalemia or diabetic ketoacidosis.

【9】The classic triad of physical findings in patients with acute intestinal obstruction is as follows：

【10】1 Sudden onset of colicky abdominal pain

【11】2 Vomiting

【12】3 Obstipation

Bowel sounds are generally hyperactive and high pitched and occur in rushes； if perforation or peritonitis occurs， the bowel sounds become reduced. When the obstruction is in the large intestine，|删除0换行|abdominal distention and general or local intestinal distention may occur. With voloulus， gross distention of the entire abdomen may occur early in the disease.

【14】**Salpingitis**

【15】The physical findings in salpingitis include unilateral or bilateral tenderness on palpation in the lower abdomen and increased bowel sounds. Involuntary guarding and rigidity are rare findings. Pelvic examination often elicits pain， particularly with lateral movement of the cervix and adnexal palpation. The patient frequently has a purulent cervical discharge.

【16】**rritable Bowel**

【17】Although most patients with an irritable bowel have no significant physical findings (the diagnosis is made by careful history)， a tender ascending or descending colon may be palpable. Diagnosis of IBS is best made using elements of history as suggested by the Rome II criteria .

【18】**Acute Diverticulitis**

【19】**The classic triad for acute diverticulitis is as follows：**

【20】**1 Abdominal tenderness**

【21】2 A palpable mass in the LLQ

【22】**3 Fever**

【23】The mass or tenderness may be occasionally detected only by rectal examination. Diarrhea and rectal bleeding are uncommon， and bowel sounds are usually decreased.

【24】**Ureterolithiasis**

【25】Tenderness on percussion in the costovertebral angle and ileus may be the only physical finding in patients with ureterolithiasis. This diagnosis is usually confirmed by the presence of hematuria.

【26】**Diagnostic studies**

【27】Although plain or flat abdominal radiographs (often with chest radiographs) are frequently ordered in patients with acute abdominal pain， they are diagnostic in less than 50% of cases. They are useful in identifying free air in the case of a perforated viscous or dilated loops of bowel in an intestinal obstruction. Abdominal computed tomography(CT) scans and abdominal ultrasonography are often helpful， _especially when gallbladder， pancreatic， or pelvic disease is suspected. CT_ scans provide information concerning the bowel wall， mesentery， and intraperitoneal and retroperitoneal structures and are useful in surgical decision making. Noncontrast CT scanning is useful in diagnosing ureterolithiasis. In pregnant women with abdominal pain， if the necessary information can be obtained without using ionizing radiation (i.e.， with ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging \[MRI\])， those should be used as first line examinations. If ionizing radiation is necessary (i.e.， CT scanning)， the radiation dose should be kept as low as possible without compromising diagnostic accuracy.

If an acute surgical abdomen is suspected but the diagnosis is|删除0换行|unknown or dubious， the physician should obtain an electrocardiogram， chest and abdominal radiographs， complete blood count (CBC) with differential， measurements of electrolytes， blood urea nitrogen， serum amylase (if pancreatitis is suspected)， and cardiac enzymes， and urine and stool tests.

【29】Specific laboratory tests may be ordered when particular diagnoses are suspected， as follows：

【30】Appendicitis -CBC with differential and C-reactive protein measurement (a normal C-reactive protein level and leukocyte count mitigates against appendicitis)

【31】Cholecystitis-CBC with differential and complete metabolic profile Ureterolithiasis-microscopic urinalysis

【32】Pancreatitis-serum amylase and lipase measurements

Early laparoscopy has been shown to accelerate diagnosis and treatment for patients with nonspecific abdominal pain compared|删除0换行|with active observation， although it has yet to be adopted as a uniform strategy. Laparoscopy has been recommended for all women of reproductive age in whom appendicitis is suspected. The advantages of laparoscopy in women with NSAP and suspected appendicitis include a higher rate of specific diagnoses being made and a lower rate of removal of normal appendices compared with open appendectomy only.

【34】In one series， 7.4% of patients presenting with abdominal pain with colonic wall thickening on CT had colorectal carcinoma on colonoscopy and 74% had clinically significant pathology， suggesting the value of colonoscopy for following up colonic wall thickening found on CT. Endoscopic ultrasonography is useful in evaluating esophageal， gastric， and particularly pancreatic lesions.

【35】Transabdominal ultrasound may be used as an initial imaging modality for suspected appendicitis， although CT scanning is more sensitive and should be used immediately for patients with atypical clinical presentation and for patients for whom ultrasound findings were negative， and there still remains a high clinical suspicion. Low-dose unenhanced CT is equal to standard-dose CT with intravenous contrast agents in the detection of five signs of acute appendicitis(thickened appendiceal wall more than 2 mm，cross-sectional diameter greater than 6 mm， periappendicitis，abscess， and appendicolith). Despite a more than doubling of the use of CT in the emergency department in recent years， there has been no increase in detection rates for appendicitis， diverticulitis， and gallbladder disease. There was also no reduction in hospital admissions for these conditions. There is some evidence that use of CT reduces negative appendectomy rates. These data reinforce the principle of the importance of history and physical examination in the diagnosis of abdominal pain.
**Less common diagnostic considerations**

【36】Abdominal pain may result from pneumonia， particularly in a lower lobe. Abdominal pain and vomiting may be the presenting symptoms in diabetes. RUQ pain can be caused by congestive heart failure resulting from stretching of Glisson capsule. RUQ pain， jaundice， and anorexia may be the presenting symptoms of hepatitis.

【37】RLQ pain from cecal epiploic appendagitis can mimic appendicitis. In women of childbearing age， with RUQ pain， Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome should be considered.

【38】Amebiasis can mimic appendicitis， diverticulitis， or both. Abdominal or flank pain or both， when associated with nausea and vomiting， may be the presenting symptoms of hydronephrosis.

【39】Hereditary angioedema should be suspected in young adults with recurrent abdominal pain when more common causes have been excluded. Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor-related angioedema may also manifest as abdominal pain due to edema of the small bowel. This is more prevalent in blacks treated with ACE inhibitors and is often accompanied by ascites.

【40】Cocaine use can cause gastric ulcers， visceral infarction， intestinal ischemia， and ischemic colitis.

【41】Eosinophilic enteritis， a rare cause of abdominal pain， can cause recurrent abdominal pain associated with vomiting， loose stools， and weight loss.

【42】An acute abdomen in a young black patient classically suggests the possibility of sickle cell crisis. Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain may be caused by familial Mediterranean fever， which occurs in people of Jewish， Arabic， Turkish， and Armenian ancestry. Severe abdominal wall tenderness can result from a spider bite. Rarely， diffuse abdominal pain can be secondary to marked gaseous distention.

When abdominal pain is triggered by spinal movement， spinal pathology may be the origin of abdominal pain. Severe pain in the back|删除0换行|or flank or vague， poorly localized abdominal pain may be the first presenting symptom in patients with carcinoma of the pancreas. If abdominal pain is associated with thrombophlebitis (in the absence of trauma)， migratory thrombophlebitis， or the development of diabetes， pancreatic carcinoma should be suspected. Carcinoma of the head of the pancreas usually manifests as jaundice or abdominal pain early in the course of illness.

【44】Abdominal pain， sometimes associated with vomiting， that occurs in the middle of the menstrual cycle is called mittelschmerz. It represents pain associated with the physiologic rupture of an ovarian follicle.

【45】If a female of childbearing age suddenly experiences severe， generalized abdominal pain， often associated with syncope or persistent dizziness， ectopic preonancy must be considered. This is more common in younger women， in women of low parity， and in those with a history of pelvic sepsis or infertility. Physical findings include acute abdominal pain with guarding and rigidity， especially in the lower abdomen. Extreme tenderness to cervical manipulation has been reported in 85% of patients with an ectopic pregnancy. Transvaginal sonography is the single best diagnostic modality for evaluating women with suspected ectopic pregnancy. The presence of an adnexal mass in the absence of an intrauterine pregnancy on transvaginal sonography and the physical examination findings of cervical motion tenderness， an adnexal mass， and adnexal tenderness all increase the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy. A lack of adnexal abnormalities on transvaginal sonography decreases the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy. The presence of abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding during early pregnancy should prompt a transvaginal sonogram and quantitative serum human chorionic gonadotropin(hCG) testing.

【49】Vascular causes of abdominal pain include mesenteric thrombosis and acute mesenteric occlusion by embolism or torsion. The latter may have no associated signs or symptoms-only severe abdominal pain， with bloody stools occurring later. Aortic aneurysm may cause constant low back pain， which may worsen with recumbency； dissection is characterized by severe， excruciating pain.

【10】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【11】**_◆_ Arterial stenosis： A stenosis of the femoral artery could cause increased diastolic flow， loss of high resis-tance， arterial waveform， and color Doppler bruit， but it should not alter the venous waveforms.**

【12】**_◆_ Arterial dissection： A dissection or flap may have fea-tures similar to atherosclerotic narrowing， but no venous waveform changes should occur.**

【13】**Venous stenosis： A narrowed and stenotic vein may cause high-velocity venous flow， but no arterial changes.**

【14】**◆Arteriovenous fistula (AVF)： This is the best diagno-sis because it explains both the arterial and venous waveform changes.**

【15】**◆DIAGNOSIS： Femoral arteriovenous fistula.**

【16】**#KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【17】**◆An AVF resulting from arterial puncture and catheteri-zation is a less common complication than a pseudo-aneurvsm，**

【18】**◆An AVF is an abnormal communication between the arterial and venous systems that creates a shunt from the high-rcsistance artcrial system into the low-resistance venous system.**

【19】**◆An AVF is caused by simultaneous puncture of the adjacent artery and vein and by simultaneous arterial and venous catheterization，**

【20】**◆An AVF is manifest clinically by a continous bruit or thrill in the region of trauma.**

**◆An AVF may be asymptomatic or can produce local-ized symptoms， including pain， claudication distal to|删除0换行|the AVF secondary to decreased arterial flow， and venous stasis duc to increased venous pressure. Systemic symptoms such as high-output congestive heart failure and angina may also result.**

【22】**An asymptomatic AVF does not require treatment and may resolve spontaneously.**

【23】**◆Surgical treatment or ultrasound-guided compres-sion/repair may be necessary.**

【24】**◆An AVF may coexist with a postcatheterization pseudoaneurysm.**

【25】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【26】**◆The classic arterial pattern is high diastolic flow (a low resistance waveform) with spectral broadening just proximal to the fistula.**

【27】**_◆_ The classic venous pattern is increased flow velocity with pulsatile disturbed waveforms near the fistula.**

【28】**◆Color Doppler signal in the soft tissues surrounding the AVF is caused by the transmitted thrill from dis-turbed flow.**

【29】**A visible tract of flow connccting the artery and vein may be seen， cspccially with color Doppler.**

【30】**There is often decreased arterial flow distal to the fistula.**

【31】**Some AVFs may not demonstrate all of these features.**

【16】**#KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【17】**◆An AVF resulting from arterial puncture and catheteri-zation is a less common complication than a pseudo-aneurvsm，**

【18】**◆An AVF is an abnormal communication between the arterial and venous systems that creates a shunt from the high-rcsistance artcrial system into the low-resistance venous system.**

【19】**◆An AVF is caused by simultaneous puncture of the adjacent artery and vein and by simultaneous arterial and venous catheterization，**

【20】**◆An AVF is manifest clinically by a continous bruit or thrill in the region of trauma.**

**◆An AVF may be asymptomatic or can produce local-ized symptoms， including pain， claudication distal to|删除0换行|the AVF secondary to decreased arterial flow， and venous stasis duc to increased venous pressure. Systemic symptoms such as high-output congestive heart failure and angina may also result.**

【22】**An asymptomatic AVF does not require treatment and may resolve spontaneously.**

【23】**◆Surgical treatment or ultrasound-guided compres-sion/repair may be necessary.**

【27】**_◆_ The classic venous pattern is increased flow velocity with pulsatile disturbed waveforms near the fistula.**

【28】**◆Color Doppler signal in the soft tissues surrounding the AVF is caused by the transmitted thrill from dis-turbed flow.**

【29】**A visible tract of flow connccting the artery and vein may be seen， cspccially with color Doppler.**

【30】**There is often decreased arterial flow distal to the fistula.**

【31】**Some AVFs may not demonstrate all of these features.**

【58】**_A_ Although the natural history of pseudoaneurysms is variable， spontaneous thrombosis is common. Unfortunately， there is no way of discerning which pseudoaneurysms will thrombose based on their ultra-sound appearancc.**

【59】**Traditional therapy for pseudoaneurysms has been surgical intervention. However， many pseudo-aneurysms thrombose spontancously. Furthermore， nonsurgical ultrasound-guided compression repair(UGCR) has been found to be a very successful inter-ventional technique.**

【61】**(Contraindications to UCGR include overlying skin ischemia or skin infection， peripheral vascular compro-mise， location of the pseudoaneurysm above the inguinal ligament， and inability to compress the pseudoancurysm without simultaneous occlusion of the uinderlying artery.**

【62】**Complications of UCGR are uncommon； they include arterial occlusion， peripheral embolization， pseudo-aneurysm rupture， and thrombosis of the adjacent common femoral vein.**

【65】**◆To-and-fro pulsed Doppler waveforms are localized to the region of the pseudoaneurysm neck.**

【66】**Pseudoaneurysms may be multiple and create a“string-of-beads”appearancc.**

【19】**ChapterAn Approach to Palpitations5 and Arrhythmias**

【20】**Clinical Case**

【21】**_A 19-year-old female dance student walks into clinic complaining of intermittent_ _palpitations. She has had four episodes in the last month， each lasting 5 min. Popping her_ _ears (as one does in a landing aeroplane) apparently stops the palpitations. During_ _episodes， she does not faint， feel giddy or have chest pain or diaphoresis. She feels perfectly_ _normal between episodes， and has no other past medical history. Physical examination is_ _normal. How would you approach her palpitations? She is currently asymptomatic._**

【22】**Palpitations are an unpleasant awareness of the forceful， rapid and/or irregular beating of the heart. It may be due to both cardiac and non-cardiac disease. Most cases are benign， but there are a number of potentially life-threatening arrhythmias. A rational decision-making strategy is needed to quickly identify patients with life-threatening arrhythmias， then risk stratify and determine which patients require advanced investi-gations .**

【23】**A. Unstable Tachyarrhythmias**

【24】**Some arrhythmias can cause haemodynamic instability. First assess the patient for hypotension or serious signs or symptoms (e.g.， drowsiness， shortness of breath， chest pain， syncope). An unstable tachyarrhythmia may require urgent intervention， usually cardioversion.**

【25】**The next step is a 12-lead ECG.**

【26】**Abnormal ECG**

【27】**B. The Tachycardias**

【28】**Two key differentiators are (1) is rhythm regular or irregular， and (2) is the QRS complex narrow or wide (normal=80-120 ms=2-3 small squares). The QRS width is the time taken for the complex to reach all ventricular myocardium. An impulse originating from or above the atrioventricular (AV) node， and going down the rapid conducting system， has a short conduction time and narrow QRS width； conversely， QRS is wide in a complex that originates in the ventricles and is not conducted through the rapid conducting system， or if there is a defect in the conducting system. (Note： patients with pacemakers are not discussed in this chapter).**

【29】**A. flutter， atrial flutter； AF， atrial fibrillation； MAT， multifocal atrial tachycardia； SVT， supraventricular tachycardia； VF， ventricular fibrillation；VT， ventricular tachycardia； WPW，Wolff-Parkinson-White.**

【30】通用删除16(英):<u>**Figure 5.1. Approach to palpitations.**</u>

【31】**(a) Regular narrow-complex tachycardia： Look at the timing and morphology of the P waves.**

【32】**Sinus tachycardia： Sinus P waves present before each QRS， with 1 QRS complex for every P wave. This is usually a response to non-cardiac disease， for example， pain， infection， hypovolaemia， anaemia， hyperthyroidism，pulmonary embolism or anxiety . Work up for these aetiologies.**

【33】**·SSupraventricular tachycardia 通用删除1(英):<u>(SVT； Figure 5.2a)</u>： P waves are absent or abnormal in morphology and/or timing. For instance， retrograde impulse con-duction from the AV node to the atria results in inverted P waves (best seen in inferior leads) occurring soon after the QRS complex. There are different SVTs， including atrial tachycardia (AT)， AV nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT)and orthodromic AV re-entrant tachycardia (AVRT)； it is sometimes possible to determine the exact type of SVT from the 12-lead ECG， but this is not a diag-nostic priority and usually does not change initial management.**

【34】**Is all lost when P waves cannot be found?→ see GO FURTHER' question at the end of this** **chapter.**

【35】**Atrial flutter ： Rapid P waves (atrial rate： 250-300 beats/min) forming a saw-tooth baseline， most commonly with conduction of every second P wave (2：1 AV conduction)， leading to a ventricular rate of 150 beats/min. Less commonly， there may be 3：1 or 4：1 AV conduction. The approach is as for atrial fibrillation (AF) .**

【36】**(b) Irregular narrow-complex tachycardia**

【37】**AF ： Irregularly irregular R-R intervals with absent P waves. Search for a provoking cause， including non-cardiac (sepsis， electrolyte imbalance， hyperthyroidism) and cardiac (e.g.， ischaemic heart disease and heart failure) aetiologies， as dictated by the clinical presentation.**

【38】**1Multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT)： An irregular tachycardia with ≥3 dif-ferent P wave morphologies， and narrow QRS complexes following the P waves. This tends to occur in patients with lung disease (e.g.， COPD and pneumonia) or heart disease with pulmonary hypertension.**

【39】**(c) Regular wide-complex tachycardia**

【40】**·Ventricular tachycardia 通用删除1(英):<u>(VT； Figure 5.2d)</u>： VT is the most common cause of regular wide-complex tachycardia， especially in patients with underlying ischaemic heart disease. Check vital signs-patients with VT may be unstable.**

【41】**SSVT with aberrant conduction： SVT mimics VT in the presence of conduction delay， which prolongs the QRS complex. Consider SVT with aberrancy in young patients with structurally normal hearts，2 especially if the QRS complex has a bundle branch block morphology. Conversely， features favouring VT over SVT include known ischaemic heart disease， very wide QRS complex (> 160 ms)， northwest ECG axis， fusion or capture beats， AV dissociation (P waves seen with no relationship to QRS) or concordance (all precordial leads positive， or all neg-ative). If in doubt， diagnose VT rather than SVT with aberrancy； managing VT as for SVT can cause haemodynamic instability.**

【42】**SVT with pre-excitation： Consider antidromic AVRT in patients with Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome； this is important as AV nodal blocking drugs should be avoided in WPW. Unfortunately， if there is no prior diagnosis of WPW， it is difficult to distinguish from VT.**

【43】**(d) Irregular wide-complex tachycardia**

【44】**Ventricular fibrillation： Patient would have collapsed.**

【45】**AF with aberrant conduction ： Irregularly irregular rhythm.**

【46】**Further workup： This would depend on the specific tachycardia. The majority of these aetiologies， except for sinus tachycardia and SVT， would require evaluation for cardiac function， and possible underlying ischaemic or valvular heart disease. This would include an echocardiogram + stress testing， and at times electrophysiologic studies.**

【47】**2Young patients with structurally normal hearts may also develop specific， uncommon types of** **VT. These include right ventricular outflow tract tachycardia， catecholaminergic polymorphic** **VT and so forth.**

【48】通用删除16(英):<u>**Figure 5.2. The ECG in tachycardia.**</u>

【49】**(a) Supraventricular tachycardia： Regular， with narrow QRS complexes. P waves are not well seen in this ECG.**

【50】**(b) Atrial flutter： Note narrow QRS complexes， saw-toothed P waves with 3：1 conduction.**

【51】**(c) Atrial fibrillation： Irregularly irregular， narrow QRS tachycardia.**

【52】**(d) Ventricular tachycardia： QRS complexes are very broad.**

【53】**(e) Atrial fibrillation with aberrant conduction： The rhythm is irregularly irregular. QRS complexes are broad with suggestion of a right bundle branch block pattern.**

【54】**C. Other ECG Abnormalities**

【55】**Premature beats： May present with palpitations. These tend to occur suddenly and last for no more than an instant.**

【56】**· Premature ventricular contraction (PVC)： A wide QRS complex， not preceded by P wave， followed by a T wave in the opposite direction， and then a compensatory pause. Isolated PVCs are common and do not require further workup. If frequent， consider ambulatory monitoring to determine the frequency and morphology of PVCs， and evaluation for an underlying aetiology-cardiac (hypertensive heart disease， myocardial infarction， heart failure) and non-cardiac disease (caffeine， COPD， hyperthyroidism， etc.).**

【57】**· Premature atrial contraction (PAC)： A premature P wave triggering a normal or aberrant QRS complex. Isolated PACs are common and do not require further workup. If frequent， consider workup to rule out underlying structural heart disease.**

【58】**Arrhythmia not captured： Many arrhythmias are intermittent and may not be cap-tured on a single ECG. However， abnormalities in the rest ECG may suggest a diagnosis.**

【59】**Structural cardiac abnormalities： Q waves (old infarction)， left ventricular hyper-trophy (structural heart disease and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy) suggest that an arrhythmia may be the cause of palpitations. Attempts to capture the arrhythmia should be pursued .**

【60】**__ Wolff-Parkinson-White(WPW)syndrome： Delta waves with a short PR interval may be seen . This is associated with a number of supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias， and sudden cardiac death.**

【61】**Brugada pattern： Coved ST segment elevation>2 mm， followed by a negative T wave， in more than 1 anterior lead (V1-V3). If symptomatic， this is associated with VT， AF and sudden cardiac death.**

Initial ECG (a) shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia for which IV adenosine is administered. Repeat ECG (b) uncovers underlying delta-waves，indicating an underlying WPW syndrome.**</u>

【63】**Normal ECG or Sinus Tachycardia D. Consider Non-cardiac Causes**

【64】**All patients with a normal initial ECG， and those with sinus tachycardia， should be evaluated for non-cardiac causes of palpitations. This includes**

【65】**Workup**

【66】**· Endocrine disorders：**

【67】**\- Hyperthyroidism： Clinical features include heat intolerance， weight loss， diarrhoea， tremor删除2:<u>(Chapter 36)</u>.**

【68】**\- Thyroid function tests**

【69】**\-Hypoglycaemia： Usually a diabetic on insulin or oral hypoglycaemic agents who has missed meals _C_ or had recent dose adjustments.**

【70】**\-Blood glucose**

【71】**\- Phaeochromocytoma： Episodes of palpitations， hypertension， headache and diaphoresis.**

【72】**\- Urine metanephrine screening**

【73】**·Drugs： Beta-agonists or sudden cessation of beta-blockers， vasodilators， anticholinergics， recreational drugs (e.g.， cocaine) and caffeine.**

【74】**·Hypovolaemia**

【75】**· Anaemia**

【76】**\- Full blood count**

【77】**· Psychiatric： Panic attacks， anxiety disorders and somatisation. This is a diagnosis of exclusion.**

【78】**E. Consider Extended ECG Monitoring**

【79】**Many arrhythmias are intermittent， and may not be captured on a single 10-second ECG. The ECG is more likely diagnostic if captured when the patient has ongoing pal-pitations (e.g.， in an emergency department setting). If an initial ECG is normal， the next decision is whether to pursue extended ECG monitoring. This would depend on the clinical suspicion of an arrhythmia (especially a malignant one).**

【80】**Suggest extended monitoring in patients with：**

【81】**__ Severe symptoms (syncope， chest pain， diaphoresis) during episodes of arrhythmia.**

【82】**Known structural heart disease including ischaemic heart disease， valvular heart disease， cardiomyopathies.**

【83】**__ Family history of sudden cardiac death.**

【84】**Abnormal physical examination， including murmurs， heart failure， displaced apex beat.**

【85】**_Abnormal rest ECG._**

【86】**__ Recurrent bothersome symptoms.**

【87】**Extended ECG monitoring can be accomplished via Holter devices (24 or 48 hr)， trans-telephonic monitoring (2 weeks) or implantable loop recorders (even longer duration， but invasive).**

【4】**History**

【5】The presentation with cardiac pain is often one ofconcem. Cardiac pain is often the result of coronary artery oc-clusion caused by atherosclerosis or vasospasm. Given|删除0换行|that atherosclerosis is a slowly accumulating process， it is logical to assume cardiac disease in older patients who have chest pain. T’he classic presentation of an older man with retrosternal pain relieved by 5 to 15 minutes of rest is so characteristic of coronary heart disease (CHD) that the patient has a 94% probability of having at least 75%occlusion of one coronary artery on angiography. The opposite is also true； a young woman with chest pain that is not typical cardiac pain has a less than 1% chance of coronary artery occlusion.

【14】Musculoskeletal and somatic chest pain has a broader range of attributes； however， it often presents as follows：

【19】When a history of trauma is given (fall or blow to the chest)， a suspicion of rib fracture is high. Rib fractures gen-erally feel worse with deep inspiration， coughing，sneez-ing， and while lying supine. Rib fractures may be the result ofabuse， and eliciting a clear history is often diffi-cult. Instead， the patient may claim an“accident.”It is im-portant to look for other clues of abuse during the examination， such as bruises and scars or radiographi-cally for past fractures.

Overuse may be obvious， such as starting a new exer-cise or workout routine， or as subtle as doing housework， yardwork， or helping someone move furniture， If the pain is sharp and felt unilaterally at the costosternal junc-|删除0换行|tion， Tietze's syndrome should be considered. Other causes include repeated coughing or vomiting.

【21】By focusing on the standard approach to history of a chief complaint questioning a rather accurate distinction can usually be made between cardiac and noncardiac pain. Further distinction between cardiac and other visceral sources may be more clouded. Substernal pain is also possible with esophageal disorders such as reflux or esophageal spasm. Questions pertaining to swallowing and relationship to meals are often revealing. If swal-lowing is difficult， it is important to ask about the rela-tionship to hot， cold， solid， and liquid foods. If the pain begins after drinking or eating very hot or cold foods and is associated with difficulty swallowing both solids and liq-uids， esophageal spasm must be considered a likely pos-sibility. Pain that is worse with recumbency， especially after meals or with wearing a tight belt， is indicative of re-flux. Reflux may also be associated with the ingestion of certain foods such as chocolate， fats， caffeine， orange juice， onions， and garlic. It is important to note， how-ever， that patients with cardiac pain often have associ-ated epigastric complaints.

【22】The distinction between superficial and deep pain helps first to distinguish between cardiac and noncardiac pain. It also helps in distinguishing among various non-cardiac sources of pain. If the patient complains of a su-perficial sensation of burning or hypersensitivity along a patch of skin， herpes zoster (shingles) should be sus-pected. This is confirmed within a few days with the appearance of a vesicular rash roughly following a der-matome (not necessarily the entire dermatome). This same superficial sensation may be the result of irritation from osteophytic impingement of a thoracic nerve root or may be due to diabetes. Another rare possibility is Mondor's disease. This occurs in women as a superficial thrombophlebitis of the thoracoepigastric vein. The pa-tient feels a tender cordlike swelling beneath the breast.

【23】Chest pain associated with difficulty breathing is com-mon. If there are no indicators of an underlying respira-tory infection， several possibilities to consider are the following：

【24】A sudden onset of chest pain associated with dysp-lassOCia nea and fever suggests a pulmonary embolism， es-pecially in a patient who was immobilized， is taking oral contraceptives， or has antecedent calf pain. lmmcdiate referral is necessary.

【25】11Dyspnea preceding chest pain and associated with lightheadedness， dizziness， or syncope， especially ina younger _1_ male a _1_ thlete， suggests HOCM. Referral for ECG or ultrasound evaluation is necessary.

Sharp pains localized to the posterior chest that are made worse with respiration， there is no history of trauma， and there are no signs ofinfection suggest the possibility of spontaneous pneumothorax， es-|删除0换行|pecially if the patient is young and tall with a his-tory of an exerting activity such as backpacking or exercise. 【27】A psychogenic cause should be suspected in patients with multiple body complaints that appear unrelated， in patients with a past or current psychiatric diagnosis (es-pecially depression)， and in those who appear to have anx-iety reactions to stressful situations. It is important not to“excuse” the complaint without a thorough evaluation. Hyperventilation is often found with anxious patients.

【28】**Examination**

【29】Cardiac involvement is discovered largely through the history. Signs of cardiac involvement are rarely found when the patient is asymptomatic. These signs， when present， would largely be found on an ECG. Changes in the ST segment may reflect underlying ischemia. Depending on severity， either ST elevation or ST de-pression may be indicative of an ischemic cardiac prob-lem. Given that a restingECG can provide information only over a short period of time， a TIolter monitor(portable recording unit) is often prescribed in an at-tempt to match the patient's symptoms to a recorded ECG abnormality. Further monitoring with a stress ECG should be done through referral and consultation with a cardiologist.

【30】Indirect implications are generated through auscul-tatory findings such as murmurs or lung congestion. Hypertension also may be an indirect indicator of systemic atherosclerosis suggesting coronary involvement. Other indicators of atherosclerotic involvement are signs of in-termittent claudication in the lower or upper extremi-ties. This is characterized by pain and weakness/tiredness when exercising the extremity that is promptly relieved by rest.

【31】Musculoskcletal involvement may be exposed， repro-ducing mechanically the patient's complaint with regard to location and quality. Muscles are challenged through a procedure involving contraction， stretch， and contrac-tion in a stretched position. Palpation is used to localize tenderness and in a scarch for nodules or referred pain upon palpation of specific trigger points. The most comn-mon muscles that can cause chest pain are those that are geographically situated in close proximity： the pectoralis major， pectoralis minor， serratus anterior， and intercostals. Following are positions and contraction patterns that may stretch or contract these structures：

【50】**CARDIAC**

【51】**Angina**

【52】Classic Presentation

【53】The patient complains of a squeezing or pressure sensation in the chest. It came on rather suddenly after exertion. The patient said that after resting for several minutes the sensation went away. This was not the first time it had happened. He or she also noticed that there was an aching pain felt down the left inside arm to the fingers.

【54】Cause

【55】Angina is usually due to atherosclerosis； however， a variant of angina is related to vasospasm that may occur in isolation or with atherosclerosis (Prinzmetal’s angina). Patients with Prinzmetal's angina of-ten have an atypical presentation in that they may be women under age 50 with angina that occurs at night (involves the right coronary artery most often). Another entity is called syndrome X in which therc is no apparent coronary atherosclerosis. It is believed that there are microvascular abnormalities in these patients. The threshold for an angina attack may be decreased by factors such as anemia， valvular dis-orders (especially aortic stenosis)， or conduction problems. Cocaine may also provoke an attack. When atherosclerosis is excessive， angina may occur at rest without provocation (unstable angina). These attacks tend to be longer and may be a portent of impending myocardial infarction.

【56】Evaluation

【57】The history of a pressure or squeczing pain lasting for several minutes to 30 minutes with possible ra-diation to the arm or jaw is characteristic of angina. If the pain occurs at rest or without provocation， unstable angina is likely， indicating more occlusion. Given that it is rarely possible to examine a pa-tient during an attack， most findings such as hypertension are indirect indicators of underlying ath-erosclcrosis. Valvular abnormalities such as aortic stenosis in older patients and mitral valve prolapse in younger patients may be found. ECG findings are nonspecific except during the attack， when ei-ther ST depression1 Oor，1 with more severe ischemia， ST elevation is found. Provocation with exercisetesting includes an ECG. Based on these findings scintigraphic or echocardiographic studies may be added. 4 Ambulatory monitoring with a Holter device may be used， especially ifan underlying arrhythmia is suspected. Coronary angiography should be used in selected patients only.

【58】Management

【59】Nitroglycerin is used for symptomatic management of angina. It decreases contraction of the heart and causes vasodilation. It is usually taken sublingually and takes a minute or two to work. With more fulminant involvement of the coronary arteries， angioplasty or surgery may be suggested to the pa-tient. It is important to advise patients with mild symptoms that supervised lifestyle changes includ-ing a healthful diet and exercise may decrease the nced for nitroglycerin and， in some patients，reverse the underlying process. It is a comanagement scenario in which the medical doctor， chiropractor， and patient work together.

【60】**Myocardial Infarction**

【61】Classic Presentation

【62】Not all patients with myocardial infarction (MI) are unconscious or in severe pain， although the ma-jority of patients have pain severe enough to warrant a trip to the emergency department or a 911 call. It is possible to have a patient complain about pain that is often preceded by a history of angina. The substernal pain is more severe and often builds up over a few minutes. Nitroglycerin does not help.

【65】Cause

【66】Usually MI is due to coronary thrombus or vasospasin. Blockage of a specific coronary artery causes damage to the area supplied. For example， blockage of the anterior descending branch of the left coronary artery causes infarction of the anterior left ventricle and interventricular septum. The ex-tent of damage is subendocardial with some transmural extension evident in most cases. Extension of infarcted tissue increases after the occlusion and may be diminished by prompt thrombolytic therapy.

【67】Fvaluation

【68】Evaluation is performed in the hospital with a check for associated arrhythmias. There are large vari-ations at presentation with regard to heart rate， advential respiratory sounds， and general status of the patient. Laboratory testing performed within the first few hours will reveal an elevation of creatine kinase (CK) that peaks in about 12 to 24 hours. The isoenzyme CK-MB (inyocardial band) is specific for the heart. The level of CK elevation correlates to the degree of damage. This has led to the use of these tests in place of the older method of measuring lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) isoenzyme levels in patients who present after 48 hours or are assessed after this time. ECG findings involve a sequence of hyperacute T waves， progressing to ST elevation， to Q wave de-velopment， to T wave inversion. 【70】It is important for chiropractors to maintain cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) certification (or knowledge). Although rare， it may be necessary to perform CPR in or out of the office. 【32】**INTRODUCTION**

Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is a group of heteroge-neous clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders characterized clinically and morphologically by ineffective hematopoiesis and dyspoiesis leading to cytopenia(s) (which often result IOC in transfusion-dependent anemia and/or increased infection or hemorrhage) and risk of progression to acute leukemia通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-14\]</u>. The incidence of MDS varies from 2.1 to 12.6 cases per 100，000 population per year， but approaches 50 cases per|删除0换行|100，000 per year in persons over age 70 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15-17\]</u>. Ineffective hematopoiesis in MDS has been attributed in part to a com-plex interaction between the progenitor cells and the micro-environment that results in the premature apoptotic death of blood cell precursors， which is counterbalanced by increased proliferation of hematopoietic elements 通用删除6(英):<u>\[18-20\]</u>.

【39】**MINIMAL DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA**

The diagnosis of MDS is suspected based on the presence of unexplained cytopenia(s). Recently， the minimal diagnostic criteria for MDS have been proposed by introducing MDS prerequisite-type criteria (both must be fulfilled)， MDS-related criteria (one of these must be fulfilled)， and several co-criteria 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，3，22-24\]</u>. Prerequisite-type criteria include(1) marked and constant cytopenia (>6 months unless cyto-genetic studies reveal MDS) in at least one hematopoietic lineage (hemoglobin <10 g/dL， neutrophilic granulocytes<1.8× 10/L， platelets <100 ×10/L) and (2) exclusion of all other clonal or nonclonal hematopoietic disease or non-hematopoietic disease as the primary reason for cytopenia and/or dysplasia (clinical history， BM morphology， flow cytometry (FC)， cytogenetic/molecular markers， other rel-evant tests). MDS-related criteria include (1) morphologic dysplasia in ≥10% of all cells in one or more of the cell lineages in the aspirate smear (erythroid， myeloid， and/or megakaryocytes)； (2) ring sideroblast count ≥15% as a criterion of dyserythropoiesis； (3) MDS-related karyotype by cytogenetics and/or fluorescence in situ hybridization(FISH) studies (e.g.， +8， -7，5q-，20q-)； and (4) constant blast count ≥5 (<20%). For patients with clinical features highly suggestive of MDS (the prerequisite 1ggcriteria are met)， but when MDS-related criteria cannot be fulfilled， identification of additional abnormalities (co-criteria) may be helpful in establishing the diagnosis of MDS. These co-criteria include (1) abnormal phenotype by FC analysis，|删除0换行|(2) monoclonal myeloid cell population (molecular assays and/or point mutation analysis such as RAS mutations)， (3) abnormal gene expression profile (mRNA profiling assays)， and (4) markedly and persistently reduced colony formation of the BM or/and circulating progenitor cells \[colony-form-ing unit (CFU) assay\].

【41】**Patients who do not meet the minimal criteria for MDS and whose sustained cytopenia(s) (@6 months) cannot be explained by other hematopoietic or nonhematopoietic dis-ease are diagnosed with idiopathic cytopenia of undeter-mined significance (ICUS). Initial investigations required to establish the diagnosis of ICUS include detailed clinical his-tory (toxins， drugs， mutagenic events， etc.)， clinical evalua-tion with X-ray， differential blood count and complete serum chemistry， BM histology with immunohistochemistry， BM smear including iron staining， FC of the BM/blood， chromo-somal analysis (cytogenetics/FISH)， exclusion of viral infec-tions \[hepatitis C virus (HCV)， human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)， cytomegalovirus (CMV)， Epstein-Barr virus(EBV)， etc.\]， and molecular tests where appropriate \[e.g.， to exclude T-cell large granular lymphocyte (T-LGL) leukemia in patients with neutropenia\]. Patients with ICUS should be carefully monitored with repeated tests to exclude progres-sion to MDS (blood count with differential in 1-6-month interval and BM analysis when appropriate). Patients with-out significant cytopenias， but who have obvious dysplastic morphologic features， are diagnosed with idiopathic dyspla-sia of unknown significance (IDUS). Although IDUS is rare， patients need to be followed， as they may progress to frank myeloid malignancy.**

【43】**BLOOD**

【44】**Blood， apart from anemia， which is the most common finding in MDS， may show neutropenia and/or thrombocytopenia. Red blood cells are most often macrocytic， but may be nor-mocytic (microcytic anemia is unusual for MDS). The MDS category RARS is usually associated with mean corpuscular volume (MCV) values between 100 and 105. The red cells often display anisopoikilocytosis and may show basophilic stippling. Poikilocy tosisincludesdacrocytes _((1teardrop-_ shaped cells)， acanthocytes (spur-like cells)， and oval macro-cytes. Granulocytes are often hypogranular and hypolobated. Hypolobated granulocytes are reminiscent of inborn Pelger-Huet anomaly and are therefore called pseudo-Pelger cells. Platelets may also display atypia (including giant forms) when examined on oil magnification. Blasts， nucleated red blood cells， basophils， and micromegakaryocytes may be present on blood smear. MDS with basophilia was reported to be associated with worse outcome. Presence of 2%-4%blasts in the blood is diagnostic forRAEB-1 (even if the num-ber of blasts in the BM is <5%) and 5%-19% for RAEB-2. Based on the WHO classification， the presence of Auer rods is diagnostic for RAEB-2， even if the number of blasts in the blood is <5%.**

【45】**BM ASPIRATE**

The presence of dysplasia is necessary for the diagnosis of MDS. At least 10% of all cells of a given hematopoietic lineage must be dysplastic to allow for the diagnosis of MDS. Dysplastic red cell precursors (dyserythropoiesis) are characterized by nuclear and cytoplasmic abnormalities . Dysplastic nuclear features include nuclear budding， multinucleation， hyperchro-masia， nuclear hyperlobation， internuclear bridging， megalo-blastoid chromatin， nuclear fragmentation， irregular nuclear outlines， and karyorrhexis. Cytoplasmic abnormalities include nuclear fragments (basophilic stippling)， vacuolization with coalescing vacuoles， defective hemoglobinization (nuclear-cytoplasmic dyssynchrony)， periodic acid-Schiff stain positivity， and ring sideroblastosis. The findings that may be seen in MDS， but are more nonspecific， includeirregular (shaggy) cytoplasmic|删除0换行|borders and vacuolization. Although there is usually erythroid hyperplasia， occasional cases of MDS display erythroid hypo-plasia (associated with good response to cyclosporine A ther-apy). Ring sideroblasts are defined by at least five iron granules per cell encireling one-third or more of the nuclear rim (nor-mally less than four cytoplasmic ferritin particles can be seen in the subset of erythroid precursors).

【57】**HISTOMORPHOLOGY**

The cytomorphologie findings are complemented by histo-logic features， which include increased numbers of mega-karyocytes， megakaryocytic atypia， abnormal localization of immature precursors (ALIP)， decreased M：E ratio due to erythroid hyperplasia， and/or increased reticulin fibro-sis . Erythroid cells are not only hyperplastic， but often show prominent leftward shift， best visualized by staining with glycophorin A (GPHA) and CD71 (CD71 stains|删除0换行|strongly the most immature cells and the intensity of stain-ing decreases as the cells mature， whereas GPHA is positive in more mature components). ALIP， which is defined by the presence of aggregates of precursors (more than three cells) in the intertrabecular area of the BM， is predominantly seen in MDS cases with increased blasts (RAEB) and has been shown to be of independent prognostic significance within the International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS)-defined prognostic groups. In a majority of patients with MDS， the BM is hypercellular， whereas in minor subset of patients， BM may be hypocellular (~10%) in so-called hypocellular MDS(h-MDS). Other histologic features seen in MDS include accentuated paratrabecular immaturity， variable size of erythroid cell clusters， and increased (scattered) mast cells. Histologic analysis is also helpful to exclude other disorders(both hematopoietic and nonhematopoietic) and separate MDS from aplastic anemia.

【64】**Differential Diagnosis**

【65】MDS-f needs to be differentiated from acute panmyelosis with fibrosis and other BM processes with significant reticu-lin fibrosis， both primary and secondary. Acute panmyelo-sis with fibrosis is a rare variant of AML characterized by increased myeloblasts and significant leftward shift in ery-throid and megakaryocytic maturation. Similar to primary myelofibrosis (PMF)， the number of megakaryocytes and the degree of atypia are much more pronounced in acute panmyelosis than in MDS (including RAEB). Presence of prominent clusters of megakaryocytes with marked cel-lular atypia， including highly hyperchromatic and bizarre nuclei， favors PMF or acute panmyelosis over MDS. In contrast to PMF， splenomegaly is not a typical clinical fea-ture of MDS-f. Marrow fibrosis may accompany lympho-proliferative disorders (such as hairy cell leukemia that often presents with cytopenia) and metastatic carcinomas. Immunohistochemical stainings assist in establishing the proper diagnosis in those cases.

Hypoplastic MDS (hypocellular BM) is often associated with trisomy 6.**
