【1】The obese have an increased risk for cholelithiasis， thromboembolism， varicose veins， and blunted growth hormone response.

【2】A recent studyestimates that obesity-related mor-bidity accounts for approximately 6.8% of U.S. health care expenses.

A new observation may be important to understand- ing fat accumulation. Findings from several studies sug- _.1.._ gest that parasympathetic activity increases insulin sensitivity and fat synthesis. Supporting this theory is the observation that there appears to be an association be- t _\-..._ ween reduced parasympathetic nervous systemn function and increased plasma-free fatty acid levels， and also an as-sociation between insulin resistance in patients with a combination of obesity and type-2 diabetes mellitus. An increase in parasympathetic tone occurs at night， pro-moting nocturnal deposition of fat and possibly explain-ing why fat deposits in some areas and not others. For example， visceral white adipose tissue (intra-abdominal|删除0换行|fat) is more heavily innervated than subcutaneous fat. Systemic effects may be that elevated plasma levels of free fatty acids may lead to a pro-inflammatory and pro-atherogenic state. A low-grade systemic inflammation may factor into some of the morbidity associated with obesity. A laboratory test， C-reactive protein (CRP)， is an indicator of systemic inflammation and is more com-monly used with rheumatoid and other overtly inflam-matory-based conditions. CRP has been shown to estimate future risk of coronary artery disease. There appears to be a correlation between a high BMI and acute-phase CRP in middle-aged and elderly individuals. However， these studies did not account for confounding causes such as other disorders. A recent studyl2 demonstrated that a higher BMI is associated with higher CRP in adults aged17 to 39 years. This association was independent of any coexisting disorders that might also influence CRP. This study also indicated that the distribution of fat was cor-related with an increased CRP independent of BMI. A high waist-to-hip ratio was associated with an increase in CRP. This distribution indicates larger amounts of visceral fat. Elevated levels of CRP at 0.22 mg/dL were found in27.6% of individuals.

【4】**GENERAL STRATEGY**

【5】**History**

【6】Determine the amount of weight gain and specify over what period oftime.

【7】Determine what constitutes the patient's diet； fol-low with a diet diary.

【8】Determine whether the patient is taking any med-ications that may increase fluid retention or appetite.

【9】Determine the patient’s family history with regard to obesity and diabetes.

【10】Determine whether the patient has recently stopped smoking.

【11】Determine any changes in exercise levels.

【12】Determine whether the patient is under stress and uses food for relaxation or reward.

【13】Determine whether the patient has any symptoms of hypoglycemia (insulinoma； rare).

【14】**Examination**

【15】Weigh and measure height of the patient.

【16】**Determine the BMI.**

【17】Determine the patient's percentage of body fat with skin calipers or an impedance device (referral for wa-ter immersion method is less practical， but most accurate).

【18】Examine the patient for signs of fluid retention in abdomen and legs.

【19】Examine the patient for congestive heart failure if suspected from history (difficulty breathing while lying recumbent) and obtain a chest radiograph.

【20】Perform laboratory evaluation if the patient has historical and/or physical signs of diabetes，Cushing's lisease， or liypothyroidism.

【21】**Management**

【22】The majority of obese patients can be managed with a healthful diet and a graduated cxercisc prograin.

【23】It may be necessary to work with a team including a specialist in weight loss to better guarantee com-piiance with suggestions and providc a support net-work for those making substantial lifestyle changes.

【24】**EVALUATION**

【25】**History**

【26】It is extremely important to approach the obese patient from a health risk perspective and not be perceived as being judgmental or addressing the more cosmetic as-pects of excess weight. As mentioned above， weight gain o toFver a day or two is most often due to fluid retention. Therefore minor gain in weight over a number of days or during a woman's menstrual period is of little concern.The patient who is dieting， however， may feel discouraged. Also， when patients are exercising they must keep in mind that muscie weighs more than fat.

【27】**Examination**

【28】Estimation of a patient's relative body weight is best ac-complished with a formula to determine the BMI. In ad-dition. an estimate or measurement of body fat content is crucia， to determining the degree to which weight is due to fat and muscle. The BMI is calculated by dividing kilo-grams ofweight by meters of height. The conversion for pounds and inches is 750× lb/sg in. A BMT over 27 is equal to being about 20% overweight and warrants fur-ther investigation and tnanagement.

【29】**MANAGEMENI**

Given that the most common cause of weight gain is overeating or eating an unbalanced diet， the chiroprae-tor must decide how much time， investment， and inter-est can be donated to patient management. There are many centers that specialize in weight loss. Table 30-1 is a summary of many popular diet plans with a general de-|删除0换行|scription of the plan's focus and the pros and cons ofeach. These centers do not focus on diet alone but address is-sues of mental attitude， motivation， and exercise， Quick fixes with diet drinks or fad diets are to bc avoided. Statistically， most patients who diet eventually gain back weight over a period of a year or two. According to onc study，approximately one third ofadults who attempt to lose weight or maintain weight loss focus more on less fat than fewer calories， Less than one fifth of individuals combine a regimen of decreased caloric intake with a coupie of hours of physica\_activity each week. Regular ex-ercise such as brisk walking reduces body wcight and body fat in overweight and obese postmenopausal women.4 In a study of over 73，000 women ages 50 to79， subjects who walked or were engaged in vigorous ex-ercise 2.5 heurs a week reduced the risk for cardiovascu-lar events by about 30%.15 Researchers in the Ilealth Professionals Follow-Up Study assessed 44，000 men over12 ycars for exercisc activity and ievelsofactivity： Men with the greatest activity had a 30% decrcased risk over seden-tary maies for cardiovascular risk. Specific activities and risk reduction inciuded weight training -33% reduc-tion， rowing-18% reduction， and running -42% re-duction 16 Weight gain in woinen has been associated with a decrease in physical activity and increased levels of pain.Pain may act as a deterrent to exercise， yet weight loss has bcen shown to decrease body pain.

【31】The solution to permanent weight loss is total man-agement by a specific individual or team with inclusion of a sensible exercise routine coupled with a sensible diet. The time demand for education， ex-ercise and diet prescription， and counseling/support may be well beyond the time availability and expertise of the chiropractor. Comanagement with a medical doctor or a clinic specializing in weight loss is often more appropri-ate. The newest medical approach is with a new class of drugs called lipase inhibitors. Orlistat (Xenical)prevents the breakdown of some fat (up to 30%) so that it can be excreted in the feces without being absorbed. Some dc-gree of weight loss was achieved and maintained after18 months in a study comparing treatment with orlistat compared to placebo.18 Approximately 33% of patients on orlistat versus 25% of paticnts o placebo lost weight initially. Long-term maintenance of weight loss e10%of initial weight) was 28% for those on orlistat versus14% on placcbo.

【32】Referral for medical consultation is warranted when drugs are suspected as the underlying cause or when metabolic problenis such as Cushing's disease or hypo-thyroidistn are suspected.

Concers include risk ot cardiovascular disease and kidney stones.Any diet that restricts calories will，in the initial phases，likely decrease blood pressure，and reduce blood sugar，cholesterol and triglycerides. Eat Right for Not really a weight loss diet， but a diet that is based on your blood type，founded on the belief that a patient's blood type determines digestion Your Type and immune response. Diet has a list of foods to avoid and foods to emphasize based on blood type and can range from modified vegetarian to large portions of animal fat. Concerns are the lack of scientific evidence and the potential deficiencies in needed nutrients with some recommended plans. Beverly Hills A rapid weight loss plan with no long-term goals The premise is that an individual can lose 10-15 pounds in 35 days.There is a heavy initial emphasis on fruits thal will result in fluid loss but possible diarrhea.The claim is that eating one type of food with another type， such as a protein with a carbohydrare， destroys specific digestive enzymes， leading to weight gain and poor digestion.Therefore， the contention is that eating foods separately encourages weight loss.Concerns are the same for all diets that emphasize rapid weiqht loss with severe food restrictions and no long-term approach. Fit-for-Life Main focus is specific food combinations eaten at specific times of the day，emphasis is on fruits and vegetables There is no restriction specifically on calories or grams of fat due to the types of foods recommended (i.e.，fruits/vegetables).A vegetarian-based diet with restrictions of protein， including lean protein meats and low-fat dairy products， may have an effect of imbalance or deliciency in certain needed nutrients.This is less of a weight loss diet than an approach to healthy eating with weight loss as a side benefit. Jenny Craig This is a highly structured program focused initially on prepackaged foods， weekly counseling that promotes Ifestyle changes and teaches meal planning，exercise，and managing stress as important elements in maintaining weight loss. Mayo (linic The diet is not endorsed by the Mayo Clinic. Advantages are the medical supervision，which includes regular olood work，counseling with registered dieticians，and maintaining nutritional balance. Optifast quotes a study that indicated weight loss in 600 patients who lost 5-10% of body weight and maintained this loss for up to five years. However， much of the weight was gained back during this time frame.In other words， initial weight loss was greater，but then weight was gained back to aplateau. Pritikin A low-fat diet， the Pritikin diet focuses on unprocessed fruits and vegetables，lean animal foods，and non-fat dairy products.Calorie intake is based or"calorie density，"which is the amount of calories per pound，with a restriction to foods that contain 400 calories or less per pound.A generally healthy diet， the primary concern is ong-term compliance (as with many diets). Scarsdale Another rapid weight loss approach to be used for only two weeks， this diet emphasizes lean animal foods， fruits，vegetables，and the use of herbal appetite suppressants.There is an extre me caraohydrate restriction with no snacks allowed. This provides rapid weight loss through fluid loss.As with all rapid weight loss approaches，the vast majority of individuals gain weight back. There is also some increased risk of the development of kidney stones and galistones. South Beach A MD-developed program that has three phases. The first phase is two weeks long and focuses on normal-sized helpings oflean meats (e.g.，chicken， turkey， fish，and shelfish) and vegetables.Carbohydrates are restricted based on their glycemic index.so that the first two weeks eliminates alcoho， fruit， bread，rice， potatoes， pasta，baked goods，sugar， and pastries.Wine， fruits， and whole grains are phased in during the later two phases. Although considered alow-carb，low-fat diet，it is more about"good carbs"versus no carbs based on their glycemic index. Weight Watchers Weight ross is based on a point system for calorie restriction. 【4】“gray zone” lymphoma (B-cell lymphoma， unclassifiable with features intermediate between DLBCL and HL). Large B-cell lymphoma with features intermediate between HL and DLBCL is diagnosed when morphology is compatible with PMBL but phenotype is more typical for HL (expres sion of CD15 and/or EBV)， or when tumor resembles HL， but phenotype is more typical for DLBCL 通用删除1(英):<u>(CD45 positivity and/or strong expression of B-cell markers； Figure 24.16)</u>. Cases should not be classified as a gray zone lymphoma based on the strong expression of CD20 alone， as it can be seen in clas sical HL .

【5】**ANAPLASTIC LARGE CEll LYMPHOMA**

【6】ALCL and HL (especially syncytial variant of the NS and lymphocyte-depleted types) may share some morphologic features responsible for diagnostic difficulties 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40\]</u>. Negative PAX5 and positive EMA， one of pan-T-cell markers (CD2， CD3， CD5， and CD7)， CD4 or CD8， CD43， CD45， and espe-cially ALK help to diagnose ALCL. Occasional T-cell dis-orders， including ALCL and PTCL， may express CD15 通用删除6(英):<u>\[48\]</u>\[49.501. and/or MUM1 通用删除6(英):<u>\[49，50\]</u>， or may lack pan-T-cell antigen expres-sion (e.g.， null cell type of ALCL)， and therefore， expansion of the immunophenotypic panel and molecular testing for T-cell clonality may be needed for proper diagnosis. Involvement of the lymph node by mycosis fungoides/Sezary's syndrome may show giant R-S-like cells with scattered eosinophils. Clinical history and immunophenotype (e.g.， expression of pan-T-cell markers) help in differential diagnosis. HLs with unusual T-cell phenotype are negative for clonal rearrangement of TCR gene by polymerase chain reaction. Nodal involvement by cutaneous ALCL and even LYP with lymphatic drainage(from skin lesions) can mimic classical HL. Correlation with clinical data is crucial to diagnose those cases correctly.

【7】**PTCL， NoT OTHERWISE SPECIFIED**

Hodgkin-like and R-S-like cells are often present in PTCL， not otherwise specified， and its variants， especially f-PTCL. Large atypical CD30+， CD15+， and EBV+ Hodgkin-like and R-S-like cells mimicking classical HL (especially lympho-cyte-rich subtype) are typically seen in a rare variant of PTCL with a follicular growth pattern， described as the f-PTCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[51\]</u>. f-PTCL shows atypical small- to medium-sized CD3+ T cells|删除0换行|that have follicular helper T-cell (Tri) phenotype similar to AITL \[they express CD10， BCL6， programmed death (PD)-1， and CXCL13\]. Both PTCL and f-PTCL display an aberrant phenotype of T cells， which can be identified by either flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry.

【9】**ANGIOIMMUNOBLASTIC T-CELL LYMPHOMA**

【10】Hodgkin-like and R-S-like cells are often seen in AITL. The large atypical cells in AITL show B-cell phenotype and are positive for EBV and also CD30， which may lead to the misdiagnosis of HL. Atypical phenotype of T-cell population (including the expression of CD10， PD-1， BCL6， and CXCL13) and overall histomorphologic features (e.g.， increased vascularity， clusters of atypical clear cells， and expanded follicular dendritic cell meshwork) help in estab-lishing the correct diagnosis.

【11】**ADULT T-CELL LEUKEMIA/LYMPHOMA**

【12】Lymph node involvement by ATLL often shows R-S-like and Hodgkin-like cells， typically in Hodgkin-like type of ATLL， but also in other ATLL types， including pleomorphic small cell type， pleomorphic medium/large cell type， and anaplastic large cell type 通用删除6(英):<u>\[52\]</u>.

【13】**CUTANEOUS CD30+ T-CEll DISORDERS**

【14】**LYP is characterized by the presence of large multinucleated cells resembling R-S cells， which are CD30+. In addition， LYP may progress occasionally to either ALCL or HL. Skin can also be involved by both primary and systemic ALCLs. Since the skin is rarely involved by HL， the differential diag-nosis in the majority of primary cutaneous CD30+lymphop-roliferative disorders rarely includes HL and instead focuses on inflammatory or drug-induced dermatoses and progress-ing mycosis fungoides (MF). In few cases of cutaneous HL(more often secondary than primary)， the morphology and immunophenotype are similar to nodal counterpart.**

【15】**NODUlAR LYMPHOCYTE PREDOMINANT HL**

**NLPHL needs to be differentiated mainly from lymphocyte-rich variant of classical HL. Both entities are characterized|删除0换行|by predominance of small lymphocytes， vaguely nodular pat-tern on low magnification， and scattered large atypical cells with T-cell rosettes around them. Lymphocyte predominant(LP) cells of NLPHL are positive for CD45， B-cell markers(CD19， CD20， CD22， CD79a， BOB1， OCT2， and PAX5)， and occasionally EMA and IgD， and are negative for CD30， CD15， and EBV (EBER). The expression of PAX5 and other B-cell markers is strong in NLPHL. Only sporadic cases can be positive for CD30 and/or CD15. The B-cell-rich nodules in NLPHL also contain increased numbers of small T cells with TrH phenotype， expressing PD-1， CD3， CD4， and CD57.

【17】**HISTIOCYTE-RICH AGGREGATES**

【18】**HL with numerous histiocytic aggregates has to be differen-tiated from inflammatory lesions/granulomatous processes，**

【19】Lennert’s lymphoma， and other lymphomas with marked epithelioid cell reaction， for example， DLBCL， PTCL，AITL， or NLPHL .

【20】**NONHEMATOPOIETIC TUMORS**

【21】Metastatic carcinoma is distinguished by immunopheno-typing (keratin expression by tumor cells).

【22】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF HL IN THE BM**

【23】**The diagnostic considerations (especially in patients without history of HL) include ALCL， THRLBCL， primary myelo-fibrosis (PMF)， and other myeloproliferative neoplasms with increased reticulin fibers， AITL， metastatic carcinoma， DLBCL， and CLL with Richter’s syndrome.**

【26】For the differential diagnosis of HL based on the expression of CD30 or EBV (EBER)， see Chapter 5.

【94】**T-Cell/Histiocyte-Rich Large B-Cell Lymphoma.**

【95】**References.**

【96】NodularlymphocyterpredominantHodgkinlymphoma(NLPHL) is a monoclonal B-cell neoplasm characterized by the presence of scattered large atypical lymphocyte pre-dominant (LP) cells \[“popcorn cells，" formerly known as lymphocytic and histiocytic (L&H) cells\] and a distinct nodular pattern on low magnification 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-9\]</u>. NLPHL involves most often the cervical， axillary， or inguinal lymph nodes. Mediastinal and bone marrow (BM) involvement are rare.

【97】NLPHL occurs at any age， but most often in the 30-50-year-old age group with median age around 40 years 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. Patients are predominantly males. There is an association between NLPHL and progressively transformed germinal centers(PTGC)， as it may be seen simultaneously with or may pre-cede NLPHL. Therefore， patients with PTGC， but without typ-ical popcorn cells should be closely followed since they have slightly higher risk of developing NLPHL. The prognosis of NLPHL is usually favorable， especially at early stage. The dis-ease develops slowly with frequent relapses. It usually remains responsive to the therapy.

Overall survival rates are similar in patients with NLPHL(86%) and classical Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) (82%) at clini-cal stages IA and IIA treated with anthracycline-based che-motherapy plus high-dose extended irradiation； they share a very good prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11\]</u>. Treatment of NLPHL patients using standard HL protocols leads to complete remission in >95% of patients (survival and freedom from treatment failure are worse in advanced-stage patients than in early-stage patients) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6\]</u>. Only a small subset of patients with NLPHL in whom lymph node biopsy shows NLPHL with a typical， purely nodular pat-tern also may have lymphoma in the BM. BM involvement is|删除0换行|associated with laboratory， radiologic， or morphologic evidence of aggressive disease and poor prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12\]</u>.

【99】**NLPHL and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma(THRLBCL) may occur concurrently or subsequently in the same patient 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13-15\]</u>. At present， an overlap between NLPHL and THRLBCL cannot be excluded 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，16\]</u>. Presence of a diffuse T-cell/histiocyte-rich-like pattern is more common in patients with recurrent disease than those without recur-rence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[17\]</u>. The focally diffuse pattern (THRLBCL-like) in NLPHL is an independent predictor of recurrent disease \[171. Analysis of sequential biopsies from patients with recur-rent disease suggests that the presence of increased number of lymphocyte predominant (LP) cells outside the nodules might represent early evolution to a diffuse (THRLBCL-like) pattern and eventually large B-cell lymphoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[17\]</u>.**

【100】A subset of patients with NLPHL (2%-7%) may develop more aggressive lymphomas， most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)， which were reported to have a better prognosis than de novo DLBCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，14，18-21\]</u>. In a series reported by Huang et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[22\]</u>， however， there were no signifi-cant differences in the survival outcomes between patients with DLBCL arising in NLPHL and age- and sex-matched patients with de novo DLBCL. In that report， the median time to the development of DLBCL in those with prior NLPHL was only 1 year (range： 0.5-24 years)， the median age of the patients at the time of diagnosis of DLBCL was46 years (range： 18-72 years)， and the male-to-female ratio was 17：4. Initial splenic involvement by NLPHL is associ-ated with higher risk of transformation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. The 10-year progression-free and overall survival rates in patients with transformed lymphoma are 52% and 62%， respectively 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>.

【101】**MORPHOLOGY**

【102】**LYMPH NODE**

The most characteristic morphologic feature of NLPHL is the distinct nodular pattern of the lymph node under low magnification . Nodules are often ill defined and vague and are usually larger than those of follicular lymphoma (FL)， follicular hyperplasia， or nodular mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). The nodules contain histiocytes， which may give the nodules a pseudo-starry-sky appearance on low magnification. The nodular pattern is easily visual-ized by staining with CD21 and/or CD23， which also shows an expanded follicular dendritic cell (FDC) meshwork， or by staining with B-cell markers (e.g.， PAX5 or CD20). There are no fibrous septae separating individual nodules，|删除0换行|as seen in classical nodular sclerosis HL. Although focal diffuse areas may be present， cases with a completely dif-fuse growth pattern most often represent THRLBCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>.

【104】**LP cells  are large with multilobated or folded nuclei， prominent nucleoli， and pale vesicular chromatin. Because of their cytologic features， they are also called“popcorn cells” or L&H cells. LP cells differ morphologically from Reed-Sternberg (R-S) cells

【1】**“GRAY ZONE LYMPHOMA”**

【2】**Occasional cases in the mediastinum that shows overlap-ping features between HL and DLBCL are classified as**

【3】通用删除16(英):<u>FIGURE 24.16 “Gray zone lymphoma" (large B-cell lymphoma with features intermediate between HL and DLBCL).</u>

【4】“gray zone” lymphoma (B-cell lymphoma， unclassifiable with features intermediate between DLBCL and HL). Large B-cell lymphoma with features intermediate between HL and DLBCL is diagnosed when morphology is compatible with PMBL but phenotype is more typical for HL (expres sion of CD15 and/or EBV)， or when tumor resembles HL， but phenotype is more typical for DLBCL 通用删除1(英):<u>(CD45 positivity and/or strong expression of B-cell markers； Figure 24.16)</u>. Cases should not be classified as a gray zone lymphoma based on the strong expression of CD20 alone， as it can be seen in clas sical HL .

【5】**ANAPLASTIC LARGE CEll LYMPHOMA**

【6】ALCL and HL (especially syncytial variant of the NS and lymphocyte-depleted types) may share some morphologic features responsible for diagnostic difficulties 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40\]</u>. Negative PAX5 and positive EMA， one of pan-T-cell markers (CD2， CD3， CD5， and CD7)， CD4 or CD8， CD43， CD45， and espe-cially ALK help to diagnose ALCL. Occasional T-cell dis-orders， including ALCL and PTCL， may express CD15 通用删除6(英):<u>\[48\]</u>\[49.501. and/or MUM1 通用删除6(英):<u>\[49，50\]</u>， or may lack pan-T-cell antigen expres-sion (e.g.， null cell type of ALCL)， and therefore， expansion of the immunophenotypic panel and molecular testing for T-cell clonality may be needed for proper diagnosis. Involvement of the lymph node by mycosis fungoides/Sezary's syndrome may show giant R-S-like cells with scattered eosinophils. Clinical history and immunophenotype (e.g.， expression of pan-T-cell markers) help in differential diagnosis. HLs with unusual T-cell phenotype are negative for clonal rearrangement of TCR gene by polymerase chain reaction. Nodal involvement by cutaneous ALCL and even LYP with lymphatic drainage(from skin lesions) can mimic classical HL. Correlation with clinical data is crucial to diagnose those cases correctly.

【7】**PTCL， NoT OTHERWISE SPECIFIED**

Hodgkin-like and R-S-like cells are often present in PTCL， not otherwise specified， and its variants， especially f-PTCL. Large atypical CD30+， CD15+， and EBV+ Hodgkin-like and R-S-like cells mimicking classical HL (especially lympho-cyte-rich subtype) are typically seen in a rare variant of PTCL with a follicular growth pattern， described as the f-PTCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[51\]</u>. f-PTCL shows atypical small- to medium-sized CD3+ T cells|删除0换行|that have follicular helper T-cell (Tri) phenotype similar to AITL \[they express CD10， BCL6， programmed death (PD)-1， and CXCL13\]. Both PTCL and f-PTCL display an aberrant phenotype of T cells， which can be identified by either flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry.

【9】**ANGIOIMMUNOBLASTIC T-CELL LYMPHOMA**

【10】Hodgkin-like and R-S-like cells are often seen in AITL. The large atypical cells in AITL show B-cell phenotype and are positive for EBV and also CD30， which may lead to the misdiagnosis of HL. Atypical phenotype of T-cell population (including the expression of CD10， PD-1， BCL6， and CXCL13) and overall histomorphologic features (e.g.， increased vascularity， clusters of atypical clear cells， and expanded follicular dendritic cell meshwork) help in estab-lishing the correct diagnosis.

【11】**ADULT T-CELL LEUKEMIA/LYMPHOMA**

【12】Lymph node involvement by ATLL often shows R-S-like and Hodgkin-like cells， typically in Hodgkin-like type of ATLL， but also in other ATLL types， including pleomorphic small cell type， pleomorphic medium/large cell type， and anaplastic large cell type 通用删除6(英):<u>\[52\]</u>.

【13】**CUTANEOUS CD30+ T-CEll DISORDERS**

【14】**LYP is characterized by the presence of large multinucleated cells resembling R-S cells， which are CD30+. In addition， LYP may progress occasionally to either ALCL or HL. Skin can also be involved by both primary and systemic ALCLs. Since the skin is rarely involved by HL， the differential diag-nosis in the majority of primary cutaneous CD30+lymphop-roliferative disorders rarely includes HL and instead focuses on inflammatory or drug-induced dermatoses and progress-ing mycosis fungoides (MF). In few cases of cutaneous HL(more often secondary than primary)， the morphology and immunophenotype are similar to nodal counterpart.**

【15】**NODUlAR LYMPHOCYTE PREDOMINANT HL**

**NLPHL needs to be differentiated mainly from lymphocyte-rich variant of classical HL. Both entities are characterized|删除0换行|by predominance of small lymphocytes， vaguely nodular pat-tern on low magnification， and scattered large atypical cells with T-cell rosettes around them. Lymphocyte predominant(LP) cells of NLPHL are positive for CD45， B-cell markers(CD19， CD20， CD22， CD79a， BOB1， OCT2， and PAX5)， and occasionally EMA and IgD， and are negative for CD30， CD15， and EBV (EBER). The expression of PAX5 and other B-cell markers is strong in NLPHL. Only sporadic cases can be positive for CD30 and/or CD15. The B-cell-rich nodules in NLPHL also contain increased numbers of small T cells with TrH phenotype， expressing PD-1， CD3， CD4， and CD57.

【17】**HISTIOCYTE-RICH AGGREGATES**

【18】**HL with numerous histiocytic aggregates has to be differen-tiated from inflammatory lesions/granulomatous processes，**

【19】Lennert’s lymphoma， and other lymphomas with marked epithelioid cell reaction， for example， DLBCL， PTCL，AITL， or NLPHL .

【20】**NONHEMATOPOIETIC TUMORS**

【21】Metastatic carcinoma is distinguished by immunopheno-typing (keratin expression by tumor cells).

【22】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF HL IN THE BM**

【23】**The diagnostic considerations (especially in patients without history of HL) include ALCL， THRLBCL， primary myelo-fibrosis (PMF)， and other myeloproliferative neoplasms with increased reticulin fibers， AITL， metastatic carcinoma， DLBCL， and CLL with Richter’s syndrome.**

【96】NodularlymphocyterpredominantHodgkinlymphoma(NLPHL) is a monoclonal B-cell neoplasm characterized by the presence of scattered large atypical lymphocyte pre-dominant (LP) cells \[“popcorn cells，" formerly known as lymphocytic and histiocytic (L&H) cells\] and a distinct nodular pattern on low magnification 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-9\]</u>. NLPHL involves most often the cervical， axillary， or inguinal lymph nodes. Mediastinal and bone marrow (BM) involvement are rare.

【97】NLPHL occurs at any age， but most often in the 30-50-year-old age group with median age around 40 years 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. Patients are predominantly males. There is an association between NLPHL and progressively transformed germinal centers(PTGC)， as it may be seen simultaneously with or may pre-cede NLPHL. Therefore， patients with PTGC， but without typ-ical popcorn cells should be closely followed since they have slightly higher risk of developing NLPHL. The prognosis of NLPHL is usually favorable， especially at early stage. The dis-ease develops slowly with frequent relapses. It usually remains responsive to the therapy.

Overall survival rates are similar in patients with NLPHL(86%) and classical Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) (82%) at clini-cal stages IA and IIA treated with anthracycline-based che-motherapy plus high-dose extended irradiation； they share a very good prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11\]</u>. Treatment of NLPHL patients using standard HL protocols leads to complete remission in >95% of patients (survival and freedom from treatment failure are worse in advanced-stage patients than in early-stage patients) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6\]</u>. Only a small subset of patients with NLPHL in whom lymph node biopsy shows NLPHL with a typical， purely nodular pat-tern also may have lymphoma in the BM. BM involvement is|删除0换行|associated with laboratory， radiologic， or morphologic evidence of aggressive disease and poor prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12\]</u>.

【99】**NLPHL and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma(THRLBCL) may occur concurrently or subsequently in the same patient 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13-15\]</u>. At present， an overlap between NLPHL and THRLBCL cannot be excluded 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，16\]</u>. Presence of a diffuse T-cell/histiocyte-rich-like pattern is more common in patients with recurrent disease than those without recur-rence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[17\]</u>. The focally diffuse pattern (THRLBCL-like) in NLPHL is an independent predictor of recurrent disease \[171. Analysis of sequential biopsies from patients with recur-rent disease suggests that the presence of increased number of lymphocyte predominant (LP) cells outside the nodules might represent early evolution to a diffuse (THRLBCL-like) pattern and eventually large B-cell lymphoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[17\]</u>.**

【100】A subset of patients with NLPHL (2%-7%) may develop more aggressive lymphomas， most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)， which were reported to have a better prognosis than de novo DLBCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，14，18-21\]</u>. In a series reported by Huang et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[22\]</u>， however， there were no signifi-cant differences in the survival outcomes between patients with DLBCL arising in NLPHL and age- and sex-matched patients with de novo DLBCL. In that report， the median time to the development of DLBCL in those with prior NLPHL was only 1 year (range： 0.5-24 years)， the median age of the patients at the time of diagnosis of DLBCL was46 years (range： 18-72 years)， and the male-to-female ratio was 17：4. Initial splenic involvement by NLPHL is associ-ated with higher risk of transformation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. The 10-year progression-free and overall survival rates in patients with transformed lymphoma are 52% and 62%， respectively 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>.

【101】**MORPHOLOGY**

【102】**LYMPH NODE**

The most characteristic morphologic feature of NLPHL is the distinct nodular pattern of the lymph node under low magnification . Nodules are often ill defined and vague and are usually larger than those of follicular lymphoma (FL)， follicular hyperplasia， or nodular mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). The nodules contain histiocytes， which may give the nodules a pseudo-starry-sky appearance on low magnification. The nodular pattern is easily visual-ized by staining with CD21 and/or CD23， which also shows an expanded follicular dendritic cell (FDC) meshwork， or by staining with B-cell markers (e.g.， PAX5 or CD20). There are no fibrous septae separating individual nodules，|删除0换行|as seen in classical nodular sclerosis HL. Although focal diffuse areas may be present， cases with a completely dif-fuse growth pattern most often represent THRLBCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>.

【104】**LP cells  are large with multilobated or folded nuclei， prominent nucleoli， and pale vesicular chromatin. Because of their cytologic features， they are also called“popcorn cells” or L&H cells. LP cells differ morphologically from Reed-Sternberg (R-S) cells

【1】**Visual hallucinations are defined by seeing something that is not present. Closely related to the pathology of visual hallucinations， there is another neu-ropsychiatric syndrome which is more often present in LBD and PDD than in AD. This syndrome is called delusional misidentification and is usually restricted to relatives of patients with Capgras syndrome 删除1:<u>(Thiel， Studte， Hildebrandt， Huster， & Weerda， 2014)</u>. Patients with Capgras syndrome recog-nize the faces of relatives but do not believe that the subject with this face aligns with what their relatives really look like. In addition， for cognitive neuropsychological purposes， patients with the Capgras syndrome show almost no impairment in face recognition (i.e.， no prosopagnosia). However， patients with LBD suffer from face recognition problems， whereby these problems also correlate with their tendency to detect pareidolias 删除1:<u>(Uchiyama et al.， 2012)</u>.**

【3】**3.4.4 Treatment of Lewy body disease (and Parkinson’s disease with dementia)**

【4】**AIrecentsystematic review by Morrin， Fang， Servant， Aarsland， and Rajkumar ((2018) on the efficacy of nonpharmacological interventions in LBD revealed that there are only a few studies regarding nonpharmacologi-cal interventions in LBD. Further none of these studies had an evidence-based medicine level higher than three， which means that there are no con-trolled studies on this topic at all. The majority of these studies used brain stimulation (deep brain stimulation， transcranial direct current stimulation， etc.). Only one study focused on cognitive impairment and followed a single case design， therefore offering limited evidence. The results of this study dis-played a positive result for the cognitive intervention. However， on the back-ground of this review， it is impossible to argue whether a nonpharmacological treatment of LBD is possible or not.**

【5】**There are no definite guidelines for a pharmacological treatment of LBD. The tendency to develop visual hallucinations restricts the possibility of a dopaminergic treatment. On the other hand， LBD patients are hypersensitive to neuroleptic drugs， which might be helpful to reduce the hallucinations. The acetylcholine- esterase inhibitors may be beneficial in dampening the tendency to hallucinate， however， this is not always the case. The German guideline for dementia argues that memantine may reduce the neuropsychiat-ric symptoms in LBD patients. It should also be noted that the efficacy of acetylcholine- esterase inhibitors was shown for demented PD patients but not for patients with the clinical diagnosis of LBD. Thus the usage of these drugs in LBD might not routinely covered by the healthSsystem reimbursement.**

【6】**3.4.5 A case example**

【8】The visual field showed no deficits， eye movements were unimpaired and there was no sign for a vertical gaze paresis or restriction of vertical sac-cades. Additionally the performance in the VOSP subtest “incomplete let-ters” and “number location” was impaired.

Rey's complex understanding was too difficult and therefore its execution was discontinued. The results of the MMSE showed a score of 15， which corresponds to a moderate dementia. 【14】**Patients with LBD suffer from attentional deficits including short- and long-term attentional fluctuations. If LBD is suspected， relatives and the patient should be examined for such deficits (e.g.， by using the Mayo Fluctuation Scale) and through alertness and vigilance tests (as long as the patients tolerate such investigations). Cognitive fluctuations and visuoper-ceptive disorders are predictors for the existence of visual hallucination， which is a prominent sign of LBD. The screening test of the VOSP， the incomplete letters test of the VOSP， and the number location test of the VOSP can be used to explore the existence of visuoperceptive impair-ments. The screening test of the VOSP assesses the tendency to detect par-eidolias due to a local attention bias， the incomplete letters test concerns the ventral visual pathway and the numbers location test the dorsal visual pathway. If the patient is able to， a more strenuous copying task should be included as part of the assessment as opposed to the items of visuocon-struction of the CERAD-NAB. The exploration for visual hallucination should also include enquiries regarding REM sleep behavioral disorder and concerning dream-like states during the night and illusion of movement or objects in darkened room or in the evening. The approach is a broad-based evaluation look-ing for any clue that may suggest the underlying cause. It is highly unusual to have fever as the only indicator of a disease or disorder. Localizing fndings by organ or sys-tem is usually revealing. See the applicable chapters of this text based on these accompanying signs or symptoms.

【26】General indicators of a viral infection in an adult are a low-grade fever and associated general aches and pains， a headache， malaise， or fatigue. An adult with a bacterial infection presents with a fever above 103°F and the gen-eral symptoms of a viral infection plus some localizingfindings in the throat， abdomen， or chest. Children， on HnOngs1 the other hand， may run high temperatures with almost any illness， including viral infections， otitis media， measles， and roseola. Very high readings (>105°F) are medical emergencies suggesting intracranial hetnorrhage or tu-mor， pancreatitis， or a bad urinary tract infection. If the temperature remains at this elevation， significant brain damage or malignant cardiac arrhythinias may occur.

【27】When the fever is not obviously tied to a flu or upper respiratory infection， a potential valuable avenue ot ques-tioning is recent travel within or outside the United States.8 Certain fungal infections are endemic to specific regions of the United States. Following the same line of questioning， contact with certain animals such as birds， dogs， cats， rats or other rodents， or livestock suggests a spe-cific infectious organism.

【28】In the past， it was recommended to determine a time curve for fever presentation in an attenipt to attach a spe-cific diagnosis to a specific pattern of fever activity. This approach is now not considered useful as a match-type ap-proach. The temporal sequence， however， may provide valuable clues to the underlying cause.

【29】**MANAGEMENT**

There are two overlapping goals of management：(1) con-trol for excessive fever and ensure adequate hydration and (2) treat the underlying cause if it poses a health risk ISTA1to the patient. Control of fever is rarely necessary unless it reaches the range of 103° to 104°F At this level of fever it may be necessary to use cold packs， alcohol or cold sponges， or cold baths. Generally， this level of fever is well tolerated. If medication is used it is important to give aspirin or acetaminophen every 4 hours without a|删除0换行|break in routine. Giving it only at night may cause a re-actionary occurrence of chills or sweats. It is important not to give aspirin to children， especially those with flu or chicken pox， because of the risk of Reye's syndrome(leads to brain and liver darage or death).

【42】**CONTEXT**

【43】If asked， most patients in their life would have a com-plaint of disrupted sleep at some times. Often they can re-late this to a specific event such as a stressful incident， alcohol ingestion， or pain. When it is a prolonged or chronic problem， the patient becomes concerned. The conscious effort to initiate sleep often may worsen the condition. It is interesting to note that underreporting is the standard for one of the most common sleep disor-ders： insomnia. A 1991 Gallup survey found that only5% ofinsomniacs consulted a physician. Approximately30% had mentioned it when presenting to a doctor for other complaints.

【44】It is not always obvious what a person does or does not do during sleep. With exces-sive tiredness or fatigue， there is the obvious disruption of functional ability with daily activities； however， the larger concern is the potential danger when driving a car or operating other potentially dangerous machinery.

【45】Although many sleep problems arc transient and/or benign， when a primary sleep disorder is detected， fur-ther evaluation at a sleep laboratory is necessary to identify clearly the cause and plan for subsequent management.

【66】**RELEVANT ANATOMY AND PHYSIOLOGY**

【67】Sleep is a complex interactive function coordinated by many parts of the brain. The structures that facilitate sleep include the basal forebrain， the dorsal raphe nu-clei， the midline thalamus， and the area around the soli-tary tract in the medulla. Waking is facilitated by the reticular activating system (pons and midbrain) and the posterior hypothalamus. This interaction is dependent on changing levels of serotonin， catecholamines， acetyl-choline， and a host of other neurotransmitters. During sleep there are also fluctuations of hormonal levels that may play a role in the quality of sleep and wakefulness. One example is the decrease in epinephrine and cortisol cou-pled with elevated histamine and other mediator levels be-tween midnightand 4AM. These changes correlate with worsening of asthma at night.

【68】Sleep is generally divided into two phases in relation-ship to changing eye movement and other electrophysi-ologic events： rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. These two dis-tinct states cycle throughout the night at about 90-minute intervals. They are not equal， however. NREM accounts for approximately 80% of total sleep.

【69】NREM sleep is divided into four stages. Stages 3 and4 are referred to as delta sleep. NREM is characterized by slowing of the electroencephalogram (EEG)， with ac-companying muscle relaxation， and slow， rolling eye movements. EEG activity slows dramatically during stages 3 and 4. This dleep sleep occurs mainly in the first few hours of sleeping. During this delta sleep， dreaming is less vivid than it is during REM. Patients awakened during delta sleep recall more thought fragments than actual drearns. Only 5% of patients recall vivid dreams.-

【70】REM sleep is more analogous to wakefulness in that there is a faster EEG rate combined with an increase and variability of autonomic nervous system function. Heart rate， respiration， blood pressure， and penile erec-tions vary widely throughout REM sleep. Peripheral voluntary muscles， however， are paralyzed with the ex-ception of the eyelids. This accounts for the phenome-non of sleep paralysis wherein， upon wakening， an individual is temporarily not able to move. When per-sistent and recurrent， narcolepsy， a disorder of REM sleep， is suggested.

【71】NREM begins first， cycling through its four stages. This is followed approximately 80 to 120 minutes later with the first REM sleep， lasting only about 5 to 10 min-utes. As the night progresses， the intensity and duration of REM sleep increase to about 15 to 45 minutes. Vivid dreaming is a characteristic event of REM sleep. Given that REM sleep becomes more intense and lasts longer as the night progresses， the majority of dreaming occurs in the last few hours ofsleeping.

【72】There is a maturation phenomenon associated with time spent in REM or NREM. Newborns spend 50% of their time in REM and enter REM soon after sleep ini-tiation. The time spent in REM decreases as the newborn matures to as little as 20% by 6 months of age. The cor-responding switch to an adult pattern of REM/NREM cy-cling begins at around 4 months and is associated with a concomitant increase in the production of melatonin. This connection between melatonin and sleep has led to the recent use of melatonin in the elderly to help “nor-OfRFMR malize" sleep. In the elderly the amount of RFM remains the same； however， there is a marked decrease in deep sleep (stages 3 and 4).

【117】**History**

【118】A full history of the presenting complaint is extremely important， as are any associated symptoms. The history must be interpreted with reference to the gestational age， as aetiolo-gies change throughout pregnancy.

【119】Specific questions that may aid diagnosis include the following.

【120】Did the pain start gradually or suddenly?

【121】Is it dull， aching and constant， or is it sharp and stabbing?

【122】**Is it associated with meals?**

【123】Is it well localised and has there been any change?

【124】Are there any associated features， e.g. nausea and vomiting?

【125】Are there any obvious relieving or exacerbating factors?

【126】**Physical examination**

【127】Clinical findings may be less obvious and more dif-ficult to elicit in pregnancy than in non-pregnant women with the same disorder.

【128】Peritoneal signs are often absent in pregnancy as a result of lifting and stretching of the anterior abdominal wall. This means that any underlying inflammation is not in direct contact with the peri-toneum， thus reducing guarding.

【129】To help distinguish extrauterine tenderness from uterine tenderness， examination of the patient in a lateral decubitus position may be useful. This manoeuvre displaces the uterus to one side.

【130】**Laboratory investigations**

【131】Commonly used laboratory tests have different ranges in1pregnancy  and， therefore， can be of limited use in aiding diagnosis.

【132】**Radiological investigations**

【133】Ultrasound scanning is the most commonly used investigation for investigating a pregnant abdomen. It is safe， and the gallbladder， liver， pancreas and kidneys can be evaluated easily.

【134】lonising radiation that produces exposures <0.05 Gy(=50rad) have not been associated with fetal abnor-malities or pregnancy loss. However， there is a possi-ble association between prenatal radiation exposure and childhood cancer.

【135】lonising radiation should only beused when absolutely indicated medically， and other imaging options have been considered and rejected.

【136】Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is not recom-mended in the first trimester and not all MRI con-trast agents are approved for use in pregnancy. It has been used in later pregnancy to exclude mor-bidly adherent placentae. It must be remembered that the duty of care of any attending doctor is pri-marily to the mother as the fetus has no legal standing whilst in utero.

【137】**Conditions with increased frequency in pregnancy**

【138】The following conditions occur：more fre-quently in pregnant women compared with non-pregnant women：

【139】gastro-oesophageal reflux/oesophagitis；

【140】biliary colic；

【141】acute cholecystitis.

【142】**Conditions due to pregnancy**

【143】The following conditions occur as a result of pregnancy：

【144】rupture of the rectus abdominis muscles；

【145】acute fatty liver of pregnancy；

【146】HELLP (haemolysis， elevated liver enzymes and low platelets)；

【147】spontaneous rupture of the liver (due to HELPP).

【148】**Conditions incidental to pregnancy**

【149】**These are：**

【150】non-ulcer dyspepsia；

【151】**gastric and duodenal ulceration；**

【152】gastritis and duodenitis：

【153】acute and chronic pancreatitis.

【154】**Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease**

【155】This condition is common in non-pregnant women and almost universal to some degree in pregnancy. It is due to an increased intra-abdominal pressure from a gravid uterus and leads to dysfunction of the lower oesophageal sphincter . This is also aggravated by increased serum progesterone levels， which cause relaxation of involuntary muscle. There is also delayed clearance of the reflux leading to increased acid exposure times.

【157】**Clinical features include：**

【158】heartburn (retrosternal pain related to meals， pos-ture and exercise)；

【159】waterbrash (excess salivation， especially during an episode of pain)；

【160】regurgitation of acid and bile， which can， rarely， give rise to nocturnal sore throat or indeed asthma.

【161】**Treatment**

【162】General measures include elevation of the head of the bed， small frequent meals and avoiding any-thing that obviously exacerbates the symptoms. Patients should be advised to avoid eating just prior to lying down. Alginates can be very useful for symptomatic relief of mild symptoms. Although there is no conclusive evidence for the safety of H2 blockers and proton-pump inhibitors in preg-nancy， both have been widely used for symptomatic relief of refractory symptoms.

【163】**Biliary colic and acute cholecystitis**

【164】Asymptomatic gallbladder disease occurs in 3-4per cent of pregnant women. It is estimated that acute cholecystitis occurs in 1：1130 to 1：12 890pregnancies.

【165】Clinical features

【166】Pain is usually moderately severe and constant in both acute cholecystitis and biliary colic. It is most commonly felt in the right upper quadrant but can be epigastric radiating to the back.

【167】Vomiting occurs in 50 per cent of patients and fever is common in cholecystitis.

【168】Ultrasound scanning is diagnostic and safe.

【169】Blood tests are of limited value as both leucocytosis and raised alkaline phosphatasSeelevels are observed in healthy pregnancies.

【170】Transient increases in amylase can occur in 30 per cent of those with biliary colic but markedly raised levels suggest pancreatitis.

【171】**Treatment**

【172】Conservative treatment with intravenous fluids and analgesia， particularly pethidine， is the initial approach. Broad-spectrum antibiotics should be included if systemic symptoms are prominent. Surgery may be necessary but timing is contro-versial， with advocates of both surgery postpar-tum and during pregnancy. Ideally this should be undertaken during the second trimester， which minimises the risks for premature delivery. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is safe in preg-nancy， although caution must be observed owing to potential pressure on the inferior vena cava as well as the increasing size of the uterus.

【173】**Acute pancreatitis**

【174】This occurs most commonly secondary to gall-stones and is associated with a fetal loss of 10-20per cent. In these cases， endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreaticogram and sphincterotomy have been performed safely in pregnant patients with gallstone pancreatitis or obstructive jaun-dice. In such cases， the uterus must be protected with a lead shield.

【31】**ILATED pore and pilar sheath acanthoma have numerous denominators in common. Both are characterized by a central crater comprised of contiguous infundibula， and within the crater are plugs of cornified cells. Both conditions exhibit buds of epithelial cells that radiate from the lining of the central infundibular crater. The buds of epithelial cells have smooth borders. At the periphery of the infundibular component of both conditions， fibrous tissue is compressed. Both lesions are well cir-cumscribed， may be vertical in orientation， and may extend to the level of’skeletal muscle on the face， where both tend to occur.**

【32】**Despite the numerous histopathologic features shared by dilated pore and pilar sheath acanthoma， they can be differentiated from one another histopathologically by several repeatable findings. The buds of epithelium in dilated pore consist of cells of the infundibulum， i.e.， they are infundibular rete ridges， whereas the lobules of pilar sheath acanthoma are constituted mostly of cells of the isthmic portion of the upper segment of a hair follicle. The infundibular rete ridges of dilated pore are devoid of ducts or cysts， whereas the lobules of pilar sheath acanthoma usually contain structures that resemble sebaceous ducts and cysts that contain cornified cells. Last， dilated pore shows no evidence of follicular or sebaceous differentiation， but Pilar sheath acanthoma reveals both， i.e. isthmic differentiation in lobules and sebaccous differentiation in the form of sebaceous ductal structures， individual sebaceous cells， and， rarely， sebaccous lobules. Episodically， fol-licular differentiation may be toward germs and papillae that are situated at the periphery of lobules. In short， dilated pore is a variant of an infundib-ular cyst in which prominent rete ridges are present along the entire cir-cumference， whereas pilar sheath acanthoma is a benign neoplasm with follicular and sebaceous differentiation.**

【33】**Clinically， dilated pore， as the name denotes， usually presents itselfon a face as a widely dilated follicular ostium plugged by horny material. The age of patients with dilated pore ranges from the 20’s to the 80's， but most patients are in their 50's and 60’s. The commonest sites for dilated pore are the lip and cheeks. Pilar sheath acanthoma also presents itself clinically as a“dilated pore，" being typified by a central ostium that is plugged by horny contents. Pilar sheath acanthoma tends to occur on the upper lip and the age range for it is much like that for dilated pore. Early lesions of pilar sheath acanthoma have a silhouette much like that of dilated pore. As pilar sheath acanthoma evolves， however， differences between the t wWoO Cconditions become evident.**

【34】**Dilated pore is nothing more than an infundibular cyst that has a widely dilated ostium and rete ridges that punctuate the circumference of the lining. Step sections through a dilated pore invariably reveal an indubi-table infundibular cyst that often can be seen to have ruptured as evidenced by either suppurative granulomatous inflammation contiguous with it or by an adjacent scar.**

【35】**DilatedFpore must be distingjuished from a comedo. Unlike a comedo， dilated pore has cornified cells arranged in basket-weave and laminated pattern， whereas cornified cells in a comedo are arranged compactly. Fur-thermore， comedones do not have rete ridges along their sides. Pilar sheath acanthoma must be set apart histopathologically from infundibulocystic basal-cell carcinoma， which also has numerous infundibular cyst-like struc-tures and two types of epitheliumn， but one of them at the periphery of aggregations is basophilic and resembles follicular germs， and the other is eosinophilic and resembles epithelium of the outer sheath above Adamson’s fringe. In contrast to this distinctive variant of basal-cell carcinoma with follicular differentiation， pilar sheath acanthoma lacks evidences consis-tently of follicular germs， is characterized by a central crater filled with cornified cells， and shows signs of sebaceous differentiation in the form of sebaceous ducts and sebaceous cells.**

【36】In sum， dilated pore and pilar sheath acanthoma are follicular abnor-malities with many similarities， but with differences that enable them to be recognized at scanning magnification， so-called dilated pore being an in-fundibular cyst and so-calledpilar sheath acanthoma being a benign neo-plasm with follicular and sebaceous differentiation.

**TRICHOADENOMA and microcystic adnexal carci-|删除0换行|noma resemble cach other sufficiently to pose a diagnostic dilemma at times， even though the former is a hamartoma and the latter an adenocarci-noma. Both may have several histopathologic features in common： presence of infundibular cyst-like structures， scant stroma， epithelial components connected to pre-existing normal epithelial structures， cords and columns of epithelium linking cystic structures， and granulomatous foreign body reaction to ruptured “cysts”"in some specimens. Both lesions also tend to involve at least the entire dermis， and both have cornified cells inside cystic spaces. Criteria that allow them to be distinguished are symmetry of trichoadenoma and asymmetry of microcystic adnexal carcinoma， predom-inance always of the cystic component in trichoadenoma and predominance usually of the solid component in microcystic adnexal carcinoma， large， ovoid“cysts”in trichoadenoma whose walls are hardly variable in thickness， but small“cysts”in microcystic adnexal carcinoma that are highly variable in shape and in the thickness of their walls， and an occasional cyst lined by sebaceous ductal epithelium in trichoadenoma， but not in microcystic ad-nexal carcinoma. As a rule， trichoadenomas are limited to the dermis， whereas microcystic adnexal carcinomas tend to extend into subcutaneous fat and even into fascia and skeletal muscle.

Clinically， trichoadenomas are solitary lesions positioned principally on the face. They range in size from about 3 mm to 15 mm and may appear any time during adult life. They are considered by many authors to be benign neoplasms， but to us they seem to represent a hamartoma. Microcys-tic adnexal carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm that occurs mostly in middle-aged women. The clinical appearance usually is that of an indurated plaque situated commonly on an upper lip or elsewhere in the central part of the face. These carcinomas are destructive locally and can penetrate into deep structures such as a paranasal sinus and an orbit. Many authors con-sider microcystic adnexal carcinoma to be a neoplasm of follicular and eccrine origin. We have observed “decapitation” secretion episodically in tubules of microcystic adnexal carcinoma， a finding that indicates apocrine， rather than eccrine， differentiation. Homogeneous eosinophilic material often fills lumens of tubules in microcystic adnexal carcinoma， and that also is a sign of apocrine secretion. The conclusion that microcystic adnexal carcinoma shows apocrine， rather than eccrine， differentiation seems espe-cially tenable in the context of the close relationship between apocrine and follicular structures in the neoplasm，i.e.， tubules sometimes are continuous with infundibular cystic structures. The relationship recapitulates happen-|删除0换行|ings in an embryo where apocrine units derive from follicular ones. A neo-plasm on a breast designated syringomatous adenoma of the nipple seems to us to be identical to microcystic adnexal carcinoma.**

【106】**Management of microcystic adnexal carcinoma is total excision of the neoplasm. Because that is not always feasible by conventional surgical tech-nique， Moh’s micrographic surgery may be the method of choice in selected cases.**

【107】**Trichoadenoma also must be differentiated from comedones and in-fundibular cysts that develop over the zygoma in persons whose skin has been battered by sunlight， a condition known as Favre-Rachouchot syn-drome. The latter syndrome is characterized by discrete， true infundibular cysts that are not connected to one another by columns of epithelial cells and by extensive solar elastosis. In some instances microcystic adnexal carci-nomna must be distinguished from syringoma. The latter condition tends to be confined to the upper half of the dermis and is unassociated with elon-gated tubules whose lumens house brightly eosinophilic homogeneous ma-terial. Syringomatous foci are discerned sometimes in microcystic adnexal carcinoma， an observation that prompts us to question the conventional wisdom that syringoma is really an eccrine and not an apocrine neoplasm.**

【108】**In sum， differentiation of trichoadenoma from microcystic adnexal carcinoma is important because the former is benign， presumably a hamar-toma， whereas the latter is an adenocarcinoma that， left untreated， may have catastrophic consequences for a person who bears it. Criteria listed at the beginning of this chapter allow correct diagnosis and appropriate therapy.**

【165】**RICHOEPITHELIOMA and the infundibulo-cystic type of basal-cell carcinoma have many features in common， including rela-tive symmetry， follicular differentiation， elements of both basaloid and squamoid cells， necrotic keratinocytes， mitotic figures in keratinocytes， cords of cells that interconnect， continuity with the surface epithelium， in-fundibular cyst-like structures， calcification of cystic structures， clefts within the stroma， and sparse infiltrates of inflammatory cells.**

【166】**Despite the many histopathologic similarities between them， trichoepi-thelioma and infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma have different bio-logic potentialities that can be inferred from several contrasting histopatho-logic findings. Trichoepithelioma is associated nearly always with some evidence of follicular differentiation in the manner of follicular germs and papillae at the least， whereas infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma prac-tically never exhibits follicular germs and papillae. Instead， it shows signs of follicular differentiation in the form of follicular germs alone at distal ends of columns and cords of pink neoplastic cells and of tiny infundibular cysts. The stroma in trichoepithelioma nearly always is prominent and consists of bundles of collagen that resemble those of the perifollicular sheath. In con-trast， practically no stroma is associated with an infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma. Last， trichoepithelioma usually is constructed of neoplastic basaloid cells arranged in cribriform pattern， whereas neoplastic squamoid cells of infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma are arraved in an anasto-mosing pattern.**

【167】**At times it may be impossible to distinguish a trichoepithelioma clini-cally from an infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma. Both neoplasms mostly occur as a solitary papule on a face. The papules are somewhat opalescent and do not ulcerate. Once growth of papules has stabilized， they do not enlarge much further. Interestingly， dermatologists are able to recog. nize trichoepitheliomas for what they are in more than 50% of instances， and they nearly always diagnose infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma clinically as basal-cell carcinoma.**

【168】**Trichoepithelioma may present itself as numerous lesions inherited as an autosomal dominant disorder or as a solitary papul e _C_ . Irrespective of _._ whether solitary or numerous， trichoepitheliomas have repeatable histo-pathologic findings. Trichoepitheliomas differentiate along a variety of fol-licular lines， the most common being follicular germs and papillae (limited differentiation)， but signs of outer sheath， inner sheath， and hair (advanced differentiation) are not uncommon. That is not the situation for infun-dibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma， a neoplasm that has limited follicular**
differentiation. At the peripheries of columns and cords of mostly squamoid neoplastic cells are collections of basaloid cells that simulate follicular germs. In early lesions， no infundibular “cysts”are present in this distinctive expression of basal-cell carcinoma； fully developed lesions， however， are marked by numerous tiny infundibular cyst-like structures. That infun-dibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma is truly a basal-cell carcinoma and not a benign adnexal neoplasm， such as a trichoepithelioma， can be determined by several findings： (1) occurrence sometimes in continuity with indubitable nodular types of basal-cell carcinoma， (2) presence often of neoplastic cells in mitosis， (3) nurnerous necrotic neoplastic cells， usually arranged as soli-tary units but often in small collections as necrosis en masse， (4) remarkably scant stroma， (5) occurrence in patients with basal-cell carcinoma nevoid syndrome， and (6) extension deep into the skin and into subcutaneous tis-sues， albeit rarely.

_cDNA Microarrays_ The concept of expression profiling led to the development of robotic methods for arraying thou-sands of cDNAs on microarrays. These cDNA arrays that can be spotted on either nylon filters or glass slides are hybridized with labeled aRNA or cDNA to generate a molecular finger-print of a specific cell type， disease state， or therapeutic efficacy. The highly parallel data acquisition and data analysis on cDNA arrays allows the exact determination of complex|删除0换行|changes in gene expression. Apart from cDNA microarrays， several other methods have been devised to study gene expres-sion on alarge scale：cDNA subtraction，differential display，rep-resentational difference analysis (RDA)， expressed sequence tag(EST) sequencing， serial analysis of gene expression (SAGE)， and differential hybridization on either high-density spotted nylon filters or glass. Profiles of gene expression obtained with all these techniques， however， are reliable and meaningful only， if they can be assigned to morphologically identified pure cell populations. Until recently，the application ofcDNA array tech-niques has been limited to mRNA isolated from millions or， at very best， several thousand cells， thereby restricting the study of small samples and complex tissues. Because the total RNA content of mammalian cells is in the range of 20-40 pg and mRNA accounts for only 1-5% of the cellularRNA， any attempt at single-cell profiling must be capable of dealing with a total of 105-106 mRNA molecules. In lymphomas or soft tissue sarcomas， clonality can be assessed by the identification of associated genetic changes such as clonal rearrangements of the immunoglobulin heavy chain or T-cell receptoror translocations. As in endocrine tumors no such general genetic lesions are known， a more general approach is needed.

【30】**FUTURE ASPECTS**

【31】It is anticipated that with the techniques available at present and the information provided by the completed Human Genome Project， the molecular basis of many endocrine neoplasms will be elucidated in the near future. In consequence， our daily rou-tine work as pathologists may look somewhat different in a few years. It may include the application of new assays on slides or extracted tissues， of additional immunohistochemical and molecular markers， as well as the necessity to use adapted clas-sifications of tumors based on additional criteria derived from molecular studies.

【32】In the meantime we should remain involved in the progress of research by ensuring that only tissues of well characterized tumors of patients with comprehensive follow-up data are in-cluded in ongoing studies to achieve the goal of understanding the molecular aspects of endocrine neoplasms.

【8】**Array Technology**

_cDNA Microarrays_ The concept of expression profiling led to the development of robotic methods for arraying thou-sands of cDNAs on microarrays. These cDNA arrays that can be spotted on either nylon filters or glass slides are hybridized with labeled aRNA or cDNA to generate a molecular finger-print of a specific cell type， disease state， or therapeutic efficacy. The highly parallel data acquisition and data analysis on cDNA arrays allows the exact determination of complex|删除0换行|changes in gene expression. Apart from cDNA microarrays， several other methods have been devised to study gene expres-sion on alarge scale：cDNA subtraction，differential display，rep-resentational difference analysis (RDA)， expressed sequence tag(EST) sequencing， serial analysis of gene expression (SAGE)， and differential hybridization on either high-density spotted nylon filters or glass. Profiles of gene expression obtained with all these techniques， however， are reliable and meaningful only， if they can be assigned to morphologically identified pure cell populations. Until recently，the application ofcDNA array tech-niques has been limited to mRNA isolated from millions or， at very best， several thousand cells， thereby restricting the study of small samples and complex tissues. Because the total RNA content of mammalian cells is in the range of 20-40 pg and mRNA accounts for only 1-5% of the cellularRNA， any attempt at single-cell profiling must be capable of dealing with a total of 105-106 mRNA molecules. Nonamplified RNA from micro-dissected tissue samples has been used as a radioactive probe forcDNA arrays； however， at least 5000-50，000 microdissected cells are required for this type of analysis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[136，137\]</u>.

【12】An array is an orderly arrangement of samples. It provides a medium for matching known and unknown DNA samples based on basepairing rules and automating the process of iden-tifying the unknowns. An array experiment can make use of common assay systems such as microplates or standard blotting membranes，and can be created by hand or make use of robotics to deposit the sample. In general， arrays are described as macro-arrays or microarrays， the difference being the size of the sam-ple spots.Macroarrays contain sample spot sizes of about 300um or larger and can be easily imaged by existing gel and blot scanners. The sample spot sizes in microarrays are typically<200 um in diameter and these arrays usually contain thousands of spots. Microarrays require specialized robotics and imaging equipment that generally are not commercially available as a complete system.

【15】Thus far， expression arrays are mainly applied to research. However， it is anticipated that with the help of automated sys-tems specialized “prognostic”and“therapeutic” arrays will be available in the near future， which will allow for a tailor-made therapy of the affected patient. Recent applications of expres-sion arrays in the research of endocrine neoplasms are listed in Table 10.

_Tissue Microarrays_ Theimplementations of high-through-put genetic technologies， such as oligonucleotide microarrays， generate myriad points of data. The identified potential candi-date genes need to be characterized further and selected using a large number of well-characterized tumors and stringent criteria. Tissue microarrays allow for such high-throughput expression profiling of tumor samples， providing， in addition， information|删除0换行|at the microanatomical level. Different techniques could be applied for identification of specific phenotypic (immunohis-tochemistry and ISH) or genotypic (FISH) alterations， holding strong potential for translational research. Tissue microarrays consisting of 0.6-mm biopsies of paraffin-embedded tissues are well validated and have been used for various clinicopatholog-ical studies.

【17】Tissue microarrays carrying three cores of paraffin-embed-ded tumors per specimen deliver accurate results and allow economic high-throughput processing of cancer specimens and other tissues. This technology has the potential to accelerate translational research and to analyze efficiently tissue expres-sion of genes identified by DNA microarray studies. In addition， multi-cell-line arrays are useful for rapid characterization of the expression profiles of multiple cell lines relevant for cancer research. Both tissue and cell line arrays are powerful tools for the screening of new reagents like hybridization probes and anti-bodies. The standardization of staining procedures and reduc-tion of intraassay variability can also be significantly improved with this technique. Tissue microarrays are useful for estab-lishing large disease-specific tissue collections for future analy-sis of new targets in a particular tumor entity and can be helpful for collaborations between major institutions. The new tissue microarray techniques can be used for various different array designs such as (1) progression arrays containing precursor lesions of cancer and cancer specimens of lesions withincreas-ingaggressiveness； (2) tissue-type comparative arrays contain-ing normal， benign， and malignant specimens from the same tissue type； or (3) cancer arrays containing different subtypes or stages of the same tumor entity.

【18】Clonality Analysis Assessment of clonality is an impor-tant factor in differentiating reactive from neoplastic lesions. In lymphomas or soft tissue sarcomas， clonality can be assessed by the identification of associated genetic changes such as clonal rearrangements of the immunoglobulin heavy chain or T-cell receptoror translocations. As in endocrine tumors no such general genetic lesions are known， a more general approach is needed.

【19】_Principles of Clonality Analysis_ Female cells carry a double amountof X-chromosomal genes. To avoid an increased expression of these genes either the maternally or paternally derived X chromosome is inactivated. This inactivation occurs during embryogenesis by random methylation of one X chro-mosome in each cell 通用删除6(英):<u>\[138，139\]</u>. As this process is stable during subsequentcell divisions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[140\]</u>， normal tissues in adultfemales are cellular mosaics differing in which of the two X chromo-somes is methylated. In contrast， neoplasms derived from a single somatic cell show a uniform pattern of X-chromosome inactivation indicating cellular monoclonality .

【20】Different activities of the X-chromosomal glucose-6-phos-phate dehydrogenase (G6PD)isoenzymes were the first approach to analyze clonality using X-inactivation patterns 通用删除6(英):<u>\[141\]</u>. How-ever， the low frequency of heterozygosity (2%) for the G6PD isoenzymes made this approach impractical. Methylation-sen-sitive restriction enzymes， which selectively cleave nonmethy-lated DNA， allow discrimination between the active (unmethy-lated) and inactive (methylated) X chromosome on DNA level. As this process is stable during subsequentcell divisions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[140\]</u>， normal tissues in adultfemales are cellular mosaics differing in which of the two X chromo-somes is methylated. In contrast， neoplasms derived from a single somatic cell show a uniform pattern of X-chromosome inactivation indicating cellular monoclonality .

【30】**FUTURE ASPECTS**

【31】It is anticipated that with the techniques available at present and the information provided by the completed Human Genome Project， the molecular basis of many endocrine neoplasms will be elucidated in the near future. In consequence， our daily rou-tine work as pathologists may look somewhat different in a few years. It may include the application of new assays on slides or extracted tissues， of additional immunohistochemical and molecular markers， as well as the necessity to use adapted clas-sifications of tumors based on additional criteria derived from molecular studies.

【32】In the meantime we should remain involved in the progress of research by ensuring that only tissues of well characterized tumors of patients with comprehensive follow-up data are in-cluded in ongoing studies to achieve the goal of understanding the molecular aspects of endocrine neoplasms.

This technology has the potential to accelerate translational research and to analyze efficiently tissue expres-sion of genes identified by DNA microarray studies. In addition， multi-cell-line arrays are useful for rapid characterization of the expression profiles of multiple cell lines relevant for cancer research. Both tissue and cell line arrays are powerful tools for the screening of new reagents like hybridization probes and anti-bodies. The standardization of staining procedures and reduc-tion of intraassay variability can also be significantly improved with this technique. Tissue microarrays are useful for estab-lishing large disease-specific tissue collections for future analy-sis of new targets in a particular tumor entity and can be helpful for collaborations between major institutions. The new tissue microarray techniques can be used for various different array designs such as (1) progression arrays containing precursor lesions of cancer and cancer specimens of lesions withincreas-ingaggressiveness； (2) tissue-type comparative arrays contain-ing normal， benign， and malignant specimens from the same tissue type； or (3) cancer arrays containing different subtypes or stages of the same tumor entity.

【18】Clonality Analysis Assessment of clonality is an impor-tant factor in differentiating reactive from neoplastic lesions. In lymphomas or soft tissue sarcomas， clonality can be assessed by the identification of associated genetic changes such as clonal rearrangements of the immunoglobulin heavy chain or T-cell receptoror translocations. As in endocrine tumors no such general genetic lesions are known， a more general approach is needed.

【19】_Principles of Clonality Analysis_ Female cells carry a double amountof X-chromosomal genes. To avoid an increased expression of these genes either the maternally or paternally derived X chromosome is inactivated. This inactivation occurs during embryogenesis by random methylation of one X chro-mosome in each cell 通用删除6(英):<u>\[138，139\]</u>. As this process is stable during subsequentcell divisions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[140\]</u>， normal tissues in adultfemales are cellular mosaics differing in which of the two X chromo-somes is methylated. In contrast， neoplasms derived from a single somatic cell show a uniform pattern of X-chromosome inactivation indicating cellular monoclonality .

【30】**FUTURE ASPECTS**

【31】It is anticipated that with the techniques available at present and the information provided by the completed Human Genome Project， the molecular basis of many endocrine neoplasms will be elucidated in the near future. In consequence， our daily rou-tine work as pathologists may look somewhat different in a few years. It may include the application of new assays on slides or extracted tissues， of additional immunohistochemical and molecular markers， as well as the necessity to use adapted clas-sifications of tumors based on additional criteria derived from molecular studies.

【32】In the meantime we should remain involved in the progress of research by ensuring that only tissues of well characterized tumors of patients with comprehensive follow-up data are in-cluded in ongoing studies to achieve the goal of understanding the molecular aspects of endocrine neoplasms.
