【2】LAURA E.  
HEYNEMAN

【3】HISTORY

【4】A 70-year-old with history of coronary artery disease presenting with chest pain.

【5】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 11-13A Short-axis SSFP MR image reveals a thin inferior left ventricular wall.</u>

【6】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 11-13B Short-axis delayed-enhancement MR image demonstrates transmural enhancement of the inferior wall. The remaining myocardium shows no enhancement.</u>

【7】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【8】 Chronic myocardial infarction: This is the most likely diagnosis given the focal thinning of the LV inferior wall with associated transmural enhancement. The abnormality is in the distribution of the RCA.

【9】 Infectious myocarditis: This is less likely given that focal wall thinning is very unusual in the setting of an infectious (viral) myocarditis. Furthermore, myocarditis usually results in either no myocardial enhancement or extensive enhancement of the epicardial wall; a solitary focus of transmural enhancement would be rare.

【10】 Cardiac amyloid: This infiltrative process usually results in extensive myocardial thickening rather than focal thinning. On delayed-enhancement sequences, amyloid may cause diffuse, circumferential subendo-cardial enhancement that progresses with the course of the disease to diffuse transmural enhancement. A solitary region of enhancement would be highly unusual.

【11】 Cardiac sarcoid: While sarcoidosis can cause focal wall thinning, there are usually multiple sites of deposition of the sarcoid granulomata; this frequently results in multifocal enhancement on delayed-enhancement imaging. Furthermore, at least one site of the enhancement usually demonstrates a nonischemic pattern of enhancement: either midmyocardial or epicardial. The presence of a single focus of transmural enhancement as evidenced in this case would be unusual for sarcoid.

【12】DIAGNOSIS

【13】Chronic myocardial infarction

【14】KEY FACTS

【15】Clinical

【16】 Pathophysiology: In the setting of acute myocardial infarction, there is a sudden loss of integrity of myocyte cell membranes. The ventricular wall remains normal in size, or occasionally is slightly thickened by edema. In chronic myocardial infarction, myocytes are replaced by fibrous tissue. This myocyte replacement by fibrosis often results in thinning of the ventricular wall.

【17】 Myocyte injury from myocardial infarction always begins at the subendocardium and then extends to a variable degree through the myocardium and epicardium of the adjacent wall. Therefore, a small infarction that was reperfused quickly may only cause death within the subendocardial layer of myocardium. A large infarct may be transmural.

【18】 Treatment: Patients with either acute or chronic myo-cardial infarction in which scar involves >50% of the wall thickness  are unlikely to show improvement in wall function after revascularization. In such patients, emphasis is placed on medical therapy.

【19】Radiologic

【20】 The LV wall is mapped to different coronary artery territories. In general, the LAD artery serves the anterior wall and anteroseptal walls; the LCx artery serves the lateral wall, and the RCA serves the inferolateral, inferior, and inferoseptal walls.

【21】 Cine MR:

【22】>  Wall function provides indirect evidence of the status of the supplying coronary artery since normal wall function requires normal myocardial perfusion. Therefore, patients who have had a myocar-dial infarction may show a wall motion abnormality that involves the portion of the left ventricle that was supplied by the affected artery. However, very small infarcts involving only a tiny amount of the subendocardium usually do not result in a wall function abnormality.

【23】>  Wall thickness can provide clues to the chronicity of the process. The wall thickness may be normal in the setting of both acute and chronic infarctions, but wall thinning is usually indicative of chronic infarction.

【24】 Delayed-enhancement MR findings:

【25】>  Delayed-enhancement imaging is performed approximately 5 to15 minutes after intravenous gadolinium administration. Images are obtained so as to null normal myocardial signal. Therefore, in this sequence, normal myocardium is uniformly black in signal. Fibrosis and scar enhance.

【26】>  Both acute and chronic infarcts result in delayed enhancement on delayed-enhancement (also known as “viability”) sequences. Acute infarcts enhance due to the loss of integrity of the cell membranes which, in turn, allow gadolinium to accumulate within the intracellular space. Chronic infarcts enhance due to the large amount of extracellular space within fibrotic tissue.

【27】>  All myocardial infarctions result in subendocardial enhancement. As the infarction progresses, more of the thickness of the wall is affected, resulting in a greater amount of transmural enhancement on delayed-enhancement imaging.

【28】>  Ventricular enhancement that spares the subendo-cardium (i.e. enhancement confined to the midmyo-cardium or epicardium) is indicative of a nonischemic process. Infectious myocarditis and cardiac sarcoid are examples of inflammatory processes that demonstrate a nonischemic pattern of enhancement on delayed-enhancement MR. Cardiac amyloidosis tends to cause diffuse, circumferential subendocar-dial enhancement; the global involvement indicates that the pathology is not a result of CAD.

【33】CASE 14

【34】CHRISTOPHER J.  
ROTH

【35】HISTORY

【36】A 17-year-old male with no significant past medical history collapsed during a basketball game and required cardiac life support measures for resuscitation.

【37】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURES 11-14A-11-14D SSFP three-chamber view in diastole (A) and peak systole (B), and four-chamber view (C) demonstrate marked LV wall hypertrophy with outflow tract obstruction. A jet of turbulent flow is identified in the LV outflow tract on the peak systolic image (B). Hypertrophy preferentially involves the basal septum on the four-chamber view (C). Contrast-enhanced inversion recovery three chamber MR image demonstrates patchy, midwall enhancement in the region of septal hypertrophy (D) .</u>

【38】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【39】 Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM): The presence of asymmetric septal wall thickening, a turbulent jet of blood in the subvalvular LV outflow tract, and patchy midmyocardial septal enhancement on the delayed-enhancement image make this the most likely cause of the patient’s cardiac arrest.

【40】 Aortic stenosis (AS): The presence of asymmetric septal hypertrophy would be unusual in the setting of AS, which most often would result in concentric hypertrophy. Additionally, the jet of turbulent flow during systole would originate from the level of the aortic valve rather than the subvalvular level, as seen in this case.

【41】 Amyloidosis: Cardiac amyloidosis generally results in global hypertrophy and extensive subendocardial enhancement rather than the asymmetric hypertrophy and midmyocardial focal enhancement as seen in this case.

【42】 Sarcoidosis: Cardiac sarcoidosis does not usually result in the severe myocardial hypertrophy as seen in this case. While delayed enhancement in sarcoidosis may be midmyocardial in location, it may also be epicardial or transmural.

【43】 Fabry’s disease: Fabry’s disease is a rare X-linked metabolic storage disorder with cardiac manifestations that include concentric LV wall thickening and midmyocardial enhancement involving the basal inferolateral wall.

【44】DIAGNOSIS

【45】Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM)

【46】KEY FACTS

【47】Clinical

【48】 Histologically, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by disarrayed ventricular myocyte organization, manifesting in ventricular hypertrophy.

【49】 HCM may demonstrate concentric or asymmetric ventricular hypertrophy. In the Western hemisphere, in patients with asymmetric hypertrophy, the ventricular septum is preferentially involved; less commonly, asymmetric hypertrophy involves the LV apex or right ventricle.

【50】 HCM can be subdivided into obstructive and nonobstructive physiologies. The obstruction is at the level of the LV outflow tract. Patients with asymmetric HCM involving the septum are at increased risk for obstructive physiology.

【51】 In the obstructive subtype of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HOCM)—previously referred to as idiopathic hypertrophic aortic stenosis (IHSS)—there is systolic LV outflow tract stenosis as a result of the asymmetric ventricular hypertrophy superimposed on an abnormal motion of the mitral valve in which the anterior leaflet shifts anteriorly and toward the septum during systole (SAM, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve).

【52】 Patients with either the obstructive or nonobstructive variety of HCM are at risk of sudden death due to arrhythmogenic foci within the regions of ventricular hypertrophy.

Midmyocardial enhancement at the junction of the interventricular septal junction and the anterior ventricular free wall is also common. The foci of enhancement represent regions of fibrosis and scar tissue that, in turn, are thought to act as arrhythmogenic foci.

However, on steady-state free precession (SSFP) MR, the turbulent flow jet would extend from the aortic valve into the left ventricle during diastole, a finding that is not seen in this case. Furthermore, a tangential view of the aortic valve in patients with aortic regurgitation would demonstrate lack of coaptation of the aortic valve leaflets during diastole.

【78】 Cystic medial necrosis: This can result in dilation of the ascending aorta, but generally results in dilation of the aortic root and sinuses of Valsalva as well as the tubular portion of the ascending aorta. The result is a “tulip bulb” shape of the ascending aorta. Cystic medial necrosis is often associated with aortic insufficiency as well as aortic dissection.

This would spare the sinuses of Valsalva and involve only the tubular portion of the aorta. However, this would not explain the thickening of the aortic valve, the flow jet through the aortic valve, or the fused valvular commissures.

Furthermore, diastolic flow into the coronary arteries begins to decrease, causing angina pectoris.

【100】>  Phase contrast MR imaging can be used to calculate the transvalvular gradient, which, in turn, can help classify severity of stenosis. 【3】HISTORY

【4】A 70-year-old with history of coronary artery disease presenting with chest pain.

【5】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 11-13A Short-axis SSFP MR image reveals a thin inferior left ventricular wall.</u>

【6】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 11-13B Short-axis delayed-enhancement MR image demonstrates transmural enhancement of the inferior wall. The remaining myocardium shows no enhancement.</u>

【7】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【8】 Chronic myocardial infarction: This is the most likely diagnosis given the focal thinning of the LV inferior wall with associated transmural enhancement. The abnormality is in the distribution of the RCA.

【9】 Infectious myocarditis: This is less likely given that focal wall thinning is very unusual in the setting of an infectious (viral) myocarditis. Furthermore, myocarditis usually results in either no myocardial enhancement or extensive enhancement of the epicardial wall; a solitary focus of transmural enhancement would be rare.

【10】 Cardiac amyloid: This infiltrative process usually results in extensive myocardial thickening rather than focal thinning. On delayed-enhancement sequences, amyloid may cause diffuse, circumferential subendo-cardial enhancement that progresses with the course of the disease to diffuse transmural enhancement. A solitary region of enhancement would be highly unusual.

【11】 Cardiac sarcoid: While sarcoidosis can cause focal wall thinning, there are usually multiple sites of deposition of the sarcoid granulomata; this frequently results in multifocal enhancement on delayed-enhancement imaging. Furthermore, at least one site of the enhancement usually demonstrates a nonischemic pattern of enhancement: either midmyocardial or epicardial. The presence of a single focus of transmural enhancement as evidenced in this case would be unusual for sarcoid.

【12】DIAGNOSIS

【13】Chronic myocardial infarction

【14】KEY FACTS

【15】Clinical

【16】 Pathophysiology: In the setting of acute myocardial infarction, there is a sudden loss of integrity of myocyte cell membranes. The ventricular wall remains normal in size, or occasionally is slightly thickened by edema. In chronic myocardial infarction, myocytes are replaced by fibrous tissue. This myocyte replacement by fibrosis often results in thinning of the ventricular wall.

【17】 Myocyte injury from myocardial infarction always begins at the subendocardium and then extends to a variable degree through the myocardium and epicardium of the adjacent wall. Therefore, a small infarction that was reperfused quickly may only cause death within the subendocardial layer of myocardium. A large infarct may be transmural.

【18】 Treatment: Patients with either acute or chronic myo-cardial infarction in which scar involves >50% of the wall thickness  are unlikely to show improvement in wall function after revascularization. In such patients, emphasis is placed on medical therapy.

【19】Radiologic

【20】 The LV wall is mapped to different coronary artery territories. In general, the LAD artery serves the anterior wall and anteroseptal walls; the LCx artery serves the lateral wall, and the RCA serves the inferolateral, inferior, and inferoseptal walls.

【21】 Cine MR:

【22】>  Wall function provides indirect evidence of the status of the supplying coronary artery since normal wall function requires normal myocardial perfusion. Therefore, patients who have had a myocar-dial infarction may show a wall motion abnormality that involves the portion of the left ventricle that was supplied by the affected artery. However, very small infarcts involving only a tiny amount of the subendocardium usually do not result in a wall function abnormality.

【23】>  Wall thickness can provide clues to the chronicity of the process. The wall thickness may be normal in the setting of both acute and chronic infarctions, but wall thinning is usually indicative of chronic infarction.

【24】 Delayed-enhancement MR findings:

【25】>  Delayed-enhancement imaging is performed approximately 5 to15 minutes after intravenous gadolinium administration. Images are obtained so as to null normal myocardial signal. Therefore, in this sequence, normal myocardium is uniformly black in signal. Fibrosis and scar enhance.

【26】>  Both acute and chronic infarcts result in delayed enhancement on delayed-enhancement (also known as “viability”) sequences. Acute infarcts enhance due to the loss of integrity of the cell membranes which, in turn, allow gadolinium to accumulate within the intracellular space. Chronic infarcts enhance due to the large amount of extracellular space within fibrotic tissue.

【27】>  All myocardial infarctions result in subendocardial enhancement. As the infarction progresses, more of the thickness of the wall is affected, resulting in a greater amount of transmural enhancement on delayed-enhancement imaging.

【28】>  Ventricular enhancement that spares the subendo-cardium (i.e. enhancement confined to the midmyo-cardium or epicardium) is indicative of a nonischemic process. Infectious myocarditis and cardiac sarcoid are examples of inflammatory processes that demonstrate a nonischemic pattern of enhancement on delayed-enhancement MR. Cardiac amyloidosis tends to cause diffuse, circumferential subendocar-dial enhancement; the global involvement indicates that the pathology is not a result of CAD.

Finally， osteofibrous dys-plasia should be differentiated from adamantinoma(139). The latter lesion is usually more extensive， with a more aggressive appearance. A helpful hint is that patients with adamantinoma are much older than those with osteofibrous dysplasia.

【1】**Pathology**

【2】The main differential diagnoses include fibrous dyspla- _sia and adamantinoma. Fibrous dysplasia shows the char-_ acteristic absence of osteoblasts at the surface of trabec-ulae， whereas osteofibrous dysplasia exhibits dressed trabeculae. Adamantinoma is distinguished from osteofi-brous dysplasia by the presence of single or small nests of epithelial cells within the fibroosseous stroma(14l). More problems are encountered in distinguish-ing osteofibrous dysplasia from so-called osteofibrous _dysplasia-like adamantinoma (149). From a practical_ standpoint， a diagnosis of osteofibrous dysplasia made on tissue removed by a small incisional biopsy cannot be certain because the biopsy material may not be rep-resentative of the entire lesion. One cannot rule out an osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma， which， ac-cording to the WHO， is characterized by isolated or small groups of epithelial cells intermingled with stro-mal cells (149，153). In such cases， immunohistochemi-cal staining for markers of epithelial cells， especially cytokeratins， can be helpful.

【3】Radiologic and pathologic differential diagnosis of osteofibrous dysplasia is depicted in Figure 4-53.

【4】**Desmoplastic Fibroma**

【5】Originally described by Jaffe in 1958， desmoplastic fi-broma， also known as desmoid tumor of bone， is a rare， locally aggressive lesion， closely related to the

【9】desmoid tumor of abdominal wall， characterized by the formation of abundant collagen fibers by the tu-mor cells (19，45，160，167). Although generally classi-fied as a benign bone tumor， some investigators clas-sify this lesion in a so-called intermediate category between benign and malignant lesions (29). As in ex-traosseous desmoid-type fibromatosis and in extraab-dominal (aggressive) fibromatosis， trisomies 8 and 20have been observed in desmoplastic fibroma of bone； however， thus far their significance i not clear(160，163).

【10】**_Clinical Presentation_**

【11】Desmoplastic fibroma accounted for only about 0.06%of all bone tumors and 0.3% of benign bone tumors in the Mayo Clinic series (8). It usually arises in individuals younger than 40 years； half of the cases occur during the second decade (8). There is no sex predominance. The clinical signs and symptoms are nonspe-cific (157). Because the onset is often insidious， the lesion tends to be relatively large before the patient be-gins to experience symptoms (108). In symptomatic pa-tients， pain or swelling， sometimes of long duration， is the most common complaint (162). Rarely (in about10% of cases)， a pathologic fracture through the lesion

A： Plump， irregular bone trabeculae scattered in a moder-ate-density spindle cell stroma are made up in part of a cell-rich woven bone， but at the periphery display lamellar bone rimmed by osteoblasts (hematoxylin and eosin， origi-nal magnification ×25). B： Viewed under polarized light， lamellar (light green) and woven (darker areas) bone is more clearly discernible (polarized light， original magnifica-tion ×25). C： Under higher magnification osteoblastic rim-ming of the bone trabeculae is clearly visible (hematoxylin and eosin， original magnification ×200).</u>

【14】is the first presenting symptom (172). The long bones(humerus， femur， tibia)， mandible， and pelvis are the most common sites of involvement (171). In the long bones the lesion is diaphyseal， sparing the epiphysis， but it often extends into the metaphysis and may even ex-tend into the articular end of the bone after closure of the growth plate (174).

【15】**_Imaging_**

【16】There are no characteristic radiographic features of desmoplastic fibroma. The spectrum of radiologic fea-tures of this tumor overlap the radiographic patterns described for low-grade central osteosarcoma and， in some cases， fibrous dysplasia (161). In general， it is an expansive， radiolucent lesion， usually with nonscle-rotic but sharply defined borders . Occa-sionally a wide zone of transition is present (169). The cortex is either thinned or thickened， but there is no significant periosteal response (159) . In-ternal septation or trabeculation is observed in ap-proximately 75% of cases， yielding a honeycomb pat-tern of bone destruction (164) . Locally aggressive variants， which may simulate malignant bone tumors， are marked by bone destruction and invasion of the soft tissues.

Finally， osteofibrous dys-plasia should be differentiated from adamantinoma(139). The latter lesion is usually more extensive， with a more aggressive appearance. A helpful hint is that patients with adamantinoma are much older than those with osteofibrous dysplasia.

【1】**Pathology**

【2】The main differential diagnoses include fibrous dyspla- _sia and adamantinoma. Fibrous dysplasia shows the char-_ acteristic absence of osteoblasts at the surface of trabec-ulae， whereas osteofibrous dysplasia exhibits dressed trabeculae. Adamantinoma is distinguished from osteofi-brous dysplasia by the presence of single or small nests of epithelial cells within the fibroosseous stroma(14l). More problems are encountered in distinguish-ing osteofibrous dysplasia from so-called osteofibrous _dysplasia-like adamantinoma (149). From a practical_ standpoint， a diagnosis of osteofibrous dysplasia made on tissue removed by a small incisional biopsy cannot be certain because the biopsy material may not be rep-resentative of the entire lesion. One cannot rule out an osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma， which， ac-cording to the WHO， is characterized by isolated or small groups of epithelial cells intermingled with stro-mal cells (149，153). In such cases， immunohistochemi-cal staining for markers of epithelial cells， especially cytokeratins， can be helpful.

Although generally classi-fied as a benign bone tumor， some investigators clas-sify this lesion in a so-called intermediate category between benign and malignant lesions (29). As in ex-traosseous desmoid-type fibromatosis and in extraab-dominal (aggressive) fibromatosis， trisomies 8 and 20have been observed in desmoplastic fibroma of bone； however， thus far their significance i not clear(160，163).

【10】**_Clinical Presentation_**

【11】Desmoplastic fibroma accounted for only about 0.06%of all bone tumors and 0.3% of benign bone tumors in the Mayo Clinic series (8). It usually arises in individuals younger than 40 years； half of the cases occur during the second decade (8). There is no sex predominance. The clinical signs and symptoms are nonspe-cific (157). Because the onset is often insidious， the lesion tends to be relatively large before the patient be-gins to experience symptoms (108). In symptomatic pa-tients， pain or swelling， sometimes of long duration， is the most common complaint (162). Rarely (in about10% of cases)， a pathologic fracture through the lesion

In the long bones the lesion is diaphyseal， sparing the epiphysis， but it often extends into the metaphysis and may even ex-tend into the articular end of the bone after closure of the growth plate (174).

【15】**_Imaging_**

【16】There are no characteristic radiographic features of desmoplastic fibroma. The spectrum of radiologic fea-tures of this tumor overlap the radiographic patterns described for low-grade central osteosarcoma and， in some cases， fibrous dysplasia (161). In general， it is an expansive， radiolucent lesion， usually with nonscle-rotic but sharply defined borders . Occa-sionally a wide zone of transition is present (169). The cortex is either thinned or thickened， but there is no significant periosteal response (159) . In-ternal septation or trabeculation is observed in ap-proximately 75% of cases， yielding a honeycomb pat-tern of bone destruction (164) . Locally aggressive variants， which may simulate malignant bone tumors， are marked by bone destruction and invasion of the soft tissues.

Although generally classi-fied as a benign bone tumor， some investigators clas-sify this lesion in a so-called intermediate category between benign and malignant lesions (29). As in ex-traosseous desmoid-type fibromatosis and in extraab-dominal (aggressive) fibromatosis， trisomies 8 and 20have been observed in desmoplastic fibroma of bone； however， thus far their significance i not clear(160，163).

【10】**_Clinical Presentation_**

【11】Desmoplastic fibroma accounted for only about 0.06%of all bone tumors and 0.3% of benign bone tumors in the Mayo Clinic series (8). It usually arises in individuals younger than 40 years； half of the cases occur during the second decade (8). There is no sex predominance. The clinical signs and symptoms are nonspe-cific (157). Because the onset is often insidious， the lesion tends to be relatively large before the patient be-gins to experience symptoms (108). In symptomatic pa-tients， pain or swelling， sometimes of long duration， is the most common complaint (162). Rarely (in about10% of cases)， a pathologic fracture through the lesion

In the long bones the lesion is diaphyseal， sparing the epiphysis， but it often extends into the metaphysis and may even ex-tend into the articular end of the bone after closure of the growth plate (174).

【15】**_Imaging_**

【16】There are no characteristic radiographic features of desmoplastic fibroma. The spectrum of radiologic fea-tures of this tumor overlap the radiographic patterns described for low-grade central osteosarcoma and， in some cases， fibrous dysplasia (161). In general， it is an expansive， radiolucent lesion， usually with nonscle-rotic but sharply defined borders . Occa-sionally a wide zone of transition is present (169). The cortex is either thinned or thickened， but there is no significant periosteal response (159) . In-ternal septation or trabeculation is observed in ap-proximately 75% of cases， yielding a honeycomb pat-tern of bone destruction (164) . Locally aggressive variants， which may simulate malignant bone tumors， are marked by bone destruction and invasion of the soft tissues.

【12】**Referral Information**

【13】The 10th-grade high school science and homeroom teacher has referred Lucy Johnson to you due to frequent school absenteeism， falling grades， and withdrawn behavior. Lucy is 15 years old and usu-ally an A student. After several attempts to reach her mother by phone， you decide to make a home visit.

【14】**Home Visit**

【15】Lucy lives in a rural area approximately 10 miles outside a small town in Virginia. Her mother， Judy， works a rotating shift at a hosiery factory in town. Judy is a single mother with three daughters ages12， 15， and 17. When you arrive in the vicinity of her house， you discover she lives in a run-down trailer park without numbers to identify the resi-dences. You stop at the first trailer and ask where Ms. Johnson lives. The woman tells you the trailer is at the end of the road. As you drive up to the Johnson trailer， you see Lucy sitting on the steps with her head in her hands.

【16】She looks up and waves when you get out of the car. She seems surprised to see you there. She walks over to your car and asks you why you’re at her house. “You’ve missed a lot of school lately， and Ms. James has been worried about you，"you reply.“Can we talk somewhere?”

【17】“My mother is busy inside right now， but we can walk down the road if you like，” Lucy suggests. She begins walking down the road， and you follow her.

【18】“Why have you missed so much school?” you ask her.

【19】Lucy tells you that her mother’s car has been in the shop and she didn’t want to take the bus with the little kids. Her boyfriend， Joe， has been taking her to school on days when he doesn’t have to be at work early. Lucy looks very unhappy and tired.

【20】You ask her if there are other things going on that she'd like to talk about. She shakes her head and says she'll be at school the next day.

【21】You tell Lucy that she can come by your office anytime if she wants to talk. She glances at you and sayyss。“All right， just not now.”

【22】You ask her if you can visit with her mother now， and Lucy quickly and emphatically tells you that her mother really can’t be disturbed.“Please don’t go into the trailer right now. I’ll tell her you came by and give her your phone number. Okay?”

【23】“Are you sure everything is all right， Lucy?”you implore.

【24】“Yes， everything is fine. My mother just can’t be disturbed right now. She'll call you，” Lucy says with a look of determination in her eyes.

【25】Because Lucy seems so concerned about you in-truding， you agree to leave and talk to her mother later.

【26】The following day， you check and find Lucy is at school as she said she would be. You try calling her mother at home， and once again， there is no answer. At lunch， Ms. James tells you that Lucy seems somewhat despondent but has made it to all her classes that morning.

【27】**Interview with Lucy**

【28】About a week later， as you’re getting ready to leave for the day， you notice Lucy standing in the hall-way outside your office. You ask her if she’d like to come in for a few minutes and talk.

【29】Lucy walks into your office， and as you close the door， she bursts into tears. You guide her to a chair where she slumps down and continues to sob. You sit down opposite her and give her some time to calm down.

【30】After crying hard for a few minutes， Lucy looks at you and says she doesn’t know why she's so upset.“I’m just so very sad these days. I don’t feel like doing anything except sleeping or crying. I've been crying for 3 days and can’t seem to stop." She looks around the room for a tissue as she continues to apologize for getting upset.

【31】“What do you think all those tears are about?”you ask.

【32】“I’m really not sure. It seems ridiculous to me， but I just can’t stop，”Lucy sobs.

【33】“Maybe you could tell me a little about what’s been going on with you lately， and we can figure it out together，” you suggest.

【1】**On a global level， the impairment corresponded with an MCI； however there were already some impairments iIADL. Verbal memory performance clearly verified a consolidation deficit concerning learning， delayed recall and recognition performance . Visuospatial memory of the CERAD-NAB was also impaired. Moreover， the patient had clear problems with PAL and the patient showed an increase number of false positives in the picture recognition testing. The diagnosis was an MCI at the margin of a dementia with the possible cause of AD. The results of the cere-brospinal puncture endorsed this suggestion， because total tau and phosphor tau were in an abnormal range. A medication with an acetylcholine esterase inhibitor was started.**

The samepatient came back for a control investigation 15 months later. He was still leading a very active lifestyle. This time we performed the MMSE and the score wasnow _V_ 22\. Memory performance was somewhat|删除0换行|improved for verbal memory， however， decreased for visuospatial memory. Time for the TMT-A was almost identical (85 seconds)， but the patient was meanwhile unable to do the TMT-B in 5 minutes. Recognition errors were still highly increased and on a clinical level the word findings problems were more evident than during the first visit.**

【3】**Obviously the combination of active training and taking the acetylcholine esterase inhibitor prevented cognitive decline in most of the measured domains. We will come back to the prospects of treating AD patients with such a combination in the last sections of this chapter.**

【4】**2.7Summary of neuropsychological testing in patients suspected for Alzheimer’s disease**

【5】**In summary， it can be stated that neuropsychological testing is able to distin-guish between typical AD patients and healthy controls rather well， but the differentiation between different neurodegenerative diseases leading to mem-ory impairments poses considerable problems. Consolidation of information is highly impaired in AD patients and should be used to separate AD patients from patients with unknown causes of cognitive impairment. Still， even com-posite scores for verbal learning， recall and recognition， or verbal and visuo-constructive recall suffer from the fact that they are affected by the stage of disease progression. They differ from CSF biomarkers in this respect. The probability for diagnosing AD increases in patients with consolidation deficits if they show normal phonological word fluency， impaired semantic word fluency and have anaverage digit span percentile above _3_ 30\. Neuropsychiatric changes of AD encompass higher apathy， increased anxiety and dependence， but not depressive mood. Despite these distinctive symp-toms of AD， neuropsychological assessment still looks for cutoff scores that do not depend on the global impairment to enhance the probability of their differential diagnosis.**

【6】**Neuropsychological assessment of patients suspected to suffer from (pre-clinical) AD should additionally rely on a measurement of false positives in a PRT. Patients with AD display an increased number of false positives. They also tend to have a lower primacy proportion than recency proportion when analyzing the wordlist serial position effect. Paired associate learning is highly sensitive for memory impairments very early in the disease progres-sion. However， impairments in PAL are also common in other neurodegener-ative diseases， if the patients start to progress. Thus an impairment in PAL does not seem to be specific feature of AD but a global measurement of the severity of the memory decline.**

**Arguing that there are no single tests or combination of test results that allow for an accurate clinical diagnosis， does not mean that the clini-cal investigation is invalid. It means that the combined information from|删除0换行|the different aspects of the assessment must guide the decision for the correct diagnosis.**

【8】**2.8 Prediction of conversion to Alzheimer's disease by neuropsychological tests**

【9】**2.8.1 Prediction using the WMS logical memory test and the ADNI neuropsychological mild cognitive impairment criteria**

【10】**The case presented earlier highlights another problem regarding the assess-ment of neurodegenerative diseases： the question of the prognosis. In many patients， only another future assessment will deliver the correct diagnosis. On the other hand， the main interest of the patients is to obtain information immediately about how their problems might develop in the future. Will they progress to a state of dementia or not? This question can be reframed in clinical terms as predicting whether the patient’s state will convert from MCI to dementia and， in the case of typical AD， from amnestic MCI to AD.**

【11】**One of the earliest studies， with a large number of patients from two dif-ferent study centers (the Mayo Clinic and the Karolinska Institute)， showed an increased risk for MCI patients to concert to dementia， depending on the number of cognitive domains being affected 删除1:<u>(Arnaiz et al.， 2004)</u>： about 40%of the patients with impairment in memory performance converted to demen-tia after 5 years， however， this number rose to more than 50% when the patient was impaired in more than one neuropsychological test).**

【12】**Taken together， these results suggest a conversion rate of about 7%-8%per year for pure amnestic MCI patients and 12% for multidomain impaired patients. It should be kept in mind that all these patients came to the hospital because they or their relatives noted cognitive decline， and that other causes for that experienced decline were excluded through an extended neurological examination. Thus the results cannot be easily generalized to population samples that do not possess an urgent enough sense of cognitive decline that causes them to get in contact with a diagnostic unit.**

**Over the past 15 years， the ADNI research group， a very large Northern America-based research network， was able to include a large number of par-ticipants in their data set. They were categorized into those with and without amnestic MCI according to the result of the logical memory test of the WMS IV (being impaired corresponded with a score smaller than-1.5SD). Patients who were impaired in other tests， but not in the logical memory test， were categorized as having a nonamnestic MCI. Storandt and Morris (2010) analyzed the predictive value of the logical memory test in a longitudinal project including healthy controls. The brains of all subjects were analyzed postmortem to determine whether they had developed Alzheimer’s dementia(or not) to provide a definitive diagnosis. The predictive value of the logical memory test was low， and specificity and sensitivity ranged from 55% to|删除0换行|50%. Other neuropsychological tests， like visual associate learning from the WMS and Block design， showed a higher specificity (above 80%) but a low sensitivity (between 30% and 40%).

【14】**Bondi et al. (2014) also used the logical memory test of the WMS and the data of participants from the ADNI project to analyze the predictive power of this test. As mentioned previously， a score less than -1.5SD is the hallmark of amnestic MCI for the ADNI diagnosis. After about 4years， 35.8% of the pure amnestic MCI patients converted to dementia，61.7% remained stable and 4.2% reversed to a normal score. Fifty-seven percentage of the patients with more than one impairment converted to dementia and only 1% reversed. Additionally there was a group of unim-paired participants and 9.3% of them converted to dementia. Bondi et al.(2014) compared these percentages with a categorization based on two measures for each cognitive domain tested. With respect to memory， this was done by adding the performance in the auditory verbal learning test(which includes learning trials and a recognition measure) with the text reproduction of the WMS. The classification based on two measures per-formed better than that based on the text reproduction alone： 46.5% of the patients with amnestic MCI converted to dementia and none of these patients reverted to an unimpaired state. In the case of being impaired in more than one cognitive domain (being impaired in both memory tests and in one other test)， the conversion rate was even higher： 60% of these patients converted to dementia within the following 7 years. These num-bers are very similar to results from the Mayo Clinic and the Karolinska Institute mentioned earlier 删除1:<u>(Arnaiz et al.， 2004)</u>. The study by Bondi et al.(2014) also compared the predictive power of the auditory verbal learning test alone with that of text reproduction alone. The auditory verbal learn-ing test was better in predicting the conversion. One may conclude that a“one-shot presentation”of verbal information， as is the case in the text reproduction test of the WMS IV， is suboptimal for diagnosing MCI. Memory measures based on several learning trials and those that include recognition elements yielded better results for making predictions regard-ing the fate of the patients.**

【15】**2.8.2 Prediction using the CERAD-NAB or standard neuropsychological tests**

In a systematic review， Belleville et al. (2017) found that immediate and delayed free recall of different verbal learning tests are the most sensitive and specific tests for predicting the conversion of patients with MCI to Alzheimer’s dementia. Depending on the study， the sensitivity was about75% and the specificity was often around 80% (or even higher). Visuospatial memory tests assessing free recall were slightly less accurate than verbal memory tests in predicting the conversion to dementia. Other|删除0换行|neuropsychological tests showed a lower sensitivity， but sometimes a similar specificity. The sensitivity of word fluency， for example， increased relative to the number of years between the assessment and the clinical diagnosis of dementia. Furthermore a low Boston Naming Test result predicted a fast pro-gression. According to the review， immediate and delayed verbal free recalls are the best variables for prediction， whereas verbal recognition and cued recall measures do not improve their sensitivity and specificity. In this respect， it is important to mention that a differential diagnosis was not the focus of the studies reviewed here. Instead， the focus was only on making predictions for patients not showing any signs of other neurodegenerative diseases than AD. Studies utilizing the CERAD-NAB were not included in the review by Belleville et al. (2017). Cerami et al. (2017) reviewed two studies with a large number of patients who used the CERAD-NAB. Both showed an accuracy of at least 90%.**

【17】**Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) followed up 357 patients， who were at least75 years old， with MCI (assessed with the CERAD-NAB) for a period of3 years. Overall 41.5% of the patients had a remission of symptoms with normal cognitive function 1.5 and 3 years later， 21.3% showed a fluctuating course， 14.8% had stable symptoms， and 22.4% progressed to dementia. This study is important because it allows patients with MCI to be informed that they have a 78% chance to recover or remain stable over 3 years. On the other hand， 22.4% showed additional decline which is a rate of 7.5 per year. When compared with the single-domain nonamnestic subtype， patients with multidomain amnestic MCI had a three times greater risk of developing a more severe course of MCI. This was followed by patients with multidomain nonamnestic MCI， whose risk was two timesSgreater. Patients with the single-domain amnestic subtype did not have a significantly elevated risk. Patients were at a higher risk of advancing from one course to the next along this spectrum if they had symptoms of depression， impairment in more than one cognitive domain， more severe cognitive impairment， or were older. The result of a test regarding the ability to learn and reproduce new material after a 10-minute period was the best indicator for differentiating between remit-tent and progressive MCI at baseline. Symptoms of depression modified the prognosis.**

**The total number of recalled words during wordlist learning was the most sensitive parameter for predicting deterioration. Among patients who learned less than 15 words， almost 50% performed worse 3 years later. Since the risk for the other groups was low or related to noncognitive factors such as depression， the result of this study is very helpful to inform patients about their prognosis. Cognitive impairments of 50% of patients who learn more than 14 words will improve/be reversed after 3 years. Furthermore these patients showed a risk of MCI progression that is as low as the general popu-lation (less than 3% per year). Conversely 50% of patients who learn less than 15 words are expected to progress from MCI to dementia over the same|删除0换行|amount of time. Bear in mind， however， that the patients were at least 75years old.**

【19】**The study by Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) has a high clinical meaning as it was designed and conducted in assetting in which many patients are assessed for dementia， that is， visiting a geriatric unit due to cognitive impairment. Therefore the cutoff scores published by Kaduszkiewicz et al.(2014) can be used when discussing assessment results with the patients. However， it is unclear whether the results can also be generalized to patients visiting a neurology unit since these patients often suffer from additional gait or other movement disorders and may， therefore， differ from geriatric patients.**

【20】Nonetheless， special concern should be given to the group that learned less than 15 words during the CERAD-NAB. These individuals should be informed about the necessary lifestyle modifications that may reduce their risk. Furthermore their performance should be reevaluated on a yearly basis so that medication， if needed， can be started as early as possible.

【21】**The result of the study by Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) differs from other studies because Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) argue that wordlist learning， and not delayed recall， is the most meaningful parameter. Furthermore they included patients with MCI， whereas other studies， reviewed in more detail later， focused on cognitively unimpaired patients at baseline. The study by Mistridis， Krumm， Monsch， Berres， and Taylor (2015) showed that wordlist learning starts to differ between participants without cognitive impairment and those who will fulfill the criteria of a MCI diagnosis 4 years before the diagnosis can be made， whereas delayed recall already differs between these groups 8 years earlier. One explanation might be that wordlist learning does not show floor effects like delayed recall and may therefore allow a better discrimination in patients already presenting impairments.**

【22】**2.8.3 How early can cognitive impairments be measured in patients converting to dementia?**

**How early can we detect cognitive differences between participants that develop dementia and participants who do not develop the disease? This question can be studied only in longitudinal studies which include normal healthy participants or participants who express another nonbrain disease， which increases the risk of developing dementia. Cervilla， Prince， Joels， Lovestone， and Mann (2004) followed a group of patients with hypertension over a time period of 12 years and used various cognitive tests to assess their cognitive functioning at inclusion and during the following years. Forty-one of the analyzed group of 387 patients developed dementia. Patients who developed dementia significantly differed from patients who did not develop dementia with regard to neuropsychological test results. Furthermore these differences were already detectable 12 years prior to dementia onset. The|删除0换行|highest difference between the groups was found in the trail making test A， while the lowest difference was in the PAL task. When the focus was only on patients with a clinically based diagnosis of AD， performance in the PAL task increased as a relevant test marker. With the same focus， the difference in the TMT-A decreased， however， the TMT-A still showed the highest effect size. Although the results of this study are interesting and suggest that neuropsychological test results already start to differ 10 years before the patients enter the diagnosis of dementia， it should be kept in mind that all patients suffered from hypertension during their participation. Therefore compared with healthy controls a higher number of them will show vascular lesions regardless of a clinically diagnosed AD (which may explain the pre-dictive power of the TMT-A). Consequently it is unclear if the results can be generalized to the general population.**

【24】**Boraxbekk et al. (2015) analyzed data from the Betula longitudinal cohort study. They followed 3250 participants for a period of 22 years. They were able to distinguish between three groups： Group 1 developed dementia11-22 years after baseline testing (n=111)， group 2 developed dementia1-10 years after baseline testing (n=280)， and group 3 showed no deterio-ration indicative of dementia (n=2855). The results showed that two free recall episodic memory tests predicted dementia 10 years before the clinical diagnosis. There was also a statistically significant difference in free recall in the first group； however， this difference did not survive the statistical cor-rection for age differences. Unfortunately the cause of the dementia was not validated by other investigations； therefore we do not know how many of the patients with dementia suffered from AD.**

【25】There is one other longitudinal study that should be mentioned here. Mistridis et al. (2015) used the CERAD-NAB to follow cognitive decline in the Basel Study on the Elderly longitudinal study. All participants were assessed every 2 years. They divided the whole group into two subgroups. The first group， the preclinical AD group， developed MCI. The other group did not deteriorate in their performance. Both the wordlist delayed recall and the word list savings subtests of the CERAD-NAB showed statistically significant dif-ferences between the two groups even 8 years before the onset of MCI. This result is a very similar to that of Boraxbekk et al. (2015).

【26】**Visuoconstructive memory performance started to differ between the two groups 4 years before the MCI diagnosis emerged. The same held true for semantic fluency and word list learning. The discriminability index and the TMT subtests differed 2 years earlier， while the visuoconstructive performance and phonological word fluency did not differ at the time of the diagnosis. Patients with CSF-based confirmed AD did not show impairment in the pho-nological word fluency task but in the semantic word fluency task. It is also of interest that in the study by Mistridis et al. (2015)， impaired wordlist delayed recall and wordlist learning were the earliest signs of progression and not wordlist discrimination and delayed recall of visuoconstruction.**

【4】**2.7Summary of neuropsychological testing in patients suspected for Alzheimer’s disease**

【5】**In summary， it can be stated that neuropsychological testing is able to distin-guish between typical AD patients and healthy controls rather well， but the differentiation between different neurodegenerative diseases leading to mem-ory impairments poses considerable problems. Consolidation of information is highly impaired in AD patients and should be used to separate AD patients from patients with unknown causes of cognitive impairment. Still， even com-posite scores for verbal learning， recall and recognition， or verbal and visuo-constructive recall suffer from the fact that they are affected by the stage of disease progression. They differ from CSF biomarkers in this respect. The probability for diagnosing AD increases in patients with consolidation deficits if they show normal phonological word fluency， impaired semantic word fluency and have anaverage digit span percentile above _3_ 30\. Neuropsychiatric changes of AD encompass higher apathy， increased anxiety and dependence， but not depressive mood. Despite these distinctive symp-toms of AD， neuropsychological assessment still looks for cutoff scores that do not depend on the global impairment to enhance the probability of their differential diagnosis.**

【6】**Neuropsychological assessment of patients suspected to suffer from (pre-clinical) AD should additionally rely on a measurement of false positives in a PRT. Patients with AD display an increased number of false positives. They also tend to have a lower primacy proportion than recency proportion when analyzing the wordlist serial position effect. Paired associate learning is highly sensitive for memory impairments very early in the disease progres-sion. However， impairments in PAL are also common in other neurodegener-ative diseases， if the patients start to progress. Thus an impairment in PAL does not seem to be specific feature of AD but a global measurement of the severity of the memory decline.**

**Arguing that there are no single tests or combination of test results that allow for an accurate clinical diagnosis， does not mean that the clini-cal investigation is invalid. It means that the combined information from|删除0换行|the different aspects of the assessment must guide the decision for the correct diagnosis.**

【8】**2.8 Prediction of conversion to Alzheimer's disease by neuropsychological tests**

【9】**2.8.1 Prediction using the WMS logical memory test and the ADNI neuropsychological mild cognitive impairment criteria**

【10】**The case presented earlier highlights another problem regarding the assess-ment of neurodegenerative diseases： the question of the prognosis. In many patients， only another future assessment will deliver the correct diagnosis. On the other hand， the main interest of the patients is to obtain information immediately about how their problems might develop in the future. Will they progress to a state of dementia or not? This question can be reframed in clinical terms as predicting whether the patient’s state will convert from MCI to dementia and， in the case of typical AD， from amnestic MCI to AD.**

【11】**One of the earliest studies， with a large number of patients from two dif-ferent study centers (the Mayo Clinic and the Karolinska Institute)， showed an increased risk for MCI patients to concert to dementia， depending on the number of cognitive domains being affected 删除1:<u>(Arnaiz et al.， 2004)</u>： about 40%of the patients with impairment in memory performance converted to demen-tia after 5 years， however， this number rose to more than 50% when the patient was impaired in more than one neuropsychological test).**

【12】**Taken together， these results suggest a conversion rate of about 7%-8%per year for pure amnestic MCI patients and 12% for multidomain impaired patients. It should be kept in mind that all these patients came to the hospital because they or their relatives noted cognitive decline， and that other causes for that experienced decline were excluded through an extended neurological examination. Thus the results cannot be easily generalized to population samples that do not possess an urgent enough sense of cognitive decline that causes them to get in contact with a diagnostic unit.**

**Over the past 15 years， the ADNI research group， a very large Northern America-based research network， was able to include a large number of par-ticipants in their data set. They were categorized into those with and without amnestic MCI according to the result of the logical memory test of the WMS IV (being impaired corresponded with a score smaller than-1.5SD). Patients who were impaired in other tests， but not in the logical memory test， were categorized as having a nonamnestic MCI. Storandt and Morris (2010) analyzed the predictive value of the logical memory test in a longitudinal project including healthy controls. The brains of all subjects were analyzed postmortem to determine whether they had developed Alzheimer’s dementia(or not) to provide a definitive diagnosis. The predictive value of the logical memory test was low， and specificity and sensitivity ranged from 55% to|删除0换行|50%. Other neuropsychological tests， like visual associate learning from the WMS and Block design， showed a higher specificity (above 80%) but a low sensitivity (between 30% and 40%).

【14】**Bondi et al. (2014) also used the logical memory test of the WMS and the data of participants from the ADNI project to analyze the predictive power of this test. As mentioned previously， a score less than -1.5SD is the hallmark of amnestic MCI for the ADNI diagnosis. After about 4years， 35.8% of the pure amnestic MCI patients converted to dementia，61.7% remained stable and 4.2% reversed to a normal score. Fifty-seven percentage of the patients with more than one impairment converted to dementia and only 1% reversed. Additionally there was a group of unim-paired participants and 9.3% of them converted to dementia. Bondi et al.(2014) compared these percentages with a categorization based on two measures for each cognitive domain tested. With respect to memory， this was done by adding the performance in the auditory verbal learning test(which includes learning trials and a recognition measure) with the text reproduction of the WMS. The classification based on two measures per-formed better than that based on the text reproduction alone： 46.5% of the patients with amnestic MCI converted to dementia and none of these patients reverted to an unimpaired state. In the case of being impaired in more than one cognitive domain (being impaired in both memory tests and in one other test)， the conversion rate was even higher： 60% of these patients converted to dementia within the following 7 years. These num-bers are very similar to results from the Mayo Clinic and the Karolinska Institute mentioned earlier 删除1:<u>(Arnaiz et al.， 2004)</u>. The study by Bondi et al.(2014) also compared the predictive power of the auditory verbal learning test alone with that of text reproduction alone. The auditory verbal learn-ing test was better in predicting the conversion. One may conclude that a“one-shot presentation”of verbal information， as is the case in the text reproduction test of the WMS IV， is suboptimal for diagnosing MCI. Memory measures based on several learning trials and those that include recognition elements yielded better results for making predictions regard-ing the fate of the patients.**

【15】**2.8.2 Prediction using the CERAD-NAB or standard neuropsychological tests**

In a systematic review， Belleville et al. (2017) found that immediate and delayed free recall of different verbal learning tests are the most sensitive and specific tests for predicting the conversion of patients with MCI to Alzheimer’s dementia. Depending on the study， the sensitivity was about75% and the specificity was often around 80% (or even higher). Visuospatial memory tests assessing free recall were slightly less accurate than verbal memory tests in predicting the conversion to dementia. Other|删除0换行|neuropsychological tests showed a lower sensitivity， but sometimes a similar specificity. The sensitivity of word fluency， for example， increased relative to the number of years between the assessment and the clinical diagnosis of dementia. Furthermore a low Boston Naming Test result predicted a fast pro-gression. According to the review， immediate and delayed verbal free recalls are the best variables for prediction， whereas verbal recognition and cued recall measures do not improve their sensitivity and specificity. In this respect， it is important to mention that a differential diagnosis was not the focus of the studies reviewed here. Instead， the focus was only on making predictions for patients not showing any signs of other neurodegenerative diseases than AD. Studies utilizing the CERAD-NAB were not included in the review by Belleville et al. (2017). Cerami et al. (2017) reviewed two studies with a large number of patients who used the CERAD-NAB. Both showed an accuracy of at least 90%.**

【17】**Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) followed up 357 patients， who were at least75 years old， with MCI (assessed with the CERAD-NAB) for a period of3 years. Overall 41.5% of the patients had a remission of symptoms with normal cognitive function 1.5 and 3 years later， 21.3% showed a fluctuating course， 14.8% had stable symptoms， and 22.4% progressed to dementia. This study is important because it allows patients with MCI to be informed that they have a 78% chance to recover or remain stable over 3 years. On the other hand， 22.4% showed additional decline which is a rate of 7.5 per year. When compared with the single-domain nonamnestic subtype， patients with multidomain amnestic MCI had a three times greater risk of developing a more severe course of MCI. This was followed by patients with multidomain nonamnestic MCI， whose risk was two timesSgreater. Patients with the single-domain amnestic subtype did not have a significantly elevated risk. Patients were at a higher risk of advancing from one course to the next along this spectrum if they had symptoms of depression， impairment in more than one cognitive domain， more severe cognitive impairment， or were older. The result of a test regarding the ability to learn and reproduce new material after a 10-minute period was the best indicator for differentiating between remit-tent and progressive MCI at baseline. Symptoms of depression modified the prognosis.**

**The total number of recalled words during wordlist learning was the most sensitive parameter for predicting deterioration. Among patients who learned less than 15 words， almost 50% performed worse 3 years later. Since the risk for the other groups was low or related to noncognitive factors such as depression， the result of this study is very helpful to inform patients about their prognosis. Cognitive impairments of 50% of patients who learn more than 14 words will improve/be reversed after 3 years. Furthermore these patients showed a risk of MCI progression that is as low as the general popu-lation (less than 3% per year). Conversely 50% of patients who learn less than 15 words are expected to progress from MCI to dementia over the same|删除0换行|amount of time. Bear in mind， however， that the patients were at least 75years old.**

【19】**The study by Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) has a high clinical meaning as it was designed and conducted in assetting in which many patients are assessed for dementia， that is， visiting a geriatric unit due to cognitive impairment. Therefore the cutoff scores published by Kaduszkiewicz et al.(2014) can be used when discussing assessment results with the patients. However， it is unclear whether the results can also be generalized to patients visiting a neurology unit since these patients often suffer from additional gait or other movement disorders and may， therefore， differ from geriatric patients.**

【20】Nonetheless， special concern should be given to the group that learned less than 15 words during the CERAD-NAB. These individuals should be informed about the necessary lifestyle modifications that may reduce their risk. Furthermore their performance should be reevaluated on a yearly basis so that medication， if needed， can be started as early as possible.

【21】**The result of the study by Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) differs from other studies because Kaduszkiewicz et al. (2014) argue that wordlist learning， and not delayed recall， is the most meaningful parameter. Furthermore they included patients with MCI， whereas other studies， reviewed in more detail later， focused on cognitively unimpaired patients at baseline. The study by Mistridis， Krumm， Monsch， Berres， and Taylor (2015) showed that wordlist learning starts to differ between participants without cognitive impairment and those who will fulfill the criteria of a MCI diagnosis 4 years before the diagnosis can be made， whereas delayed recall already differs between these groups 8 years earlier. One explanation might be that wordlist learning does not show floor effects like delayed recall and may therefore allow a better discrimination in patients already presenting impairments.**

【22】**2.8.3 How early can cognitive impairments be measured in patients converting to dementia?**

**How early can we detect cognitive differences between participants that develop dementia and participants who do not develop the disease? This question can be studied only in longitudinal studies which include normal healthy participants or participants who express another nonbrain disease， which increases the risk of developing dementia. Cervilla， Prince， Joels， Lovestone， and Mann (2004) followed a group of patients with hypertension over a time period of 12 years and used various cognitive tests to assess their cognitive functioning at inclusion and during the following years. Forty-one of the analyzed group of 387 patients developed dementia. Patients who developed dementia significantly differed from patients who did not develop dementia with regard to neuropsychological test results. Furthermore these differences were already detectable 12 years prior to dementia onset. The|删除0换行|highest difference between the groups was found in the trail making test A， while the lowest difference was in the PAL task. When the focus was only on patients with a clinically based diagnosis of AD， performance in the PAL task increased as a relevant test marker. With the same focus， the difference in the TMT-A decreased， however， the TMT-A still showed the highest effect size. Although the results of this study are interesting and suggest that neuropsychological test results already start to differ 10 years before the patients enter the diagnosis of dementia， it should be kept in mind that all patients suffered from hypertension during their participation. Therefore compared with healthy controls a higher number of them will show vascular lesions regardless of a clinically diagnosed AD (which may explain the pre-dictive power of the TMT-A). Consequently it is unclear if the results can be generalized to the general population.**

【24】**Boraxbekk et al. (2015) analyzed data from the Betula longitudinal cohort study. They followed 3250 participants for a period of 22 years. They were able to distinguish between three groups： Group 1 developed dementia11-22 years after baseline testing (n=111)， group 2 developed dementia1-10 years after baseline testing (n=280)， and group 3 showed no deterio-ration indicative of dementia (n=2855). The results showed that two free recall episodic memory tests predicted dementia 10 years before the clinical diagnosis. There was also a statistically significant difference in free recall in the first group； however， this difference did not survive the statistical cor-rection for age differences. Unfortunately the cause of the dementia was not validated by other investigations； therefore we do not know how many of the patients with dementia suffered from AD.**

【25】There is one other longitudinal study that should be mentioned here. Mistridis et al. (2015) used the CERAD-NAB to follow cognitive decline in the Basel Study on the Elderly longitudinal study. All participants were assessed every 2 years. They divided the whole group into two subgroups. The first group， the preclinical AD group， developed MCI. The other group did not deteriorate in their performance. Both the wordlist delayed recall and the word list savings subtests of the CERAD-NAB showed statistically significant dif-ferences between the two groups even 8 years before the onset of MCI. This result is a very similar to that of Boraxbekk et al. (2015).

【26】**Visuoconstructive memory performance started to differ between the two groups 4 years before the MCI diagnosis emerged. The same held true for semantic fluency and word list learning. The discriminability index and the TMT subtests differed 2 years earlier， while the visuoconstructive performance and phonological word fluency did not differ at the time of the diagnosis. Patients with CSF-based confirmed AD did not show impairment in the pho-nological word fluency task but in the semantic word fluency task. It is also of interest that in the study by Mistridis et al. (2015)， impaired wordlist delayed recall and wordlist learning were the earliest signs of progression and not wordlist discrimination and delayed recall of visuoconstruction.**

【20】** KEY FACTS**

【21】**_CANICAL_**

【22】**◆The symptomatic clinical presentation of renal artery stenosis is hypertension， renal failurc， or both. The emphasis in this discussion is on hypertension.**

【23】**Approximately 60 million Americans are affected by hypertension. Renovascular hypertension， however， accounts for only a small minority (<5%).**

**_◆_ Indications that hypertension may be renovascular in naturc include (1) presence of an abdominal or flank bruit (due to renal artery stenosis)， (2) increase in serum creatinine levels by 0.5 mg/dl or more follow-ing antihypertensive treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor thcrapy， and|删除0换行|(3) malignant hypertension (i.e.， hypertension that is rapid in onset and refractory to medical therapy).**

【25】**◆The diagnosis of renal artery stenosis is then made by radiographic techniques， including nuclear scintigraphy and angiography. Angiography remains the gold stan-dard and has the advantage of visualizing the arteries and permits treatment (i.e.， percutaneous transluminal angioplasty \[PTA\]) during the same examination. Nuclear scintigraphy does not directly visualize the renal arteries but can determinc relative perfusion as well as renal function. Other techniques to visualize the renal arteries include CT angiography， MRA， and sonography.**

【26】**◆PTA has become the initial treatment of choice in many patients with renovascular hypertension， espe-cially those with hypertension refractory to medical therapy. In particular， PTA has become the treatment of choice for fibromuscular disease.**

【27】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【28】**_◆_ Renal artery stenosis is considered hemodynamically significant when there is 275% narrowing of the cross-sectional area of the lumen.**

【29】**◆In performing renal PTA， it is important to choose the appropriate bailoon size. Careful measurements of the“normal” arterial lumen should be made before balloon insertion. When measurements are made from angiograms performed using conventional film-screen techniques， a magnification factor of 10% to 20% can be assumed. It is generally considered acceptable to overdi-ate the artery by that degree. Measurement programs arc available to measure the size of the artery when angiogra-phy is performed using digital subtraction technique， In this setting， overdilation by 20% is again acceptable.**

【30】**◆IDuring renal PTA， guidewires and catheters should be passed across stenoses carefully and pressures obtained on each side of a stenosis. Although controversy exists about exact values， pressure gradients of >10 mm Hg systolic are generally considered abnormal.**

**Renal PTA is usually performed after the patient is fully anticoagulated. After placement of the balloon-|删除0换行|tipped catheter across the stenosis and dilatation with the balloon， repeat angiography is pcrformed while the guidewire is traversing the stenosis.**

【32】**If the angioplasty result is radiographically acceptablc(c.g.，<10% residual stenosis)， follow-up pressures can be obtained and the procedure discontinued.**

【33】**Thcre are multiple reasons for treatment failure (as defined by a poor angiographic result). Treatment of unwanted results must be considered on an individual basis and is often decided by a multidisciplinary team of an interna medicine physician， a surgeon， and the interventional radiologist. Possible undesired outcomes include：**

【34】**a. The stenosis is still present. Treatment then often consists of use of either or both a larger balloon and placement of a stent.**

【35】**b. A large intimal dissection has resulted. This com-plication is usually treated by stent placement.**

【36】**c. Extravasation of contrast matcrial is seen. In this circumstance， typically the balloon is reinflated to occlude the site of extravasation and emergency suirgical repair is performed.**

【37】**The results of revascularization (whether by surgery or PTA) have been standardized by the Society for Vascular and Interventional Radiology， based on the resultant reduction in blood pressure. Results are cate-gorized according to the diastolic blood pressure(BP) after treatment：**

【38】**Cure BPp <90 mm Hg without medication**

【39】**improvement**

【40】**90 mm Hg <BPp <110 mm Hg with at least a 15% decreasc in BPp after PTA on similar or decreased med-ications**

【41】**Failure All other results**

【42】**Results and complications reported in the medical lit-erature have been extensively reviewed using the above classification. Although results vary among studies， the average overall cure rate for atherosclerotic disease is13%， with another 55% improved， and an approximate9% complication rate. The results for fibromuscular disease are much more encouraging， with a 40% to45% cure rate and improvement in another 45% of patients. The complication rates are comparable or less than for atherosclerotic lesions.**

【43】**◆Controversy still exists over the efficacy of PTA for ostial renal artery lesions (defined as within 5 mm of the aorta). Although such lesions were once thought to be refractory to PTA， the most recent data indicate rcasonable success rates (although they are lower than for lesions within the mid-portion of the renal artery). Most investigators agree that successful PTA of ostial stenoses usually also requires stent placement.**

【55】**_◆_ The double aortic arch results from a persistence of the theoretical embryologic double arch. **Patient B： The multilobulated，“beaded”appearance and the fact that the distal main renal artery is|删除0换行|involved (rather than the orifice) is typical of fibro-muscular dysplasia. Neurofibromatosis is another rare entity that could also produce the same appearance. 【20】** KEY FACTS**

【21】**_CANICAL_**

【22】**◆The symptomatic clinical presentation of renal artery stenosis is hypertension， renal failurc， or both. The emphasis in this discussion is on hypertension.**

【23】**Approximately 60 million Americans are affected by hypertension. Renovascular hypertension， however， accounts for only a small minority (<5%).**

**_◆_ Indications that hypertension may be renovascular in naturc include (1) presence of an abdominal or flank bruit (due to renal artery stenosis)， (2) increase in serum creatinine levels by 0.5 mg/dl or more follow-ing antihypertensive treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor thcrapy， and|删除0换行|(3) malignant hypertension (i.e.， hypertension that is rapid in onset and refractory to medical therapy).**

【25】**◆The diagnosis of renal artery stenosis is then made by radiographic techniques， including nuclear scintigraphy and angiography. Angiography remains the gold stan-dard and has the advantage of visualizing the arteries and permits treatment (i.e.， percutaneous transluminal angioplasty \[PTA\]) during the same examination. Nuclear scintigraphy does not directly visualize the renal arteries but can determinc relative perfusion as well as renal function. Other techniques to visualize the renal arteries include CT angiography， MRA， and sonography.**

【26】**◆PTA has become the initial treatment of choice in many patients with renovascular hypertension， espe-cially those with hypertension refractory to medical therapy. In particular， PTA has become the treatment of choice for fibromuscular disease.**

【27】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【28】**_◆_ Renal artery stenosis is considered hemodynamically significant when there is 275% narrowing of the cross-sectional area of the lumen.**

【29】**◆In performing renal PTA， it is important to choose the appropriate bailoon size. Careful measurements of the“normal” arterial lumen should be made before balloon insertion. When measurements are made from angiograms performed using conventional film-screen techniques， a magnification factor of 10% to 20% can be assumed. It is generally considered acceptable to overdi-ate the artery by that degree. Measurement programs arc available to measure the size of the artery when angiogra-phy is performed using digital subtraction technique， In this setting， overdilation by 20% is again acceptable.**

【30】**◆IDuring renal PTA， guidewires and catheters should be passed across stenoses carefully and pressures obtained on each side of a stenosis. Although controversy exists about exact values， pressure gradients of >10 mm Hg systolic are generally considered abnormal.**

**Renal PTA is usually performed after the patient is fully anticoagulated. After placement of the balloon-|删除0换行|tipped catheter across the stenosis and dilatation with the balloon， repeat angiography is pcrformed while the guidewire is traversing the stenosis.**

【32】**If the angioplasty result is radiographically acceptablc(c.g.，<10% residual stenosis)， follow-up pressures can be obtained and the procedure discontinued.**

【33】**Thcre are multiple reasons for treatment failure (as defined by a poor angiographic result). Treatment of unwanted results must be considered on an individual basis and is often decided by a multidisciplinary team of an interna medicine physician， a surgeon， and the interventional radiologist. Possible undesired outcomes include：**

【34】**a. The stenosis is still present. Treatment then often consists of use of either or both a larger balloon and placement of a stent.**

【35】**b. A large intimal dissection has resulted. This com-plication is usually treated by stent placement.**

【36】**c. Extravasation of contrast matcrial is seen. In this circumstance， typically the balloon is reinflated to occlude the site of extravasation and emergency suirgical repair is performed.**

【37】**The results of revascularization (whether by surgery or PTA) have been standardized by the Society for Vascular and Interventional Radiology， based on the resultant reduction in blood pressure. Results are cate-gorized according to the diastolic blood pressure(BP) after treatment：**

【38】**Cure BPp <90 mm Hg without medication**

【39】**improvement**

【40】**90 mm Hg <BPp <110 mm Hg with at least a 15% decreasc in BPp after PTA on similar or decreased med-ications**

【41】**Failure All other results**

【42】**Results and complications reported in the medical lit-erature have been extensively reviewed using the above classification. Although results vary among studies， the average overall cure rate for atherosclerotic disease is13%， with another 55% improved， and an approximate9% complication rate. The results for fibromuscular disease are much more encouraging， with a 40% to45% cure rate and improvement in another 45% of patients. The complication rates are comparable or less than for atherosclerotic lesions.**

【43】**◆Controversy still exists over the efficacy of PTA for ostial renal artery lesions (defined as within 5 mm of the aorta). Although such lesions were once thought to be refractory to PTA， the most recent data indicate rcasonable success rates (although they are lower than for lesions within the mid-portion of the renal artery). Most investigators agree that successful PTA of ostial stenoses usually also requires stent placement.**

【25】**◆The diagnosis of renal artery stenosis is then made by radiographic techniques， including nuclear scintigraphy and angiography. Angiography remains the gold stan-dard and has the advantage of visualizing the arteries and permits treatment (i.e.， percutaneous transluminal angioplasty \[PTA\]) during the same examination. Nuclear scintigraphy does not directly visualize the renal arteries but can determinc relative perfusion as well as renal function. Other techniques to visualize the renal arteries include CT angiography， MRA， and sonography.**

【26】**◆PTA has become the initial treatment of choice in many patients with renovascular hypertension， espe-cially those with hypertension refractory to medical therapy. In particular， PTA has become the treatment of choice for fibromuscular disease.**

【28】**_◆_ Renal artery stenosis is considered hemodynamically significant when there is 275% narrowing of the cross-sectional area of the lumen.**

【29】**◆In performing renal PTA， it is important to choose the appropriate bailoon size. Careful measurements of the“normal” arterial lumen should be made before balloon insertion. When measurements are made from angiograms performed using conventional film-screen techniques， a magnification factor of 10% to 20% can be assumed. It is generally considered acceptable to overdi-ate the artery by that degree. Measurement programs arc available to measure the size of the artery when angiogra-phy is performed using digital subtraction technique， In this setting， overdilation by 20% is again acceptable.**

【30】**◆IDuring renal PTA， guidewires and catheters should be passed across stenoses carefully and pressures obtained on each side of a stenosis. Although controversy exists about exact values， pressure gradients of >10 mm Hg systolic are generally considered abnormal.**

**Renal PTA is usually performed after the patient is fully anticoagulated. After placement of the balloon-|删除0换行|tipped catheter across the stenosis and dilatation with the balloon， repeat angiography is pcrformed while the guidewire is traversing the stenosis.**

【32】**If the angioplasty result is radiographically acceptablc(c.g.，<10% residual stenosis)， follow-up pressures can be obtained and the procedure discontinued.**
