【420】**Limb girdle muscular dystrophies are being rapidly charac-terized by molecular genetic techniques. The present classifi-cation rests on the basis of the 1994 criterion.**

【421】**The disease may have its initial presentation in the pelvic or shoulder girdle musculature concomitantly or seriatim. The initial symptoms relate to weakness of these muscle groups. Early contractures may be noted in some of the AD forms， but not often in the AR varieties. Calf hypertrophy is frequent and often demonstrates intrafamilial variability. Exclusion criteria are onset of weakness in distal， facial or extraocular muscles. Onset of the disease may occur at any age. In recessive forms the process generally starts prior to 20years of age. Later onset usually occurs in dominant disease.**

【422】**The classification continues to be modified according to each entities specific genetic defect. Single gene mutations may cause specific phenotypic expression. Both Miyoshi dis-tal myopathy and LGMD 2B may result from mutation of the dysferlin gene on chromosome 2p13. LGMD 2G and LGMD 2H involve distal lower extremity muscle compart-ments. LGMD 2H may have early facial involvement which usually is an exclusion criterion for LGMD**

【420】**Limb girdle muscular dystrophies are being rapidly charac-terized by molecular genetic techniques. The present classifi-cation rests on the basis of the 1994 criterion.**

【421】**The disease may have its initial presentation in the pelvic or shoulder girdle musculature concomitantly or seriatim. The initial symptoms relate to weakness of these muscle groups. Early contractures may be noted in some of the AD forms， but not often in the AR varieties. Calf hypertrophy is frequent and often demonstrates intrafamilial variability. Exclusion criteria are onset of weakness in distal， facial or extraocular muscles. Onset of the disease may occur at any age. In recessive forms the process generally starts prior to 20years of age. Later onset usually occurs in dominant disease.**

【422】**The classification continues to be modified according to each entities specific genetic defect. Single gene mutations may cause specific phenotypic expression. Both Miyoshi dis-tal myopathy and LGMD 2B may result from mutation of the dysferlin gene on chromosome 2p13. LGMD 2G and LGMD 2H involve distal lower extremity muscle compart-ments. LGMD 2H may have early facial involvement which usually is an exclusion criterion for LGMD**

【421】**The disease may have its initial presentation in the pelvic or shoulder girdle musculature concomitantly or seriatim. The initial symptoms relate to weakness of these muscle groups. Early contractures may be noted in some of the AD forms， but not often in the AR varieties. Calf hypertrophy is frequent and often demonstrates intrafamilial variability. Exclusion criteria are onset of weakness in distal， facial or extraocular muscles. Onset of the disease may occur at any age. In recessive forms the process generally starts prior to 20years of age. Later onset usually occurs in dominant disease.**

【420】**Limb girdle muscular dystrophies are being rapidly charac-terized by molecular genetic techniques. The present classifi-cation rests on the basis of the 1994 criterion.**

【421】**The disease may have its initial presentation in the pelvic or shoulder girdle musculature concomitantly or seriatim. The initial symptoms relate to weakness of these muscle groups. Early contractures may be noted in some of the AD forms， but not often in the AR varieties. Calf hypertrophy is frequent and often demonstrates intrafamilial variability. Exclusion criteria are onset of weakness in distal， facial or extraocular muscles. Onset of the disease may occur at any age. In recessive forms the process generally starts prior to 20years of age. Later onset usually occurs in dominant disease.**

【420】**Limb girdle muscular dystrophies are being rapidly charac-terized by molecular genetic techniques. The present classifi-cation rests on the basis of the 1994 criterion.**

【421】**The disease may have its initial presentation in the pelvic or shoulder girdle musculature concomitantly or seriatim. The initial symptoms relate to weakness of these muscle groups. Early contractures may be noted in some of the AD forms， but not often in the AR varieties. Calf hypertrophy is frequent and often demonstrates intrafamilial variability. Exclusion criteria are onset of weakness in distal， facial or extraocular muscles. Onset of the disease may occur at any age. In recessive forms the process generally starts prior to 20years of age. Later onset usually occurs in dominant disease.**

【422】**The classification continues to be modified according to each entities specific genetic defect. Single gene mutations may cause specific phenotypic expression. Both Miyoshi dis-tal myopathy and LGMD 2B may result from mutation of the dysferlin gene on chromosome 2p13. LGMD 2G and LGMD 2H involve distal lower extremity muscle compart-ments. LGMD 2H may have early facial involvement which usually is an exclusion criterion for LGMD**

【420】**Limb girdle muscular dystrophies are being rapidly charac-terized by molecular genetic techniques. The present classifi-cation rests on the basis of the 1994 criterion.**

【421】**The disease may have its initial presentation in the pelvic or shoulder girdle musculature concomitantly or seriatim. The initial symptoms relate to weakness of these muscle groups. Early contractures may be noted in some of the AD forms， but not often in the AR varieties. Calf hypertrophy is frequent and often demonstrates intrafamilial variability. Exclusion criteria are onset of weakness in distal， facial or extraocular muscles. Onset of the disease may occur at any age. In recessive forms the process generally starts prior to 20years of age. Later onset usually occurs in dominant disease.**

【422】**The classification continues to be modified according to each entities specific genetic defect. Single gene mutations may cause specific phenotypic expression. Both Miyoshi dis-tal myopathy and LGMD 2B may result from mutation of the dysferlin gene on chromosome 2p13. LGMD 2G and LGMD 2H involve distal lower extremity muscle compart-ments. LGMD 2H may have early facial involvement which usually is an exclusion criterion for LGMD**

【2】**Hodgkin Lymphoma**

【3】**Clinical Features**

【4】Most common malignant tumor of the mediastinum

【5】Occurs predominantly in the anterior compartment

【7】Young women in their 20s and 30s are most commonly affected

【12】With thymic involvement， cystic degeneration is common

【13】Histopathology

【14】Nodular sclerosing variant is the most common type

【15】Type is best determined by lymph node analysis， as the diagnostic features may not be represented in extranodal sites

【16】When extranodal， such as in the thymus， Hodgkin disease generally forms a discrete mass

【17】\- Collagenous fibrosis and the typical background cells (small lymphocytes， plasma cells， and eosinophils) are present

【18】_—_ Classic Reed-Sternberg cells in a background consistent with Hodgkin lymphoma are needed to establish a new diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma in an extranodal site

【19】\- In a patient with an established diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma， mononuclear cells with the other features of Reed-Sternberg cells (Hodgkin cells) in the background of collagen and cells typical of Hodgkin lymphoma are sufficient to diagnose involvement of an extranodal site

【28】**Thymoma**

【31】Eosinophils and plasma cells are rare

【33】Thymic cyst

【35】No atypical lymphoid cells are seen

【37】Sclerosing large cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma

【38】Monotonous population of large， atypical lymphoid cells without distinctive milieu of Hodgkin lymphoma(i.e.， small lymphocytes，plasma cells， and eosinophils)

【39】Tumor cells are almost always of B-cell lineage and express CD19， CD20， and CD22

【40】Negative for CD15， but many cases can be CD30positive

【41】**Pearls**

【42】Nodular sclerosing is the most common type of Hodgkin lymphoma seen in the mediastinum

【43】Young women most commonly affected

【44】Can be often cystic—thorough sampling is necessary to identify diagnostic areas

【50】**Diffuse Large Cell Lymphoma， B-Cell Type**

【55】Almost always of B-cell lineage

【76】**Almost all cases occur in males**

【77】Composed of diffuse population of large cells with abundant cytoplasm and large nuclei with irregular(spiked) nucleoli

【78】Small lymphocytes are concentrated along delicate fibrovascular septa rather than scattered throughout the tumor

【79】Presence of glycogen in the clear cytoplasm favors the diagnosis of germinoma

【80】Positive for PLAP by immunohistochemistry

【81】**Negative for CD20 and CD45**

【82】Can show striking dotlike paranuclear positivity for cytokeratin and positive staining for C-kit (CD117)

【85】**Characterized by large multinucleated tumor cells**

【89】Lymphoblastic lymphoma

【91】Patients may have frank leukemia， which is exceptional in mediastinal large cell lymphoma

【92】Cells have very scant cytoplasm and blastic chromatin

【93】Cells express CD1， CD3， CD43，TdT

【94】1Negative for CD20

【95】**Metastatic carcinoma**

【96】Sheets or nests of cohesive neoplastic cells1May form glands or show obvious keratinization

【97】Tumor cells express cytokeratin； negative for CD20and CD45

【98】**Pearls**

【99】Generally affects young women (second to fourth decades)

【100】May involve the thymus

【101】Sclerosis and necrosis are common findings

【102】Almost always B-cell lineage

【126】Blood vessel invasion and extension into perithymic fibroadipose tissue may be prominent features

【137】Flow cytometry

【147】Cytokeratin highlights network of epithelial cells throughout the tumor

【148】ILymphocytes are not clonal

【149】Large B-cell lymphoma

【182】This rapidly growing tumor is seen predominantly in children and adolescents； male predominance

【26】Negative for T- or B-cell gene rearrangements

【27】Differential Diagnosis

【28】**Thymoma**

【29】**ILow-power view can mimic Hodgkin disease because of sclerosis’ forming well-defined nodules composed of large and small cells**

【30】No atypical lymphoid cells (Hodgkin cells)

【31】Eosinophils and plasma cells are rare

【32】Thymoma cells are positive for epithelial markers(cytokeratin)

【33】Thymic cyst

【34】Cyst has an epithelial cell lining

【35】No atypical lymphoid cells are seen

【36】**Adequate and extensive sampling is required in thymic cysts to rule out Hodgkin disease**

【37】Sclerosing large cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma

【38】Monotonous population of large， atypical lymphoid cells without distinctive milieu of Hodgkin lymphoma(i.e.， small lymphocytes，plasma cells， and eosinophils)

【39】Tumor cells are almost always of B-cell lineage and express CD19， CD20， and CD22

【40】Negative for CD15， but many cases can be CD30positive

【41】**Pearls**

【42】Nodular sclerosing is the most common type of Hodgkin lymphoma seen in the mediastinum

【43】Young women most commonly affected

【44】Can be often cystic—thorough sampling is necessary to identify diagnostic areas

【50】**Diffuse Large Cell Lymphoma， B-Cell Type**

【51】**Clinical Features**

【52】Second most common type of lymphoid malignancy of the mediastinum after Hodgkin lymphoma

【53】Predominantly affects females； peak incidence between 20 and 40 years of age

【54】**Typically found in anterior mediastinum**

【55】Almost always of B-cell lineage

【56】·Usually involves the thymus with or without lymph node involvement

【57】Signs and symptoms may include superior vena cava syndrome and pleural effusions

【58】Gross Pathology

【59】**Firm mass with foci of necrosis**

【60】Typically shows extensive infiltration into surrounding tissue

【61】Histopathology

【62】Diffuse growth pattern composed of large atypical lymphoid cells with reniform or multilobated nuclei， vesicular chromatin， and distinct nucleoli

【63】Large amounts of pale or clear cytoplasm

【64】**Often shows a pattern of stromal sclerosis characterized by compartmentalization of the tumor into discrete nests and islands simulating epithelial malignancy**

【65】通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 5-12. Diffuse large cell lymphoma with sclerosis. The tumor is composed of large atypical lymphoid cells showing a compartmen-talized appearance owing to fine bands of sclerosis that separate them into small islands.</u>

【66】Entrapment of thymic and extrathymic fat often seen

【67】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【68】CD19， CD20， CD22， and CD45 positive

【69】CD10， CD5， CD43，CD21， and immunoglobulin negative (resembling the phenotype of normal thymic B cells)

【70】此段无关页码删除:<u>Negative for CD15</u>

【71】Significant percentage of these cases can be CD30positive

【72】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【73】FFlow cytometric or gene rearrangement studies to verify lymphoid B- or T-cell lineage

【74】Differential Diagnosis

【75】**Germinoma**

【76】**Almost all cases occur in males**

【77】Composed of diffuse population of large cells with abundant cytoplasm and large nuclei with irregular(spiked) nucleoli

【78】Small lymphocytes are concentrated along delicate fibrovascular septa rather than scattered throughout the tumor

【79】Presence of glycogen in the clear cytoplasm favors the diagnosis of germinoma

【80】Positive for PLAP by immunohistochemistry

【81】**Negative for CD20 and CD45**

【82】Can show striking dotlike paranuclear positivity for cytokeratin and positive staining for C-kit (CD117)

【83】Hodgkin lymphoma， syncytial variant

【84】**Sclerosis is present in broad bands rather than diffusely**

【85】**Characterized by large multinucleated tumor cells**

【86】(Reed-Sternberg cells)

【87】Large cells are CD15 and CD30 positive

【88】·Large cells usually negative for CD20 and CD45

【89】Lymphoblastic lymphoma

【90】**Male predominance**

【91】Patients may have frank leukemia， which is exceptional in mediastinal large cell lymphoma

【92】Cells have very scant cytoplasm and blastic chromatin

【93】Cells express CD1， CD3， CD43，TdT

【94】1Negative for CD20

【95】**Metastatic carcinoma**

【96】Sheets or nests of cohesive neoplastic cells1May form glands or show obvious keratinization

【97】Tumor cells express cytokeratin； negative for CD20and CD45

【98】**Pearls**

【99】Generally affects young women (second to fourth decades)

【100】May involve the thymus

【101】Sclerosis and necrosis are common findings

【102】Almost always B-cell lineage

【103】Good response to multiagent chemotherapy with consolidation radiation therapy

【110】**Lymphoblastic Lymphoma**

【111】**Clinical Features**

【112】Predominantly seen in older children and adolescents but can also occur in older adult patients

Disease shows male predominance (2：1)F Patients may have a concomitant leukemic phase Almost all cases with a mediastinal mass at|删除0换行|presentation are of T-cell lineage 

【114】通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 5-13. Lymphoblastic lymphoma. Atypical lymphoid cells with fine chromatin， inconspicuous nucleoli， and frequent nuclear membrane infoldings are seen.</u>

【115】Mediastinum is most common location， and thymus is usually involved； with thymic involvement， residual lobules and infiltrated Hassall corpuscles may be seen

【116】Patients often present with acute onset of respiratory distress owing to the rapidly growing nature of the tumor

【117】Patients may have central nervous system and gonadal involvement at presentation

【118】Gross Pathology

【119】Usually solid， infiltrative， and lacks a capsule

【120】Histopathology

【121】Diffuse growth pattern composed of atypical lymphoid cells with fine (blastic) chromatin pattern

【122】Medium-sized cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio

【123】Cells may have nuclear convolutions with finely dispersed chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli (at high power， nuclear outline suggests outline of a brain as seen on CT) or may be of nonconvoluted type

【124】Numerous mitotic figures

【125】**Necrosis can be extensive**

【126】Blood vessel invasion and extension into perithymic fibroadipose tissue may be prominent features

【127】Neoplastic cells can infiltrate the thymus

【128】May have scattered tingible body macrophages， creating a starry-sky pattern

【129】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【130】TdT positive in almost all cases

【131】LCA positive in 80% of cases

【132】CD99 positive in most cases

【133】Tumor cells usually express CD1， CD43， and CD3

【134】Tumor cells may be positive or negative for CD4 and CD8

【135】CD45RO expressed in 50% of cases； CD20 is negative

【136】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【137】Flow cytometry

【138】\- May be misleading because lymphocytes in lymphocyte-rich thymomas show similar immunophenotype (i.e.， immature， blastic T cells)

【139】\- May not always differentiate clonal immature T cells from benign prethymic cells that may be found in thymoma

【140】Molecular studies： useful to detect gene rearrangement in lymphoblasts to verify clonality

【141】Cytogenetics： helps with diagnosis and is related to prognosis； particularly for B-lineage lymphoblastic lymphoma

【142】Differential Diagnosis

【143】Thymoma

【144】Rare in children； however， adults can develop either disease

【145】Lymphocytic component may be phenotypically indistinguishable from lymphoblastic lymphoma

【146】**Apoptotic lymphocytes may simulate a starry-sky pattern**

【147】Cytokeratin highlights network of epithelial cells throughout the tumor

【148】ILymphocytes are not clonal

【149】Large B-cell lymphoma

【150】Tumor cells are larger and have clear cytoplasm， vesicular nuclei， and usually prominent nucleoli； convoluted nuclei are uncommon

【151】Phenotype is that of a B-cell neoplasm

【152】Positive for CD20； negative for TdT， CD99， CDla

【153】**Other small round blue cell tumors of childhood**

【154】**Granulocytic sarcoma**

【155】**EExtremely uncommon SSearch carefully for cells with granular cytoplasmTumor cells positive for myeloperoxidase； negative for TdT**

【156】CD43 and CD45 may be positive and are not helpful in this differential diagnosis

【157】**Neuroblastoma**

【158】Typically found in posterior mediastinum

【159】More commonly seen in younger children

【160】Composed of smaller round cells with scant cytoplasm forming characteristic rosettes； look for neuropil in the background

【161】FPositive for neuron-specific enolase (NSE)， negative for lymphoid markers

【162】Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma

【163】**Mixture of haphazardly arranged rhabdomyoblasts and undifferentiated primitive cells**

【164】Positive for MyoD1， myogenin， and other markers of muscle differentiation (desmin， actin， and myosin)

【165】1Negative for TdT and lymphoid markers

【166】Primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)

【167】**Rare in this location**

【168】May have limited neural differentiation (usually positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin)

【169】此段无关页码删除:<u>**Positive for CD99**</u>

【170】Intracytoplasmic glycogen (PAS positive)

【171】Negative for TdT and lymphoid markers

【172】Characteristic translocation t(11；22)

【173】Small cell carcinoma (neuroendocrine carcinoma， oat cell carcinomal

【174】·Mostly in older adults

【175】May be primary or metastatic

【176】**Small cells with nuclear molding and scant cytoplasm**

【177】Nuclei have fine salt-and-pepper stippled chromatin or smudged chromatin pattern

【178】**Prominent crush artefact and extensive necrosis**

【179】**Tumor cells express cytokeratin， chromogranin， and synaptophysin**

【180】Negative for TdT， CD45， and CD3

【181】**Pearls**

【182】This rapidly growing tumor is seen predominantly in children and adolescents； male predominance

【183】·Leukemia and bone marrow involvement is commonAlmost all cases presenting with a mediastinal mass are of T-cell lineage

【184】Always include a cytokeratin stain in your panel to make sure you do not miss a lymphocyte-rich thymoma

【190】**Castleman Disease**

【191】**Clinical Features**

【192】Reactive condition； also known as angiofollicular _lymph node hyperplasia_

【193】Found predominantly involving lymph nodes； occasionally may involve the thymus

【194】Both sexes may be affected

【195】Wide age range

【196】Three types： hyaline vascular， plasma cell， and mixed Hyaline vascular type (about 80% of cases)

【197】◆Usually asymptomatic except for effects of compression by mass

【198】—Plasma cell type

【199】_◆_ Patients may have anemia， hypergammaglobulinemia， and fever

【200】Typically solitary but multicentric variant does exist

【201】通用删除16(英):<u>**Figure 5-14. Castleman disease. This histologic section shows a germinal center with hyalinized blood vessels and distinct concentric layering.**</u>

【202】 Multicentric variant： multiple lymph nodes at multiple sites are involved

【203】**Hepatosplenomegaly**

【204】·Hematologic and immunologic abnormalities(pancytopenia， increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate， proteinuria)

【205】One third of patients develop other malignancies(non-Hodgkin lymphoma \[NHL\]， carcinoma， or Kaposi sarcoma)

【206】More frequent in patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection

【207】Associated with infection with Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV， human herpesvirus-8\[HHV-8\])， especially in HIV-positive patients

【208】Gross Pathology

【209】Hyaline vascular type

【210】**· Large single mass**

【211】VWell-circumscribed round nodule usually located in the anterior-superior aspect of the mediastinum

【212】Plasma cell type

【213】Forms a mass and more commonly affects multiple lymph nodes

【214】Histopathology

【215】Hyaline vascular type (about 80% of cases) Multiple follicles with small germinal centers

【216】Hyalinized blood vessels penetrate the germinal centers (lollipop sign)

【217】Germinal centers may show concentric foci of hyalinization resembling Hassall corpuscles

【218】Small cells of the mantle zone may show distinct concentric layering (onion-skinning)

【219】Abnormal follicles may contain multiple small germinal centers

【220】Rich network of capillaries in the interfollicular zone FPerivascular fibrosis may be seen around interfollicular vessels

【221】Interfollicular regions are composed primarily of lymphocytes but also contain plasma cells， immunoblasts， and eosinophils

【222】Plasma cell type (10% to 20%)

【223】· Interfollicular areas contain sheets of plasma cells(diagnostic feature)

【224】**Germinal centers are large and reactive Mixed (rare)**

【225】Combination of features from hyaline vascular and plasma cell variants

【226】**Generally asymptomatic unless mass causes compression**

【227】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【228】CD5-positive lymphoid cells are seen at the periphery of the abnormal follicles (suggesting that Castleman disease is a proliferation of CD5-positive lymphocytes stimulated by specific lymphokines)

【229】Polyclonal population of B-lymphocytes and plasma cells

【230】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【231】Flow cytometry and gene rearrangement studies：polyclonal

【232】Differential Diagnosis

【233】Follicular lymphoma

【234】Monotonous follicles composed of atypical lymphocytes

【235】Cytologically abnormal cells， most of which have cleaved nuclei (centrocytes)

【236】**Monoclonal B cells**

【237】**Positive for CD20 and bcl-2**

【238】Plasmacytoma

【239】Pure plasmacytic population composed of clonal plasma cells

【240】**Generally lacks hyalinized germinal centers and onion-skinning of mantle zone**

【241】Must be careful with clonality because several reports have demonstrated a monoclonal plasma cell component in the interfollicular area in Castleman disease

【251】**Thymic Histology in Immune Deficiencies**

【252】**Clinical Features**

【253】Thymic histology can be abnormal in a variety of congenital and acquired immune deficiency diseases， particularly in T-lymphocyte deficiencies

【254】**Generally a clinical diagnosis， with patients having characteristic clinical presentations and features of an immune deficiency**

【255】Gross Pathology

【256】DiGeorge syndrome： thymic hypoplasia or aplasia with reduced to absent normal thymic tissue

【257】Other congenital immune defects： atrophic thymic tissue

【258】DiGeorge syndrome

【259】VWhatever thymic tissue is present is histologically normal or shows variable stress involution

【260】**B-cell immune defects**

【261】Features of exaggerated stress involution

【262】Decreased corticomedullary differentiation

【263】Decreased number of lymphocytes

【264】Variable number of Hassall corpuscles

【265】Severe combined immune deficiency (SCID)

【266】__ FPattern is called thymic dysplasia

【267】Small round to oval lobules of spindle to polygonal epithelial cells

【268】Few or no lymphocytes and absence of Hassall corpuscles

【269】Patients with less severe forms of deficiency may have a few lymphocytes and Hassall corpuscles

【270】**Severe acquired immune damage (AIDS and graft-versus-host disease \[GVHD\])**

【271】SSevere lymphocyte depletion Hassall corpuscles may disappear AApoptotic bodies can be seen

【272】Apoptosis of thymic epithelial cells has been reported in GVHD

【273】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【274】**Noncontributory**

【275】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【276】Immunologic studies and lymphocyte function tests used to classify the defect are usually performed on the peripheral blood lymphocytes

【277】Differential Diagnosis

【278】**Stress involution**

【279】**Clinically important in infants**

【280】Stress involution and immune deficiencies create an overlapping range of histologic and functional alterations in the thymus (differences are those of degree)

【281】Hassall corpuscles are more often present than in severe thymic dysplasia

【282】·Lobules tend to be triangular rather than rounded

【283】Apoptotic cells are usually lymphoid

【284】**Pearls**

【285】**__ Thymus may be a target of attack in GVHD**

There may be overlap of histologic features between|删除0换行|stress involution and milder forms of thymic dysplasia in congenital immune deficiencies

【67】Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a clonal proliferation of immature hematopoietic precursors involving primarily the bone marrow (BM) and blood. The classification of acute leukemia is based on the morphologic， immunophenotypic， cytogenetic， molecular， and clinical data. Generally， acute leukemias are divided into acute lymphoblastic leukemia(ALL) and AML， with a subset of leukemias displaying fea-tures of both \[mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL】\].

【68】AML represents a heterogeneous group of disorders with variable clinical presentation， cellular morphology，immuno-phenotype， chromosomal and molecular changes， therapeu-tic response， and overall prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-15\]</u>. Generally， AML can be defined as a clonal malignancy of transformed multi-potent hematopoietic progenitor cell leading to the accumu-lation of immature cells in the BM， which replace normal elements causing cytopenias and their complications (e.g.， fatigue due to anemia， infections due to granulocytopenia， and bleeding due to thrombocytopenia). The diagnosis and prognosis are most accurately provided by the pretreatment assessment of the morphology， immunophenotype， and most importantly underlying chromosomal and/or molecular aber-rations . The WHO classifies AML based on the genetic， immunophenotypic， and clinical characteristics. AML， not otherwise specified， is further subdivided based on the morphologic criteria similar to prior French-American-

【69】British (FAB) classification .

【70】**The current WHO classification divides AML into the following four major categories ：**

【71】1\. AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities

【72】**2\. AML with myelodysplasia-related changes**

【73】3\. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms

【74】**4\. AML， not other wise specified**

【98】**CYTOGENETICS AND FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIZATION STUDIES IN AML**

Cytogenetic abnormalities in AML at presentation have been identified as one of the most important prognostic factors and have been shown to be independent of age， white blood cell(WBC) counts，andtype of leukemia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，15-18\]</u>. Approximately30% of AML patients carry recurrent chromosomal abnormal-ities associated with different clinical features and prognosis通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，18\]</u>. They include t(15；17) (13%)， t(8；21)(7%)，inv(16)/t(16；16)(5%)， t(6；9) (1%)， t(9；11) (1%)， and inv(3) (1%) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Balanced translocations tend to occur more often in younger patients， whereas del(5q)， del(7q)， +11，+13， and various monosomies|删除0换行|occur more often in older patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Cytogenetic risk sta-tus is a significant factor in predicting response of AML to therapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[19\]</u>， for example， the outcome of patients with APL has substantially improved with the use of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) in combination with chemotherapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[20，21\]</u>. Cytogenetically， normal AML represents 40%-60% of AML patients (16-60 years of age) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，17，18\]</u>. Table 34.2 lists the most common chromosomal changes in AML.**

Older patients (>60 years old) with five or more abnor-malities have extremely poor prognosis. In a study by Farag et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[22\]</u>， no patients aged ≥60 years with five or more abnor-malities were alive at 5 years， despite intensive chemotherapy.

【105】Patients with normal karyotype， nO -Y， del(9q)，t(9；11)， del(20q)， +21， and +22 belong to intermediate prognostic category 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，18，19\]</u>. Patients with t(15；17) treated with stan-dard ATRA and anthracycline-based therapy have favorable prognosis regardless of the additional abnormalities (irrespec-tive of complexity) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，15，18，19\]</u>. Neither complex karyotype nor secondary aberrations affected the outcome of patients with t(8；21)，inv(16)/t(16；16)， or t(9；11) in a series reported by Byrd et al.通用删除6(英):<u>\[9\]</u> and Grimwade et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. In patients with inv(16)， the presence of additional changes， particularly +22， predicted a better outcome \[151.

【106】**CHROMOSOMAL CHANGES**

【107】AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recog-nized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. These patients often present with anemia and normal or increased platelet count. The BM often shows increased small hypolo-bated megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. Patients are often refractory to conventional therapy and have short overall survival. AML with t(3；21) differs from that with inv(3)/t(3；3) by higher frequency of therapy-related disease， lack of megakaryocytic hyperplasia， and shorter survival通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>. The t(3；21)， which disrupts CBF， is typically present in t-AML. AML with t(3；5)/NPMI-MLF1， considered an MDS-related abnormality， has intermediate prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.

Monosomy 5/del(5q) may be seen in all types of AML， but is more common in acute erythroid leukemia (AEL) or AML with minimal differentiation. Monosomy 5/del(5q) and mono-somy 7/del(7q) represent the most common cytogenetic abnor-malities in therapy-related myeloid neoplasm and are strongly associated with prior exposure to alkylating agents 通用删除6(英):<u>\[24\]</u>. AML|删除0换行|with del(5q) or monosomy 5 is associated with poor progno-sis， similar to AML with complex chromosomal abnormali-ties， monosomy 7， and t(9；22)通用删除6(英):<u>\[8，16，18，25，26\]</u>.

【109】Patients with t(6；9) have a dismal prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，27\]</u>. The presence of t(6；9)/DEK-CAN， recognized in the current WHO classification as a separate disease entity， is associ-ated with a very poor prognosis and is generally assigned to the adverse cytogenetic risk group. The poor outcome may relate to a strong association with FLT3-internal tan-dem duplication (ITD) mutations 通用删除6(英):<u>\[27，28\]</u>. In a series by Grimwade et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>， there was some evidence of poorer outcome in patients with t(6；9) compared to normal karyo-type， but this effect was not sufficiently strong to emerge in multivariate analysis.

【110】**Trisomy 8 is the most frequently reported numerical cyto-genetic abnormality in patients with AML. Patients with sole+8 and +8 with additional abnormality other than t(8；21)， inv(16)/t(16；16)， and t(9；11) had significantly inferior overall survival， but not complete remission rate， whereas patients with +8 and a complex karyotype with three or more abnor-malities had significantly inferior complete remission rate and overall survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9\]</u>. The impact of trisomy 8 on AML patients is best predicted by the presence and nature of abnormalities that accompany it 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，29\]</u>.**

【67】Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a clonal proliferation of immature hematopoietic precursors involving primarily the bone marrow (BM) and blood. The classification of acute leukemia is based on the morphologic， immunophenotypic， cytogenetic， molecular， and clinical data. Generally， acute leukemias are divided into acute lymphoblastic leukemia(ALL) and AML， with a subset of leukemias displaying fea-tures of both \[mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL】\].

【68】AML represents a heterogeneous group of disorders with variable clinical presentation， cellular morphology，immuno-phenotype， chromosomal and molecular changes， therapeu-tic response， and overall prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-15\]</u>. Generally， AML can be defined as a clonal malignancy of transformed multi-potent hematopoietic progenitor cell leading to the accumu-lation of immature cells in the BM， which replace normal elements causing cytopenias and their complications (e.g.， fatigue due to anemia， infections due to granulocytopenia， and bleeding due to thrombocytopenia). The diagnosis and prognosis are most accurately provided by the pretreatment assessment of the morphology， immunophenotype， and most importantly underlying chromosomal and/or molecular aber-rations . The WHO classifies AML based on the genetic， immunophenotypic， and clinical characteristics. AML， not otherwise specified， is further subdivided based on the morphologic criteria similar to prior French-American-

【69】British (FAB) classification .

【70】**The current WHO classification divides AML into the following four major categories ：**

【71】1\. AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities

【72】**2\. AML with myelodysplasia-related changes**

【73】3\. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms

【74】**4\. AML， not other wise specified**

【86】**The diagnosis of AML with myelodysplasia-related changes requires one of the following：**

【87】1\. Previoushistory of myelodysplasticsyndrome(MDS) or MDS/myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) and a marrow or blood blast count of >20%

【88】2\. Fifty percent or more of cells in two or more myeloid lineages with dyspoiesis

【89】**3\. Myelodysplasia-relatedcytogeneticabnormality. Cytogenetic abnormalities sufficient to diagnosis AML with myelodysplasia-related changes include the following：**

【90】**· Complex karyotype (three or more chromosomal abnormalities)**

【91】Unbalanced changes： -7 or del(7q)， -5 or del(5q)， i(17q) or t(17p)，-13 or del(13q)， del(11q)， del(12p) or t(12p)， del(9q)， and idic(X)(q13)

【92】Balanced changes： t(11；16)(q23；p13.3)， t(3；21)(q26.2；q22.1)，t(1；3)通用删除11(英):<u>(p36.3；q21.1)</u>， t(2；11)通用删除11(英):<u>(p21；q23)</u>， t(5；12)(q33；p12)，t(5；7)(q33；q11.2)，t(5；17)(q33；p13)， t(5；10)(q33；q21)，and t(3；5)(q25；q34)

【93】Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms include therapy-related AML (t-AML)， t-MDS， and t-MDS/MPN occurring as late complications of cytotoxic chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy. 【97】specific chromosomal/molecular changes and those which do not fulfill the criteria for therapy-related or MDS-associated AML are classified as AML， not otherwise specified. They are divided into more specific categories based on the mor-phology， the degree of maturation， the phenotype， and/or the cytochemistry (e.g.， AML with maturation， acute monoblastic leukemia， etc.).

【98】**CYTOGENETICS AND FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIZATION STUDIES IN AML**

Cytogenetic abnormalities in AML at presentation have been identified as one of the most important prognostic factors and have been shown to be independent of age， white blood cell(WBC) counts，andtype of leukemia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，15-18\]</u>. Approximately30% of AML patients carry recurrent chromosomal abnormal-ities associated with different clinical features and prognosis通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，18\]</u>. They include t(15；17) (13%)， t(8；21)(7%)，inv(16)/t(16；16)(5%)， t(6；9) (1%)， t(9；11) (1%)， and inv(3) (1%) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Balanced translocations tend to occur more often in younger patients， whereas del(5q)， del(7q)， +11，+13， and various monosomies|删除0换行|occur more often in older patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Cytogenetic risk sta-tus is a significant factor in predicting response of AML to therapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[19\]</u>， for example， the outcome of patients with APL has substantially improved with the use of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) in combination with chemotherapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[20，21\]</u>. Cytogenetically， normal AML represents 40%-60% of AML patients (16-60 years of age) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，17，18\]</u>. Table 34.2 lists the most common chromosomal changes in AML.**

【100】**GENERAL PROGNOSTIC CATEGORIES**

【101】Three chromosomal abnormalities， t(8；21)/RUNXI-RUNXITI， t(15；17)/PML-RARA， and inv(16)/t(16；16)/CBFB-MYHII， are regarded as favorable prognostic factors. AML with abnormali-ties of 3q \[inv(3q)/t(3；3)\]，del(5q)， monosomies of chromosome5 and/or 7 (-5/-7)， t(6；9)， t(6；11)， or complex karyotype are associated with poor prognoses， assuming that t(15；17)，t(8；21)， and inv(16)/t(16；16) were not present 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，15\]</u>. Complex karyotype通用删除1(英):<u>(three or more abnormalities； Figure 34.2)</u> predicts significantly worse outcome compared to cytogenetically normal patients通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，9，15\]</u>. 【107】AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recog-nized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. These patients often present with anemia and normal or increased platelet count. The BM often shows increased small hypolo-bated megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. Patients are often refractory to conventional therapy and have short overall survival. AML with t(3；21) differs from that with inv(3)/t(3；3) by higher frequency of therapy-related disease， lack of megakaryocytic hyperplasia， and shorter survival通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>. The t(3；21)， which disrupts CBF， is typically present in t-AML. AML with t(3；5)/NPMI-MLF1， considered an MDS-related abnormality， has intermediate prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.

Monosomy 5/del(5q) may be seen in all types of AML， but is more common in acute erythroid leukemia (AEL) or AML with minimal differentiation. Monosomy 5/del(5q) and mono-somy 7/del(7q) represent the most common cytogenetic abnor-malities in therapy-related myeloid neoplasm and are strongly associated with prior exposure to alkylating agents 通用删除6(英):<u>\[24\]</u>. 【67】Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a clonal proliferation of immature hematopoietic precursors involving primarily the bone marrow (BM) and blood. The classification of acute leukemia is based on the morphologic， immunophenotypic， cytogenetic， molecular， and clinical data. Generally， acute leukemias are divided into acute lymphoblastic leukemia(ALL) and AML， with a subset of leukemias displaying fea-tures of both \[mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL】\].

【68】AML represents a heterogeneous group of disorders with variable clinical presentation， cellular morphology，immuno-phenotype， chromosomal and molecular changes， therapeu-tic response， and overall prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-15\]</u>. Generally， AML can be defined as a clonal malignancy of transformed multi-potent hematopoietic progenitor cell leading to the accumu-lation of immature cells in the BM， which replace normal elements causing cytopenias and their complications (e.g.， fatigue due to anemia， infections due to granulocytopenia， and bleeding due to thrombocytopenia). The diagnosis and prognosis are most accurately provided by the pretreatment assessment of the morphology， immunophenotype， and most importantly underlying chromosomal and/or molecular aber-rations . The WHO classifies AML based on the genetic， immunophenotypic， and clinical characteristics. AML， not otherwise specified， is further subdivided based on the morphologic criteria similar to prior French-American-

【98】**CYTOGENETICS AND FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIZATION STUDIES IN AML**

Cytogenetic abnormalities in AML at presentation have been identified as one of the most important prognostic factors and have been shown to be independent of age， white blood cell(WBC) counts，andtype of leukemia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，15-18\]</u>. Approximately30% of AML patients carry recurrent chromosomal abnormal-ities associated with different clinical features and prognosis通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，18\]</u>. They include t(15；17) (13%)， t(8；21)(7%)，inv(16)/t(16；16)(5%)， t(6；9) (1%)， t(9；11) (1%)， and inv(3) (1%) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Balanced translocations tend to occur more often in younger patients， whereas del(5q)， del(7q)， +11，+13， and various monosomies|删除0换行|occur more often in older patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Cytogenetic risk sta-tus is a significant factor in predicting response of AML to therapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[19\]</u>， for example， the outcome of patients with APL has substantially improved with the use of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) in combination with chemotherapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[20，21\]</u>. Cytogenetically， normal AML represents 40%-60% of AML patients (16-60 years of age) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，17，18\]</u>. Table 34.2 lists the most common chromosomal changes in AML.**

Older patients (>60 years old) with five or more abnor-malities have extremely poor prognosis. In a study by Farag et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[22\]</u>， no patients aged ≥60 years with five or more abnor-malities were alive at 5 years， despite intensive chemotherapy.

【105】Patients with normal karyotype， nO -Y， del(9q)，t(9；11)， del(20q)， +21， and +22 belong to intermediate prognostic category 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，18，19\]</u>. Patients with t(15；17) treated with stan-dard ATRA and anthracycline-based therapy have favorable prognosis regardless of the additional abnormalities (irrespec-tive of complexity) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，15，18，19\]</u>. Neither complex karyotype nor secondary aberrations affected the outcome of patients with t(8；21)，inv(16)/t(16；16)， or t(9；11) in a series reported by Byrd et al.通用删除6(英):<u>\[9\]</u> and Grimwade et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. In patients with inv(16)， the presence of additional changes， particularly +22， predicted a better outcome \[151.

【106】**CHROMOSOMAL CHANGES**

【107】AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recog-nized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. These patients often present with anemia and normal or increased platelet count. The BM often shows increased small hypolo-bated megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. Patients are often refractory to conventional therapy and have short overall survival. AML with t(3；21) differs from that with inv(3)/t(3；3) by higher frequency of therapy-related disease， lack of megakaryocytic hyperplasia， and shorter survival通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>. The t(3；21)， which disrupts CBF， is typically present in t-AML. AML with t(3；5)/NPMI-MLF1， considered an MDS-related abnormality， has intermediate prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.

Monosomy 5/del(5q) may be seen in all types of AML， but is more common in acute erythroid leukemia (AEL) or AML with minimal differentiation. Monosomy 5/del(5q) and mono-somy 7/del(7q) represent the most common cytogenetic abnor-malities in therapy-related myeloid neoplasm and are strongly associated with prior exposure to alkylating agents 通用删除6(英):<u>\[24\]</u>. AML|删除0换行|with del(5q) or monosomy 5 is associated with poor progno-sis， similar to AML with complex chromosomal abnormali-ties， monosomy 7， and t(9；22)通用删除6(英):<u>\[8，16，18，25，26\]</u>.

【109】Patients with t(6；9) have a dismal prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，27\]</u>. The presence of t(6；9)/DEK-CAN， recognized in the current WHO classification as a separate disease entity， is associ-ated with a very poor prognosis and is generally assigned to the adverse cytogenetic risk group. The poor outcome may relate to a strong association with FLT3-internal tan-dem duplication (ITD) mutations 通用删除6(英):<u>\[27，28\]</u>. In a series by Grimwade et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>， there was some evidence of poorer outcome in patients with t(6；9) compared to normal karyo-type， but this effect was not sufficiently strong to emerge in multivariate analysis.

【110】**Trisomy 8 is the most frequently reported numerical cyto-genetic abnormality in patients with AML. Patients with sole+8 and +8 with additional abnormality other than t(8；21)， inv(16)/t(16；16)， and t(9；11) had significantly inferior overall survival， but not complete remission rate， whereas patients with +8 and a complex karyotype with three or more abnor-malities had significantly inferior complete remission rate and overall survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9\]</u>. The impact of trisomy 8 on AML patients is best predicted by the presence and nature of abnormalities that accompany it 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，29\]</u>.**

【67】Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a clonal proliferation of immature hematopoietic precursors involving primarily the bone marrow (BM) and blood. The classification of acute leukemia is based on the morphologic， immunophenotypic， cytogenetic， molecular， and clinical data. Generally， acute leukemias are divided into acute lymphoblastic leukemia(ALL) and AML， with a subset of leukemias displaying fea-tures of both \[mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL】\].

【68】AML represents a heterogeneous group of disorders with variable clinical presentation， cellular morphology，immuno-phenotype， chromosomal and molecular changes， therapeu-tic response， and overall prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-15\]</u>. Generally， AML can be defined as a clonal malignancy of transformed multi-potent hematopoietic progenitor cell leading to the accumu-lation of immature cells in the BM， which replace normal elements causing cytopenias and their complications (e.g.， fatigue due to anemia， infections due to granulocytopenia， and bleeding due to thrombocytopenia). The diagnosis and prognosis are most accurately provided by the pretreatment assessment of the morphology， immunophenotype， and most importantly underlying chromosomal and/or molecular aber-rations . The WHO classifies AML based on the genetic， immunophenotypic， and clinical characteristics. AML， not otherwise specified， is further subdivided based <mark>on the morphologic criteria similar to prior French-American-

【69】British (FAB) classification .</mark>

【70】**The current WHO classification divides AML into the following four major categories ：**

【71】1\. AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities

【72】**2\. AML with myelodysplasia-related changes**

【73】3\. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms

【74】**4\. AML， not other wise specified**

【75】**AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities comprises several entities：**

【86】**The diagnosis of AML with myelodysplasia-related changes requires one of the following：**

【87】1\. Previoushistory of myelodysplasticsyndrome(MDS) or MDS/myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) and a marrow or blood blast count of >20%

【88】2\. Fifty percent or more of cells in two or more myeloid lineages with dyspoiesis

【89】**3\. Myelodysplasia-relatedcytogeneticabnormality. Cytogenetic abnormalities sufficient to diagnosis AML with myelodysplasia-related changes include the following：**

【90】**· Complex karyotype (three or more chromosomal abnormalities)**

【91】Unbalanced changes： -7 or del(7q)， -5 or del(5q)， i(17q) or t(17p)，-13 or del(13q)， del(11q)， del(12p) or t(12p)， del(9q)， and idic(X)(q13)

【107】AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recog-nized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. These patients often present with anemia and normal or increased platelet count. AML with t(3；21) differs from that with inv(3)/t(3；3) by higher frequency of therapy-related disease， lack of megakaryocytic hyperplasia， and shorter survival通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>. Monosomy 5/del(5q) may be seen in all types of AML， but is more common in acute erythroid leukemia (AEL) or AML with minimal differentiation. Monosomy 5/del(5q) and mono-somy 7/del(7q) represent the most common cytogenetic abnor-malities in therapy-related myeloid neoplasm and are strongly associated with prior exposure to alkylating agents 通用删除6(英):<u>\[24\]</u>. 【67】Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a clonal proliferation of immature hematopoietic precursors involving primarily the bone marrow (BM) and blood. The classification of acute leukemia is based on the morphologic， immunophenotypic， cytogenetic， molecular， and clinical data. Generally， acute leukemias are divided into acute lymphoblastic leukemia(ALL) and AML， with a subset of leukemias displaying fea-tures of both \[mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL】\].

【68】AML represents a heterogeneous group of disorders with variable clinical presentation， cellular morphology，immuno-phenotype， chromosomal and molecular changes， therapeu-tic response， and overall prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-15\]</u>. Generally， AML can be defined as a clonal malignancy of transformed multi-potent hematopoietic progenitor cell leading to the accumu-lation of immature cells in the BM， which replace normal elements causing cytopenias and their complications (e.g.， fatigue due to anemia， infections due to granulocytopenia， and bleeding due to thrombocytopenia). The diagnosis and prognosis are most accurately provided by the pretreatment assessment of the morphology， immunophenotype， and most importantly underlying chromosomal and/or molecular aber-rations . The WHO classifies AML based on the genetic， immunophenotypic， and clinical characteristics. AML， not otherwise specified， is further subdivided based <mark>on the morphologic criteria similar to prior French-American-

【69】British (FAB) classification .</mark>

【106】**CHROMOSOMAL CHANGES**

【107】AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recog-nized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. These patients often present with anemia and normal or increased platelet count. The BM often shows increased small hypolo-bated megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. Patients are often refractory to conventional therapy and have short overall survival. AML with t(3；21) differs from that with inv(3)/t(3；3) by higher frequency of therapy-related disease， lack of megakaryocytic hyperplasia， and shorter survival通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>. The t(3；21)， which disrupts CBF， is typically present in t-AML. AML with t(3；5)/NPMI-MLF1， considered an MDS-related abnormality， has intermediate prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.

Monosomy 5/del(5q) may be seen in all types of AML， but is more common in acute erythroid leukemia (AEL) or AML with minimal differentiation. Monosomy 5/del(5q) and mono-somy 7/del(7q) represent the most common cytogenetic abnor-malities in therapy-related myeloid neoplasm and are strongly associated with prior exposure to alkylating agents 通用删除6(英):<u>\[24\]</u>. AML|删除0换行|with del(5q) or monosomy 5 is associated with poor progno-sis， similar to AML with complex chromosomal abnormali-ties， monosomy 7， and t(9；22)通用删除6(英):<u>\[8，16，18，25，26\]</u>.

【109】Patients with t(6；9) have a dismal prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，27\]</u>. The presence of t(6；9)/DEK-CAN， recognized in the current WHO classification as a separate disease entity， is associ-ated with a very poor prognosis and is generally assigned to the adverse cytogenetic risk group. The poor outcome may relate to a strong association with FLT3-internal tan-dem duplication (ITD) mutations 通用删除6(英):<u>\[27，28\]</u>. In a series by Grimwade et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>， there was some evidence of poorer outcome in patients with t(6；9) compared to normal karyo-type， but this effect was not sufficiently strong to emerge in multivariate analysis.

【110】**Trisomy 8 is the most frequently reported numerical cyto-genetic abnormality in patients with AML. Patients with sole+8 and +8 with additional abnormality other than t(8；21)， inv(16)/t(16；16)， and t(9；11) had significantly inferior overall survival， but not complete remission rate， whereas patients with +8 and a complex karyotype with three or more abnor-malities had significantly inferior complete remission rate and overall survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9\]</u>. The impact of trisomy 8 on AML patients is best predicted by the presence and nature of abnormalities that accompany it 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，29\]</u>.**

Lastly, diaphragmatic weakness leads to respiratory failure, often manifesting first at night (orthopnea, insomnia, night sweats, non-refreshing sleep, morning headaches, etc.).

【21】A 46-year-old male was referred to our center for weakness and suspicion of “motor neuron disease versus motor neuropathy or myopathy,” based on electromyography results and after he had a muscle biopsy which was interpreted as “non-diagnostic.” He reported a 3-year history of progressive difficulties with gait, particularly getting up from chairs, walking upstairs, and also lifting his chainsaw with his arms. Despite his dysesthetic complaints, sensory examination to vibration, proprioception, light touch, and temperature was normal. He had difficulty getting out of a chair but was walking without ataxia.

【13】# Section 1 Differential Diagnosis of Abnormal Symptoms and Signs/86 Weakness, proximal

【14】### 86 Weakness, proximal

【15】Georgios Manousakis and and Glenn Lopate

【16】Neurologic Differential Diagnosis , ed. Alan B. Ettinger and Deborah M. Weisbrot. Published by Cambridge University Press.  Cambridge University Press 2014.

【17】#### Introduction

【18】Proximal weakness is a sign elicited by physical examination. Patients often use the term “weakness” to describe fatigue (asthenia) or abnormal stance and gait resulting from sensory, proprioceptive loss or various central disorders. True weakness usually interferes with specific activities of daily living. For example, patients with shoulder weakness report difficulties combing or washing their hair, or getting objects from high shelves. Patients with biceps or triceps weakness have difficulties pushing or pulling objects respectively. With hip flexion weakness, a patient cannot go upstairs; hip extension weakness leads to problems getting up from a deep-seated chair. Knee extension weakness leads to buckling upon walking and inability to walk downstairs. Hip abductor weakness leads to waddling (Trendelenburg) gait. Paraspinal muscle weakness can lead to head drop (cervical) or bent posture (thoracolumbar). Lastly, diaphragmatic weakness leads to respiratory failure, often manifesting first at night (orthopnea, insomnia, night sweats, non-refreshing sleep, morning headaches, etc.).

【19】The differential diagnosis of proximal weakness is vast and spans disorders of the upper motor neuron (UMN) and peripheral neuromuscular disorders, anywhere from the anterior horn to the muscle itself. Upper motor neuron disorders produce increased tone and reflexes, selective weakness of upper limb extensors and lower limb flexors, and slowing of coordinated movements; for their differential diagnosis, the reader is referred to other chapters in this book. To differentiate between neuromuscular disorders causing proximal weakness, specific elements of the history (e.g. time course, fluctuating versus steady deterioration, presence or absence of pain and sensory symptoms) and the examination (symmetric versus asymmetric weakness, stretch reflexes, involvement of bulbar, extraocular and/or respiratory muscles, associated sensory abnormalities) are critical. Some key clinical features that allow differentiation between each anatomic localization and disease group are outlined in Table 86.1 . The list is not exhaustive; for more details on specific diseases, further reading is suggested at the end of the chapter.

【20】#### Case vignette

【21】A 46-year-old male was referred to our center for weakness and suspicion of “motor neuron disease versus motor neuropathy or myopathy,” based on electromyography results and after he had a muscle biopsy which was interpreted as “non-diagnostic.” He reported a 3-year history of progressive difficulties with gait, particularly getting up from chairs, walking upstairs, and also lifting his chainsaw with his arms. His weakness and fatigue was fluctuating through the day, and was severely exacerbated in the evening. He also reported dry mouth, erectile dysfunction, dysesthesias and paresthesias, and a 30 lb unintentional weight loss over the last year. He was a heavy smoker (> 1 pack per day). Neurologic examination showed normal mental status and normal cranial nerve exam; there was no ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, or facial or bulbar weakness. Motor examination showed normal tone and bulk. There was no muscle atrophy or fasciculations. Symmetric proximal weakness was noted at the deltoids, iliopsoas, quadriceps, all at 4/5 on the Medical Research Council (MRC) scale with normal distal strength. Tendon reflexes were absent, but were markedly facilitated after a brief (10 s) sustained isometric contraction of muscle. Despite his dysesthetic complaints, sensory examination to vibration, proprioception, light touch, and temperature was normal. He had difficulty getting out of a chair but was walking without ataxia.

【46】Obstetric management. Should EA be suspected in a fetus， a thorough anatomic scan should be performed by an expert in order to detect major and/or minor signs possibly leading to the diagnosis of one of the associ-ated anomalies discussed in this chapter. Fetal karyo-typing is also mandatory， because of the high risk of Down syndrome and， to a lesser extent， of trisomy 18.

【47】The delivery should take place in a tertiary referral cen-ter where a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and pediatric surgery are available. 【48】Postnatal therapy. This obviously consists of surgical reconstruction of the esophagus and may be carried out in a single intervention or require a two-stage pro-cedure， according to the length of the atretic segment.

【49】The primary repair of the EA-TE fistula abnormality is considered the preferred surgical option and achieves the best results 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. The fistula is divided a few milli-meters distal to its entry in the trachea， and the defect is closed with interrupted sutures. In a second step， the proximal blind end of the esophagus is mobilized suf-ficiently to allow a tension-free anastomosis with the lower esophageal segment 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. In repairs with tension at the level of the anastomosis， the infant would be par-alyzed for five days to prevent swallowing and upward movements of the proximal esophagus. Infants with isolated EA usually have a long gap between the ends of the esophagus precluding early primary repair. The infant would be brought to the operating theater for the creation of a feeding gastrostomy and an assessment of the gap between the ends of the esophagus. Options for treatment beyond this stage include attempted delayed primary anastomosis at around six to eight weeks， or substitution of the esophagus with stomach， small bowel， or large bowel in later infancy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>.

【66】**Pharmacology for the Chiropractor：How Medications May Affect Patient Presentation and Management Outcomes**

【67】Although a heated debate may ensue when asked about the inclusion of medication prescription to the scope of practice ofthe chiropractor， it is often evident that a base-line of pharmacology knowledge is in fact realistic and nec-essary to fulfill the role of a portal-of-entry physician. Many patients are taking medications prior to entering the chiropractor's office. As a result， a basic knowledge of common prescribed and over-the-counter (OTC)med-ication is useful. Following are some important reasons：

【68】The patient often asks questions regarding the side effects of his/her medication.

【69】The patient rnay present with signs or symptoms di-rectly related to a side effect of a medication or from lack of compliance in taking a prescribed medication.

【70】The medication taken by the patient is used for the condition or symptoms the chiropractor wishes to address.

【71】In a review of a patient's medical history， it is im-portant to determine current and past medications Even if the patient has forgotten why the medica-tion was prescribed， a basic knowledge of com-monly prescribed drugs will often offer a clue.

【72】Events may have changed in the patient’s life that may influence the effect of medication. For exam-ple， certain foods， alcohol， fever， or iilness may ef-fectively increase or decrease the effects of the available drug.

【73】If laboratory studies are performed， drug interac-tions may have a significant effect on the results.

【74】Here are just a few practical examples：

【75】A patient has a sense of difficulty breathing (sense of tightess) and multiple other complaints that range from musculoskeletal aches and pains to headaches. The patient is taking alprazolam (Xanax)， which is often prescribed for anxicty， as an adjunct with antidepressants， or simply as a sleep inducer. Anxiety may have an effect on blood pressure，re-sponse to questions， and general well-being. Depression certainly may have an effect on patient complaints and their perceived response to care. Lack of sleep may have an effect on patient pres-entation as well.

【76】Another patient who takes lithium has a remarkable response one time to your care of mid-thoracic pain， yet another time is angry with you or simply nonresponsive. Knowing that lithium is used for _ma_ ISIVE， KO manje depression may help in explaining the range of response if， in fact， the patient is not consistently taking his/her me101dication.

A patient who has had chronic pain is taking large daily doses of naprosyn. The patient is complain-ing of constant heartburn and epigastric pain in ad-dition to tinnitus. Understanding that naprosyn and similar medications are potentially ototoxic at|删除0换行|high and prolonged use， and that these medications may lead to ulcers， primarily gastric ulcers， may help to explain the patient's symptoms and direct the appropriate course of management.

【78】A patient is taking Lasix for congestive heart fail-ure. He is starting to complain of some cramping and muscle weakness. When a lab is ordered， the pa-tient's serum potassium level is very low. Knowing the Lasix is non-potassium sparing helps in the ex-planation and results in an immediate referral to the prescribing physician with a suggestion that potassium supplementation is requisite.

【79】A patient with migraine headaches seemed to re-spond to chiropractic care， but when on vacation was in an area where he/she did not have a chiroprac-tor available. The patient took sumatriptin pre-scribed by her physician. It helped， but now， three days later， her headache is hack， and worse. Knowing that many medications prescribed for migraine may be the cause of a “rebound migraine”is helpful in making decisions about management and explains why this wonld aceur.

【80】A patient is taking coumadin because of deep vein thrombosis discovered one month ago. You are considering adjusting the low back with a side-posture adjustment. Understanding that coumadin is an anti-coagulant may have an affect on the de-gree of force used in the adjustment or whether an-other technique will be used during the time the patient is on the medication.

【81】A patient who was diagnosed with temporal arteri-tis is on a course of corticosteroids for 6 months. During that time the patient has mid-thoracic pain that seems fairly severe. Knowing that the patient is on corticosteroids would certainly warrant tak-ing x-rays to determine whether a compression fracture was the cause and may explain why if found. If not found， there would still be a caution against any position or exercise that would cause loaded flexion， including while adjusting， due to the os-teopenic affect of long-term corticosteroid use.

【82】Additionally， the patient is often taking many med-ications. With the senior patient， it is not uncommon to have a obtained each medication from a different physi-cian and each physician is unaware of the other’s pre-scription. As a result， unforeseen interactions may occur. The chiropractor is in the advantageous position of be-ing able to ascertain the complete picture of medications the patient is taking because the patient assumes the chi-ropractor is not involved in the regulation of these drugs.

【83】The caveat for the chiropractor is that no advice re-garding taking or withdrawing from， or increasing or de-creasing dosage can be given without violating state scope of practice laws. IIowever， when a problem is suspected or recognized， it is imperative that the chiropractor either send the patient back to the prescribing physician with in-formative questions or contact the prescribing physician to discuss the individual patient. It is extremely important to recognize that if a medication is stopped suddenly or the dose is decreased，a rebound effect or other reactions may occur that are potentially lethal. For example， sudden with-drawal of seizure mcdication may lead to status epilepticus(i.e.， a seizure that continues and may lead to death).

【84】It is important to understand that although a drug may have been developed for a specific system or condition， the same medication may be used as the primary or alter-native drug for another condition. For example， although antihypertensive and antidepressant medications were de-signed for the associated condition， these medications are also used in the treatment of headache. Antihypertensive medications may also be used in the treatment of some cardiac disorders or reflex sympathetic conditions.

【85】Table A-1 and Table A-2 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(page 1019)</u></u> list common ex-amples of medications based on generic and product name， and lists common side effects. There are many handbooks with far more extensive information on these and other medications. This table is intended to serve as a quick-reference guide. Further information should be sought from more comprehensive sources available.

【86】Some general principles of pharmacology allow a bet-ter understanding of prescribing practices. The primary concern is prescribing the optimal amount of medica-tion to be effective， but is not toxic or wrought with side effects.This dosage varies for several important reasons：

【87】_7_ The amount of active drug in the body is deter-mined by its metabolism in the liver and clearance from the kidneys. Obviously， liver or kidney dis-ease may alter the available amount of drug in the system. Some special considerations include the infant and the elderly for whom function of both or-gans is decreased compared to an average adult.

【88】The available amount of medication will vary with processes such as fever， other drugs， and metabolic conditions.

【89】Special concerns apply to particular groups， in-cluding pregnant females， the immunocompro-mised， the elderly， and infants. Some medications should not be used during pregnancy， and medica-tion dosages for the other groups will vary based upon that group's specific factors.

【66】**Pharmacology for the Chiropractor：How Medications May Affect Patient Presentation and Management Outcomes**

【67】Although a heated debate may ensue when asked about the inclusion of medication prescription to the scope of practice ofthe chiropractor， it is often evident that a base-line of pharmacology knowledge is in fact realistic and nec-essary to fulfill the role of a portal-of-entry physician. Many patients are taking medications prior to entering the chiropractor's office. As a result， a basic knowledge of common prescribed and over-the-counter (OTC)med-ication is useful. Following are some important reasons：

【68】The patient often asks questions regarding the side effects of his/her medication.

【69】The patient rnay present with signs or symptoms di-rectly related to a side effect of a medication or from lack of compliance in taking a prescribed medication.

【70】The medication taken by the patient is used for the condition or symptoms the chiropractor wishes to address.

【71】In a review of a patient's medical history， it is im-portant to determine current and past medications Even if the patient has forgotten why the medica-tion was prescribed， a basic knowledge of com-monly prescribed drugs will often offer a clue.

【72】Events may have changed in the patient’s life that may influence the effect of medication. For exam-ple， certain foods， alcohol， fever， or iilness may ef-fectively increase or decrease the effects of the available drug.

【73】If laboratory studies are performed， drug interac-tions may have a significant effect on the results.

【74】Here are just a few practical examples：

【75】A patient has a sense of difficulty breathing (sense of tightess) and multiple other complaints that range from musculoskeletal aches and pains to headaches. The patient is taking alprazolam (Xanax)， which is often prescribed for anxicty， as an adjunct with antidepressants， or simply as a sleep inducer. Anxiety may have an effect on blood pressure，re-sponse to questions， and general well-being. Depression certainly may have an effect on patient complaints and their perceived response to care. Lack of sleep may have an effect on patient pres-entation as well.

【76】Another patient who takes lithium has a remarkable response one time to your care of mid-thoracic pain， yet another time is angry with you or simply nonresponsive. Knowing that lithium is used for _ma_ ISIVE， KO manje depression may help in explaining the range of response if， in fact， the patient is not consistently taking his/her me101dication.

A patient who has had chronic pain is taking large daily doses of naprosyn. The patient is complain-ing of constant heartburn and epigastric pain in ad-dition to tinnitus. Understanding that naprosyn and similar medications are potentially ototoxic at|删除0换行|high and prolonged use， and that these medications may lead to ulcers， primarily gastric ulcers， may help to explain the patient's symptoms and direct the appropriate course of management.

【78】A patient is taking Lasix for congestive heart fail-ure. He is starting to complain of some cramping and muscle weakness. When a lab is ordered， the pa-tient's serum potassium level is very low. Knowing the Lasix is non-potassium sparing helps in the ex-planation and results in an immediate referral to the prescribing physician with a suggestion that potassium supplementation is requisite.

【79】A patient with migraine headaches seemed to re-spond to chiropractic care， but when on vacation was in an area where he/she did not have a chiroprac-tor available. The patient took sumatriptin pre-scribed by her physician. It helped， but now， three days later， her headache is hack， and worse. Knowing that many medications prescribed for migraine may be the cause of a “rebound migraine”is helpful in making decisions about management and explains why this wonld aceur.

【80】A patient is taking coumadin because of deep vein thrombosis discovered one month ago. You are considering adjusting the low back with a side-posture adjustment. Understanding that coumadin is an anti-coagulant may have an affect on the de-gree of force used in the adjustment or whether an-other technique will be used during the time the patient is on the medication.

【81】A patient who was diagnosed with temporal arteri-tis is on a course of corticosteroids for 6 months. During that time the patient has mid-thoracic pain that seems fairly severe. Knowing that the patient is on corticosteroids would certainly warrant tak-ing x-rays to determine whether a compression fracture was the cause and may explain why if found. If not found， there would still be a caution against any position or exercise that would cause loaded flexion， including while adjusting， due to the os-teopenic affect of long-term corticosteroid use.

【82】Additionally， the patient is often taking many med-ications. With the senior patient， it is not uncommon to have a obtained each medication from a different physi-cian and each physician is unaware of the other’s pre-scription. As a result， unforeseen interactions may occur. The chiropractor is in the advantageous position of be-ing able to ascertain the complete picture of medications the patient is taking because the patient assumes the chi-ropractor is not involved in the regulation of these drugs.

【83】The caveat for the chiropractor is that no advice re-garding taking or withdrawing from， or increasing or de-creasing dosage can be given without violating state scope of practice laws. IIowever， when a problem is suspected or recognized， it is imperative that the chiropractor either send the patient back to the prescribing physician with in-formative questions or contact the prescribing physician to discuss the individual patient. It is extremely important to recognize that if a medication is stopped suddenly or the dose is decreased，a rebound effect or other reactions may occur that are potentially lethal. For example， sudden with-drawal of seizure mcdication may lead to status epilepticus(i.e.， a seizure that continues and may lead to death).

【84】It is important to understand that although a drug may have been developed for a specific system or condition， the same medication may be used as the primary or alter-native drug for another condition. For example， although antihypertensive and antidepressant medications were de-signed for the associated condition， these medications are also used in the treatment of headache. Antihypertensive medications may also be used in the treatment of some cardiac disorders or reflex sympathetic conditions.

Anxiety may have an effect on blood pressure，re-sponse to questions， and general well-being. Depression certainly may have an effect on patient complaints and their perceived response to care. Lack of sleep may have an effect on patient pres-entation as well.

【76】Another patient who takes lithium has a remarkable response one time to your care of mid-thoracic pain， yet another time is angry with you or simply nonresponsive. Knowing that lithium is used for _ma_ ISIVE， KO manje depression may help in explaining the range of response if， in fact， the patient is not consistently taking his/her me101dication.

A patient who has had chronic pain is taking large daily doses of naprosyn. The patient is complain-ing of constant heartburn and epigastric pain in ad-dition to tinnitus. Understanding that naprosyn and similar medications are potentially ototoxic at|删除0换行|high and prolonged use， and that these medications may lead to ulcers， primarily gastric ulcers， may help to explain the patient's symptoms and direct the appropriate course of management.

【78】A patient is taking Lasix for congestive heart fail-ure. He is starting to complain of some cramping and muscle weakness. When a lab is ordered， the pa-tient's serum potassium level is very low. Knowing the Lasix is non-potassium sparing helps in the ex-planation and results in an immediate referral to the prescribing physician with a suggestion that potassium supplementation is requisite.

【79】A patient with migraine headaches seemed to re-spond to chiropractic care， but when on vacation was in an area where he/she did not have a chiroprac-tor available. The patient took sumatriptin pre-scribed by her physician. It helped， but now， three days later， her headache is hack， and worse. Knowing that many medications prescribed for migraine may be the cause of a “rebound migraine”is helpful in making decisions about management and explains why this wonld aceur.

【80】A patient is taking coumadin because of deep vein thrombosis discovered one month ago. You are considering adjusting the low back with a side-posture adjustment. Understanding that coumadin is an anti-coagulant may have an affect on the de-gree of force used in the adjustment or whether an-other technique will be used during the time the patient is on the medication.

【81】A patient who was diagnosed with temporal arteri-tis is on a course of corticosteroids for 6 months. During that time the patient has mid-thoracic pain that seems fairly severe. Knowing that the patient is on corticosteroids would certainly warrant tak-ing x-rays to determine whether a compression fracture was the cause and may explain why if found. If not found， there would still be a caution against any position or exercise that would cause loaded flexion， including while adjusting， due to the os-teopenic affect of long-term corticosteroid use.

【82】Additionally， the patient is often taking many med-ications. With the senior patient， it is not uncommon to have a obtained each medication from a different physi-cian and each physician is unaware of the other’s pre-scription. As a result， unforeseen interactions may occur. The chiropractor is in the advantageous position of be-ing able to ascertain the complete picture of medications the patient is taking because the patient assumes the chi-ropractor is not involved in the regulation of these drugs.

【83】The caveat for the chiropractor is that no advice re-garding taking or withdrawing from， or increasing or de-creasing dosage can be given without violating state scope of practice laws. IIowever， when a problem is suspected or recognized， it is imperative that the chiropractor either send the patient back to the prescribing physician with in-formative questions or contact the prescribing physician to discuss the individual patient. It is extremely important to recognize that if a medication is stopped suddenly or the dose is decreased，a rebound effect or other reactions may occur that are potentially lethal. For example， sudden with-drawal of seizure mcdication may lead to status epilepticus(i.e.， a seizure that continues and may lead to death).

【84】It is important to understand that although a drug may have been developed for a specific system or condition， the same medication may be used as the primary or alter-native drug for another condition. For example， although antihypertensive and antidepressant medications were de-signed for the associated condition， these medications are also used in the treatment of headache. Antihypertensive medications may also be used in the treatment of some cardiac disorders or reflex sympathetic conditions.

【85】Table A-1 and Table A-2 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(page 1019)</u></u> list common ex-amples of medications based on generic and product name， and lists common side effects. Further information should be sought from more comprehensive sources available.

【86】Some general principles of pharmacology allow a bet-ter understanding of prescribing practices. The primary concern is prescribing the optimal amount of medica-tion to be effective， but is not toxic or wrought with side effects.This dosage varies for several important reasons：

【87】_7_ The amount of active drug in the body is deter-mined by its metabolism in the liver and clearance from the kidneys. Obviously， liver or kidney dis-ease may alter the available amount of drug in the system. Some special considerations include the infant and the elderly for whom function of both or-gans is decreased compared to an average adult.

【88】The available amount of medication will vary with processes such as fever， other drugs， and metabolic conditions.

【89】Special concerns apply to particular groups， in-cluding pregnant females， the immunocompro-mised， the elderly， and infants. Some medications should not be used during pregnancy， and medica-tion dosages for the other groups will vary based upon that group's specific factors.
