【0】nt is experiencing problem drug use. The following are among the most commonly utilized and widely accepted assessment tools.

【1】The CAGE 删除1:<u>(Mayfield， McLeod，& Hall， 1994)</u> is a brief screening approach developed by John Ewing， founding director of the Bowles Center for Alcohol Studies， University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. It is an internationally used screening instrument for identifying alcoholics and other substance abus-ers. It is particularly popular with primary caregivers. CAGE has been translated into several languages. The patient is asked four questions \[emphasis added\]：

【2】(1) Have you ever felt you ought to Cut down your drinking (or drug use)?

【3】(2) Have people Annoyed you by criticizing your drinking (or drug use)?

(4) Have you had a drink (or used drugs) first thing in the morning (Eye opener) to steady your nerves or get rid of a hangover? Affirmative answers to two or more ques-tions constitute a positive screen and should prompt further history. There is also a version 删除1:<u>(CAGE-AID； Brown & Rounds， 1995)</u> adapted to include drugs.

【5】The Michigan Alcoholism Screening Test 删除1:<u>(MAST； Selzer， 1971)</u> is a self-report screening instrument that may be given to a patient initially or in follow-up to another screening test. Its brevity makes it useful as an outpatient tool. The questions in the 24-item scale address a variety of behaviors and feelings and can be answered with a simple “yes”or “no.” A short-form is also avail-able. Both versions of the MAST have shown excellent internal consistency(Cronbach’s alpha=.95 for original and .93 for short-form) and known-groups validity 删除1:<u>(Corcoran & Fischer， 2013)</u>.

【6】The Drug Abuse Screening Test 删除1:<u>(DAST； Skinner， 1983)</u> is a brief instrument that evaluates drug use and abuse. A short-form and adolescent version are also available. This 20-item questionnaire has a similar structure to the MAST but assesses problems common to drug use/abuse. Excellent reliability has been reported (Cronbach’s alpha=.92) as well as good discriminant and concurrent validity 删除1:<u>(Corcoran & Fischer， 2013)</u>. CO1

【7】Another set of self-report instruments， the Substance Abuse Subtle Screening Inventory (SASSI)， includes versions for adults 删除1:<u>(SASSI-3； Miller， 1985，1999)</u>删除1:<u>(SASSI Institute，2013)</u> and for teenagers from ages 12 to 18 删除1:<u>(SASSI-A2； Miller& Lazowski，2001)</u> 删除1:<u>(SASSI Institute， 2013)</u>. These instru WSK1，20ments are touted asbeing able to diagnose substance use problems through examining patterns of“subtle”indicators (e.g.， defensiveness) even when the respondent lies about his or her use of substances. The SASSI was developed almost 30 years ago and since has been empirically validated by numerous research studies attesting to its effectiveness as an as sSeesssment instrument to diagnose SUDs. For example， the SASSI-3 has excellent reliability with test-retest coefficients ranging from.92 to 1.00 and an alpha of .93 删除1:<u>(Lazowski， Miller， Boye， & Miller， 1998)</u>. The SASSI-3 has been used in residential treatment centers， psychiatric hospitals， sexual offender programs， and vocational rehabilitation programs. It has also been validated with clients who have a history with the criminal justice system. Although some have questioned the validity of the SASSI-3's subtle scales， oth-ers support their sensitivity and that of the whole scale in general， alluding to its predictive accuracy as being the reason why this scale is the most frequently used commercial screening instrument among addictions counselors 删除1:<u>(Laux， Pi-azza， Salyers， & Roseman， 2012)</u>.

【8】The best evaluative tool for withdrawal symptoms is the Clinical Insti-tute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol/Drugs 删除1:<u>(CIWA-AD； Sullivan， Sykora， Schneiderman， Naranjo， & Sellers， 1989)</u>. The CIWA-AD is an 8-item scale for clinical quantification of the severity of Withdrawal Syndrome. It is a reliable， brief， uncomplicated， and clinically useful scale that can also be used to monitor response to treatment.

【9】The general approach to assessment with a client contemplating or entering treatment is broadly focused (because substance-related problems impact most psychosocial areas) and based on semistructured interviews. The most com-monly used of these semistructured interviews was developed under the aus-pices of the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) and the NIDA. The adult version， the Addiction Severity Index (ASI-5； McLellan

Cengage Learning reserves the right to rerove additional content at any time if subsequent rights restrictions require it|删除0换行|et al.， 1992) is in the public domain and can be administered as a self-report scale as well as a semistructured interview. It consists of approximately 200items divided into 7 potential problem areas and generally takes 50 to 75 min-utes for administration. The instrument has been the subject of many psycho-metric studies and has proven reliable and valid . The ASI has also been used as an outcome measure in clinical research. Software is being developed to assist in the scoring and reporting of results with this instrument. It appears that there will be continued development and improvement of the current version as new research and knowledge is made available.

【11】Also in the public domain， the Teen Addiction Severity Index 删除1:<u>(T-ASI； Kaminer， Bukstein， & Tarter， 1991)</u> is recommended only as a semistructured interview. Based on 133 items divided into 7 subscales， the T-ASI generally takes between 20 and 45 minutes to administer by a trained mental health prac-titioner. Because it is a more recently developed instrument， far fewer studies have demonstrated its psychometric properties， but initial work suggests it is both reliable and valid 删除1:<u>(Kaminer et al.， 1991； Kaminer， Wagner， Plummer， &Seifer， 1993)</u>. A Spanish version is also available.

【12】The DSM-5 taskforce has included a 15-item online measure that may be useful in the assessment of substance use (including prescription medica-tion) available in three versions (adult， parent/guardian and child) that is an adaptation of the NIDA-Modified ASSIST. For more information please re-fer to the APA website http：//www.psychiatry.org/practice/dsm/dsmS/online-assessment-measures(tab under Level 2-Substance Use for Adult/Children Age11-17/Parent/Guardian of Child Age 6-17).

【13】**Emergency Considerations**

【14】Once substance dependence is suspected， a practitioner must assess a client for those physical withdrawal symptoms that can be life threatening. Many practitioners are surprised to learn that alcohol withdrawal is one of the most potentially fatal detoxifications， while cocaine withdrawal (although very un-comfortable) is virtually harmless.

【15】Substance use also causes a wide variety of medical symptoms and diseases. Common medical symptoms of substance use include vitamin deficiency， mal-nutrition， dyspepsia， upper gastrointestinal problems， peptic ulcer， hepatitis， pancreatitis， hypertension， new-onset arrhythmia， cardiomyopathy， seizures， peripheral neuropathy， and AIDS. From this list， it should be obvious that prompt medical referrals should be made even when no immediate withdrawal risks are present.

【16】Substance use can also be associated with the following behavioral， emo-tional， and cognitive problems： stress， insomnia， anxiety， depression， acute psychotic states， impaired cognition， and violent behavior. Further， substance use can generate a myriad of associated social problems. Substance users are at high risk for marital and family problems， legal difficulties， loss of employ-ment， and financial deterioration. Clearly， broad-ranged assessment to screen for comorbid mental disorders and/or impending psychosocial problems that could greatly complicate recovery is warranted.

【17】Finally， suicide risk is frequently present in substance-using clients， particu-larly as health and psychosocial deterioration is present. Even with clients who

Cengage Learning reserves the right to rerove additional content at any time if subsequent rights restrictions require it|删除0换行|do not really warrant a substance use or related diagnosis， intoxication can enhance risk. Careful screening for self-destructive thoughts and/or impulses is imperative with this population.

【19】Cultural Considerations

【20】Substance use and related disorders exist worldwide； however， cultural values about substance use vary across cultures and within cultures. The applicability COS of SUDs across cultures has shown differences in assessment instrument items， diagnostic criteria， and even the very broad concepts used to make diagnoses. Although these differences may be due to translation problems， such as a lack of words with similar meaning or when a concept may overlap， often this is not the case 删除1:<u>(Room， Janca， Bennett， Schmidt，& Sartorius， 1996)</u>. Some studies have identified problems with concepts that are integral to diagnosis but fluctu-ate across cultures such as what constitutes a problem in the first place or the validity of a cause and effect relationship with substance use 删除1:<u>(Schmidt & Room，1999)</u>. To understand how culture may influence values one need only look at the changing legality of marijuana within the United States. Although the con-cepts surrounding what constitutes symptoms or problems defining substance use may vary by culture， the stigma associated with this diagnosis appears to be universal(Room. 2006. iversal删除1:<u>(Koom，2006)</u>.

【21】Roughly 20.6 million Americans (of the total population 12 years of age and older) were classified as abusing or being dependent on a substance in 2011删除1:<u>(SAMHSA，2012b)</u>. Within the United States， national data from NIAAA， the SAMHSA as well as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) have shown ethno-racial differences in terms of alcohol use disorders and treatment. However， it is important to note that intra-ethnic and racial group differences also exist (e.g.， by gender role， by age， by subgroup) and generalities to any ethnic or racial group should be considered cautiously. Data show that Whites and Native Americans have a greater risk than other ethnic groups in terms of alcohol use disorders. However， once dependence has begun， Blacks and Hispanics have a higher risk of chronic dependency. Furthermore， the impact of alcohol-use problems appears to be greater for minority ethnic and racial groups. Explanation of these differences or their causation is complex as well as limited and warrants further study beyond those currently acknowledged from immigration/acculturation， racial/ethnic discrimination， social economic status， and biological/genetic factors 删除1:<u>(Chartier & Caetano， 2010)</u>.

【22】In terms of marijuana use disorders， African Americans had greatest risk in comparison to other racial and ethnic groups. Comorbid alcohol and marijuana use disorders were highest for African Americans and relatively equal among Whites and Hispanics 删除1:<u>(Pacek， Malcolm， & Martins， 2012)</u>. Furthermore， in-dividuals with a lifetime diagnosis for any mental illness had an elevated pos-sibility for a SUD as well as faster escalation from substance use to a SUD for a range of substances 删除1:<u>(Lev-Ran， Imtiaz， Rehm， & Le Foll， 2013)</u>. Although a significant body of research exists noting the varied levels of drug involve-ment by ethnic and racial groups， the literature is flawed in that it often fails to consider contextual variables such as poverty， gender， and acculturation. The stressors of poverty， joblessness， homelessness， and mental illness often contrib-u1te to SUDs regardless of racial or ethnic identity. It is important to note that

Due to electronic rights， sore third party content may be suppressed fror the eBook and/or eChapter\[s)** **Editorial review has deerned that any suppressed content does not raterially affect the overall learning experience. Cengage Learning reserves the right to rerove additional content at any time if subsequent rights restrictions require it|删除0换行|many myths exist with regard to ethnicity， race and alcohol/drug use， abuse and dependency.**

【24】Differences have also been reported in other sociodemographic areas as well， which include gender and age. Males have consistently demonstrated higher rates of substance use and dependency in both the general population and treatment samples 删除1:<u>(Greenfield， Back， Lawson， & Brady，2010)</u>. Addition-ally， in terms of the prevalence of a SUD and lifetime exposure to substances， males demonstrate higher rates of alcohol and cannabis dependence and fe-males， amphetamine dependence 删除1:<u>(Lev-Ran， Le Strat， Imtiaz， Rehm， & LeFoll，2013)</u>. In terms of alcohol use disorders， women have historically reported lower rates than men； however， this gender gap is tightening possibly due to the growth and earlier age of first time use among young women (aged 10 to14 years). Also， women tend to seek help for their alcohol use problems pre-dominantly from primary care physicians and usually for another mental health problem such as depression， whereas men tend to seek help specifically for their alcohol use via specialty treatment centers 删除1:<u>(Greenfield， 2002)</u>. Although some studies report that women tend to develop alcohol-related diseases faster than men 删除1:<u>(Diehl et al.， 2007； Greenfield， 2002； Zilberman， Tavares， & el-Guebaly，2003)</u>， others do not support this premise and report that women experience a more rapid progression to treatment 删除1:<u>(Lewis & Nixon， 2013)</u>. Despite these statistics， practitioners are cautioned to screen both sexes carefully for sub-stance use-related problems. The assumption that women are less prone to such difficulties can inhibit diagnosis and treatment.

【25】Data from the National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions (NESARC； 2001-2002) showed that over a one-year period， men and women had similar rates of tobacco use only， alcohol use only， and nico-tine dependence only. Men were more likely than women to use both alcohol and tobacco， have an alcohol use disorder only (based on DSM-IV criteria\[APA， 2000\])， and have a comorbid disorder. Women were more likely to abstain from both alcohol and tobacco use. However， the correlation between alcohol dependence and nicotine dependence was high for both genders 删除1:<u>(Falk et al.， 2006)</u>.

【26】Furthermore， the strongest association for tobacco use was found among individuals with mental illness. According to the NSDUH using data 删除1:<u>(from2009 to 2011)</u> among daily lifetime smokers for all ages and both genders， a _a1_ strong association was found between mental illness (36.1 with a mental illness versus 21.4 percent without) and cigarette use among daily lifetime smokers for all ages and genders 删除1:<u>(SAMHSA，2013)</u>.

【27】Gender differences have also been reported in individuals seeking treat-ment for problem gambling with men reporting earlier onset and more impul-sivity and attention seeking symptoms and women reporting later onset but with faster dependency and more anxiety/depressive symptoms 删除1:<u>(Echeburúa， Gonzalez-Ortega， Corral，& Polo-Lopez，2011)</u>.

【28】Age is another important demographic impacting substance use and re-lated disorders. Adolescence has long been recognized as a crucial period of development， and sadly， research shows that this applies to the origination of SUDs. Most adults who met the criteria for a SUD started using the substance during their youth 删除1:<u>(Freshman， 2014)</u>. Data from the most recent release (2010) of Monitoring the Future (MTF)， an annual， anonymous survey of alcohol， cigarette and illicit drug use across a nationally representative samples of 8th，

Cengage Learning reserves the right to rerove additional content at any time if subsequent rights restrictions require it|删除0换行|10th， and 12th graders funded by the National Institute of Drug Abuse (NIDA) showed an increase in the overall rate of illicit drug use for all grades studied删除1:<u>(Merikangas & McClair，2012)</u>. Alcohol continues to be the primary substance of choice used by America’s youth， greater than either tobacco or illicit drugs. More telling， early onset substance use in adolescence is a risk factor for the development of a SUD. Of particular interest is the finding that movement from cannabis use to abuse and dependence appears to happen at a faster rate than alcohol disorders or nicotine dependence 删除1:<u>(Behrendt， Wittchen， Hofler， Lieb， Beesdo， et al.， 2009)</u>. This is especially troublesome as other studies re-port that marijuana is the most used illicit drug among adolescents 删除1:<u>(Murphey， Barry， Vaughn， Guzman， & Terzian， 2013)</u>. In terms of culture and its impact on substance use among adolescents， recent studies indicate that in addition to the at-risk individual and their peer relationships， the entire school commu-nity should be targeted for prevention programs 删除1:<u>(Kristjansson， Sigfusdottir， &Allegrante，2013)</u>.

【30】Another troubling statistic is the growing prevalence of alcohol and drug abuse/misuse among the elderly in the United States. A conservative estimate of the number of adults aged 50 or older with a SUD is expected to reach 5.7million by the year 2020 删除1:<u>(Han， Gfroerer， Colliver， & Penne， 2009)</u>. Moreover， declining response rates have been reported for older Americans in national surveys on drug use 删除1:<u>(Murphy， Schwerin， Eyerman， & Kennet， 2008)</u>， which may indicate even higher levels of substance use for this older adult population. Although alcohol is the primary drug of choice with older adults， illicit drug use is growing rapidly within this population. According to the 2012 NSDUH， the number of adults aged 50 or older who had used an illicit drug during the past year was 7 million 删除1:<u>(SAMSHA， 2012b)</u>. Many older adults are prescribed psychoactive medications (25%) that may put them at risk for drug abuse and dependency. Also， a majority of this elderly population (90%) are users of pre-scription and over-the-counter medications that may have adverse effects and drug interactions when used with alcohol or illicit drugs 删除1:<u>(Han et al.， 2009)</u>. Furthermore， this older population is unlikely to get diagnosed or seek treat-ment services 删除1:<u>(Boeri & Tyndall，2012)</u>.

【31】The factors that lead to substance use and dependency in older adults dif-fer from their younger cohorts. Also， with age an individual's sensitivity to alcohol and other substances may increase due to physiological changes and variations in tolerance 删除1:<u>(Wang & Andrade， 2013)</u>. Older adults may develop SUDs at lower consumption levels and often do

From this list， it should be obvious that prompt medical referrals should be made even when no immediate withdrawal risks are present.

It is an important exercise, as it trains the Qigong doctor to harmonize any spiritual or energetic activity with the physical body, thus allowing the doctor to work confidently within the physical, energetic, and spiritual realms.

【1】By systematically focusing thoughts and intentions onto the three bodies, the imagination and feeling can be cultivated to the degree that the Yuan Shen becomes integrated with the physical, energetic, and spirit bodies.

【2】•    Begin this exercise through physical motion (in ancient China, the practice of a martial arts form, a Qigong exercise, or simple walking would suffice).

【3】•    While performing a physical movement such as walking, do not focus your attention and thoughts on your feet walking; instead, experience the spiritual feet of your spiritual body walking, which in turn moves the energetic feet of your energetic body, and finally moves the feet of your physical body.

【4】•    Expand your attention to include all of the areas of your three energetic bodies. When you are able to maintain this energetic state for at least ten minutes, proceed to the next Shengong meditation.

【5】Exercise meditation #4: Energizing the Sense Organs of the Three Bodies

【6】This Shengong meditation is practiced in order to allow the Qigong doctor to increase his or her sensory perceptional abilities on all three energetic levels.

【7】•    Begin by performing the One Through Ten Meditation and Three Invocations . After the third invocation, place your attention on the divine white light vibrating and resonating within the Lower Dantian.

【8】•    Focus your concentration on leading divine white light energy up the Taiji Pole and into the center of the Upper Dantian . Imagine and feel the divine white light radiating outward through the various nine chambers of the Upper Dantian .

【9】•    Spiritual Eyes: Focus and place your attention onto your eyes. Imagine that your sense of sight exists, not because your physical eyes can see, but because your spirit perceives everything with the help of the divine light radiating within your energetic eyes and physical eyes. Meditate on this concept to the degree that your spirit begins to perceive and see everything through your physical eyes.

【10】•    Spiritual Ears: Focus and place your attention onto your ears. Imagine that your sense of hearing exists, not because your physical ears can hear, but because your spirit perceives sound waves with the help of the divine light radiating within your energetic ears and physical ears. Meditate on this concept to the degree that your spirit begins to perceive and hear everything through your physical ears.

【11】•    Spiritual Feeling: Focus and place your attention on your body. Imagine that your sense of feeling is not because your physical tissues can feel, but because your spirit perceives objects and sensations with the help of the divine light radiating within your energetic body and physical body. Meditate on this concept to the degree that your spirit begins to feel objects and sensations (coldness, warmth) through your physical tissues.

【12】•    After several minutes, imagine and feel the divine white light returning to the Lower Dantian. End this meditation by performing three "Pulling Down the Heavens" exercises.

【13】Caution: It is important to end this meditation by returning the divine healing white light into the Lower Dantian and rooting it away from the eyes and ears. Otherwise, the constant bombardment of energetic and spiritual perceptions stimulating the conscious mind may cause psychological problems and Qi Deviations, especially if the doctor has not prepared for this state or level of receptivity.

【14】The Three Forms of Metaphysical Healing

【15】The ancient Chinese divided metaphysical healing into three forms of manifestations; Energetic Healing, Spiritual Healing, and Divine Healing. Generally, all three forms of healing take place when treating a patient, and are described as follows:

【16】•    Energetic Healing: This type of healing involves the doctor's ability to emit and project Qi into the patient. Qi is induced through specific tissue, point, channel, or organ manipulations in order to initiate energetic healing. Specific herbal formulas are also included in this category, as the combined energetic properties and influence of the herbs initiate healing within the body's tissues.

【17】•    Spiritual Healing: This type of healing involves the doctor's indirect influence through telepathy (or thought-transmission) and telekinetic projection, wherein the patient is affected via the doctor's Mind (Shen), Will (Zhi), and Intention (Yi).

【18】•    Divine Healing: This type of healing involves the doctor's direct fusion with the Dao, wherein the patient is miraculously healed via divine intervention.

【19】LEARNING TO BE A HEALER

【20】In ancient China, the early doctors of energetic medicine were actually powerful shamans (called Wu Yi), who believed that the birth, existence, transformation, and the death of everything in the universe happened under the influence of Qi. Thus, one of the most important skills and functions for the Wu Yi was the use of materializing and dematerializing energy. The Wu Yi's psychic abilities and energetic skills were simply a by-product of his or her energetic and spiritual development.

【21】In ancient China, it was also believed that healers came into existence through two manifestations: Ordained and Apprenticed, described as follows :

【22】1\.    Ordained: These were naturally gifted healers, believed to be gifted through the Divine to work miracles and heal diseases. Several "ordained" healers became the apprentices of older masters, who, after observing their skills, sought to give them guidance.

【23】2\.    Apprenticed: These were healers, who, through means of personal refinement, interaction with a master and the consistent application of technical modalities learned to work miracles and heal diseases.

【24】Both the "Ordained" and the "Apprenticed" healers would eventually train in Shengong meditations and exercises. Shengong meditations and exercises focus on the development of powerful skills in mental concentration, visualization, and imagination, and are used in order to improve and refine the individual's energetic skills. Being proficient in these skills is important in acquiring the mastery over materializing and dematerializing energy.

【25】The skills acquired from practicing the Shengong meditations also enabled the healers to access the "still point" contained within their center core Taiji Pole. Accessing the "still point" allowed the healer the ability to energetically dissolve his or her mind's perceptive intentions into the infinite space of the Wuji. Within the infinite space of Wuji, the individual was then able to transcend space and time, and attune his or her consciousness to the vibrations of any object. This allowed the healer the ability to reexperience every thought vibration at-

This energetic skill is sometimes called "Psychometry," and is used by Medical Qigong doctors to accurately diagnose the formations of energetic clusters within the patient's tissue and cells.</u>

【27】Once the Qigong doctor connects to the energy field of the patient, he or she will be able to access specific information about the patient imprinted within the energetic impressions of the patient's physical, energetic, and spiritual bodies. This allows the doctor to study and learn about the patient's past history of disease or illness, as well as the information contained within the molecular structures of the patient's tissues .

【28】The Qigong doctor's "true self" is defined as his or her pure innate spiritual existence (Yuan Shen) void of fabricated ego masks and acquired personalities (Shen Zhi). The "true self" is spiritually connected to, and rooted in, the energy of the Divine. It is the part of the soul that unconditionally accepts self and others and is more in the role of a compassionate observer rather than a judge. The "true self" allows the doctor to observe the patient's condition (spiritual, emotional, mental, energetic, and physical) void of any personal emotional biases. The "true self" is a state where unconditional love and acceptance is fostered and supported by the Divine.

【29】Uncovering the “True Self” Meditation

【30】To discover the "true self", the Qigong doctor is trained through special Shengong meditations used to unmask his or her core self. One such meditation asks the question, "Who are You?" and is described as follows:

【31】•    To begin, the instructor is seated in front of the student, and energetically projects his or her Shen into the student's body, enveloping and energetically connecting with the student's Three Dantians.

【32】•    The instructor then projects his or her Shen into the student's core self by staring into the student's left eye and penetrating his or her Eternal Soul. This Shengong technique is used to connect with the student's human soul or Original Spirit (Yuan Shen), in order to access and awaken his or her Eternal Soul (Shen Xian).

【33】•    The instructor focuses intently on the student and begins to ask the question, "Who are You?"

【34】•    This question is repeated over and over until the student begins to realize and experience the energetic and spiritual components of his or her "true self."

【35】Discovering "who you are" is not determined through expressing a "correct" answer, but by actually experiencing the spiritual awakening. It is through the understanding and realization of this innate truth (which is inherent within one's own enlightenment) that frees the student from his or her acquired ego (known as the "Death of the Ego Fear"). Once the student awakens to the realization of who he or she truly is, the enlightened answer is then reflected by the light emitted from within the student's eyes (and not through any specific cognitive explanations). There is a saying from Lao Zi written in the Dao De Jing (The Way and Its Power) that explains this phenomenon: "The Dao that can be named is not the true Dao." When the student realizes his or her connection and relationship to the Dao, Divine knowledge becomes easily accessible as the individual quickly learns to dissolve into the infinite space of the Wuji and reconnect with the divine.

【36】Entering The Wuji: Infinite Space

【37】The infinite space of the Wuji, extending from the Divine, is an infinite ocean of microscopic vibrations through which all the realms of creation and all the different energetic worlds are constructed. Like an invisible web, it is through the Wuji that the Divine manifests its infinite form. By quieting the Mind, the boundless ocean of vibrations connected to everything contained within the Wuji can be accessed and realized.

【38】On the most fundamental level, all things are constructed of quantum energy, constantly exchanging information within the Wuji's inexhaustible energetic field. All matter in the universe is interconnected by energetic waves which pierce through time and space within the Wuji's sea of infinite energy.

【39】The stable state of matter depends on the dynamic interchange of subatomic particles flowing within the Wuji for its very existence. Similar to the ripples on a pond, energetic waves are expressed by periodic oscillations, moving through the medium of the Wuji on a subatomic level. Each energetic wave is encoded with information, and the Wuji field creates a medium enabling the molecules to communicate with each other in oscillating frequencies. As molecules slow down, they give off radiation and release encoded wave information about the history of the matter.

【40】In order to dissolve into the Wuji, the apprentice allows his or her true self to "fall" into an "altered" state of energetic experience known as the "center of space" and the "center of time." It is important to acknowledge the fact that space and time exist only in the mind and are not "out there" in the "objective" world. They are only ideas that are a creation of the belief structures of the analytical mind. Being able to transcend the space-time continuum allows the apprentice to connect with the multidimensional energetic fields, and also allows true access to the healing energies of the Divine.

【41】Space and Time within the Wuji

【42】Before and while treating the patient, the Qigong doctor should continually bring his or her "true self" into the "center of space" and the "center of time." This subtle energetic and spiritual transformation (i.e. existing within the Wuji) will assist the doctor in establishing and maintaining a sacred healing space for the patient, the treatment room, and for him or herself. The dissolution into the center of space and time should be achieved while performing the "One Through Ten Meditation" or during the "Three Invocations" . Once this subtle state of perception is achieved, the doctor can then allow him or herself to act as a divine observer, viewing the patient from a non-judgmental position.

【43】Finding the Center of Space

【44】Before treating a patient, the Qigong doctor must first place his or her body, mind, emotions, energy, and spiritual essence into a place of infinite existence called the "center of space." The "center of space" is actually a spiritual and energetic concept wherein the doctor imagines him or herself as being the actual center of the universe. This concept and image maintains that all energy, light, and energetic fields extend from the middle of the doctor's center core (Taiji Pole) and expand outward into infinite space (Wuji). The Wuji is the infinite ocean of vibrations with which all the realms of creation and all the different worlds are constructed. This energy continues to extend and envelop the entire universe and all the energetic dimensions beyond.

【45】The purpose of the following meditation is to recognize the fact that you are the center of your own consciousness, power, thought, and influence. Like the various planets circling around the sun, the infinite actions and transformations occurring within your own world revolve around you as an individual.

【46】As the doctor begins to concentrate and place his or her focus of attention on the energetic and spiritual nature of the Eternal Soul, all thought and images of the outside world begin to diminish. It is important that the Qigong doctor imagine and believe that he or she is the center of all space, and within the mind, know that the entire universe evolves and rotates around them. This image is not intended to develop a heightened state of vanity, inflated ego, or a narcissistic delusion. In truth, each individual is the very center of his or her own consciousness, created by the Divine, the purpose of this training is to awaken to this energetic and spiritual union. Until the ego recognizes itself as the center of thought, influence, and power, it will not be able to manifest these unique qualities and take responsibility for purposeful actions.

【47】To access the center of space within the Wuji, the doctor must relax and place his or her awakened "true self" into the center of the Taiji Pole, quietly connecting the core self with the Divine. It is important that the doctor recognize, know, and feel this connection to be true, and that every particle of the doctor's physical body is but a portion of the various Elements of the universe. It is from the orientation of the core self that a Medical Qigong doctor accesses the deeper, hidden, spiritual, and energetic fields of the patient's body. According to the Laws of Heaven from the Magical Pivot (Ling Shu), "moving power at the center of space is clear, quiet and subtle."

【48】According to the Laws of Man from the Magical Pivot (Ling Shu), "The unskilled physician grasps only the form when he uses the techniques of acupuncture. The superior physician understands the spirit, and knows that the subtleties and movements of energy are never separated from the Qi's center of space. 【8】Bronchiectasis. Bronchiectasis is a form of obstructive lung disease that is actually a type of bronchitis. It is a pro-gressive and chronic pulmonary condition that occurs after infections such as childhood pneumonia or CF.

【9】Although bronchiectasis was once a common disease because of measles， pertussis， tuberculosis， and poorly treated bacterial pneumonias， the prevalence of bronchiectasis has diminished greatly since the introduction of antibiotics. It is characterized by abnormal and permanent dilation of the large air passages leading into the lungs (bronchi) and by destruction of bronchial walls.

【10】Bronchiectasis is caused by repeated damage to bron-chial walls. The resultant destruction and bronchial dilation reduce bronchial wall movement so that secretions cannot be removed effectively from the lungs， and the person is predis-posed to frequent respiratory infections.

【11】This vicious cycle of bacterial infection and inflammation of the bronchial wall leads to loss of ventilation and irrevers-ible lung damage. Advanced bronchiectasis may cause pneu-monia， cor pulmonale， or right-sided ventricular failure.

【12】All pulmonary irritants， especially cigarette smoke， should be avoided. Postural drainage， adequate hydration， good nutrition， and bronchodilator therapy in bronchospasm are important components in treatment. Antibiotics are used during disease exacerbations (e.g.， increased cough， purulent sputum， hemoptysis， malaise， and weight loss). The use of immunomodulatory therapy to alter the host response directly， and thereby reduce tissue damage， is under investigation.8，9

【16】Emphysema. Emphysema may develop in a person after a long history of chronic bronchitis in which the alveolar walls are destroyed， leading to permanent overdistention of the air space and loss of normal elastic tension in the lung tissue.

【17】Air passages are obstructed as a result of these changes(rather than as a result of mucous production， as in chronic bronchitis). Difficult expiration in emphysema is caused by the destruction of the walls (septa) between the alveoli， by partial airway collapse， and by the loss of elastic recoil.

【18】As the alveoli and septa collapse， pockets of air form between the alveolar spaces (called blebs) and within the lung parenchyma (called bullae). This process leads to increased ventilatory “dead space，" or areas that do not participate in gas or blood exchange. The WOB is increased because there is less functional lung tissue to exchange oxygen and CO2Emphysema also causes destruction of the pulmonary capil-laries， further decreasing oxygen perfusion and ventilation.

【19】In advanced emphysema， oxygen therapy is usually nec-essary to treat the progressive hypoxemia that occurs as the disease worsens. Oxygen therapy is carefully titrated and monitored to maintain venous oxygen saturation levels at or slightly above 90%. Too much oxygen can depress the respi-ratory drive of a person with emphysema.

【20】The drive to breathe in a healthy person results from an increase in the arterial CO， level (PCO)). In the normal adult， increased COz levels stimulate chemoreceptors in the brain-stem to increase the respiratory rate. With some chronic lung disorders these central chemoreceptors may become desen-sitized to PCOz changes， resulting in a dependence on the peripheral chemoreceptors to detect a fall in arterial oxygen levels (PO2) to stimulate the respiratory drive. Therefore too much oxygen delivered as a treatment can depress the respi-ratory drive in those individuals with COPD who have a dampening in their CO， drive.

Monitoring respiratory rate， level of oxygen administered by nasal canula， and oxygen saturation levels is very impor-tant in this client population. Some pulmonologists agree that supplemental oxygen levels can be increased during activity without compromising the individual because they|删除0换行|will “blow it (CO2) off"anyway. To our knowledge， there is no evidence yet to support this clinical practice.

【22】Types of Emphysema. There are three types of emphy-sema. Centrilobular emphysema ， the most com-mon type， destroys the bronchioles， usually in the upper lung regions. Inflammation develops in the bronchioles， but usu-ally the alveolar sac remains intact.

【23】Panlobular emphysema destroys the more distal alveolar walls， most commonly involving the lower lung. This destruc-tion of alveolar walls may occur secondary to infection or to irritants (most commonly cigarette smoke). These two forms of emphysema， collectively called centriacinar emphysema， occur most often in smokersS.

【24】_Paraseptal (or panacinar) emphysema destroys the alveoli_ in the lower lobes of the lungs， resulting in isolated blebs along the lung periphery. Paraseptal emphysema is believed to be the likely cause of spontaneous pneumothorax.

【25】_Clinical Signs and Symptoms. The irreversible destruc-_ tion reduces elasticity of the lung and increases the effort to exhale trapped air， causing marked dyspnea on exertion，later progressing to dyspnea at rest. Cough is uncommon.

【26】The client is often thin， has tachypnea with prolonged expiration， and uses the accessory muscles for respiration. The client often leans forward with the arms braced on the knees to support the shoulders and chest for breathing.

【27】The combined effects of trapped air and alveolar distention change the size and shape of the client’s chest， causing a barrel chest and increased expiratory effort.

【28】As the disease progresses， there is a loss of surface area avail-able for gas exchange. In the final stages of emphysema，cardiac complications， especially enlargement and dilation of the right ventricle， may develop. The overloaded heart reaches its limit of muscular compensation and begins to fail (cor pulmonale).

【29】The most important factor in the treatment of emphysema is smoking cessation. The main goals for the client with emphy-sema are to improve oxygenation and decrease COz retention.

【30】Pursed-lip breathing causes resistance to outflow at the lips， which in turn maintains intrabronchial pressure and improves the mixing of gases in the lungs. This type of breath-ing should be encouraged to help the client get rid of the stale air trapped in the lungsS.，

【31】Exercise has not been shown to improve pulmonary func-tion but is used to enhance cardiovascular fitness and train skeletal muscles to function more effectively. Routine pro-gressive walking is the most common form of exercise.

【32】Lung volume reduction surgery is available for some individ-uals and improves not only lung function and exercise perfor-mance， but also activities of daily function and quality of life.10，11

【36】**Asthma**

【37】Asthma is a reversible obstructive lung disease caused by increased reaction of the airways to various stimuli. It is a chronic inflammatory condition with acute exacerbations that can be life-threatening if not properly managed. Our understanding of asthma has changed dramatically over the last decade.

【38】Asthma was once viewed as a bronchoconstrictive disor-der in which the airways narrowed， causing wheezing and breathing difficulties. Treatment with bronchodilators to open airways was the primary focus. Scientific evidence now supports the idea that asthma is primarily an inflammatory disorder in which the constriction of airways is a symptom of the underlying inflammation.

【44】**Immune Sensitization and Inflammation**

【45】There are two major components to asthma. When the immune system becomes sensitized to an allergen， usually through heavy exposure in early life， an inflammatory cascade occurs， extending beyond the upper airways into the lungs.

【46】The lungs become hyperreactive， responding to allergens and other irritants in an exaggerated way. This hyperresponsiveness causes the muscles of the airways to constrict， making breathing more difficult . The second component is inflamma-tion， which causes the air passages to swell and the cells lining the passages to produce excess mucus， further impairing breathing.

【47】Asthma may be categorized as conventional asthma， occupa-tional asthma， or exercise-induced asthma (EIA)， but the under-lying pathophysiologic complex remains the same. Because the triggers or allergens vary， each person reacts differently. SOB， wheezing， tightness in the chest， and cough are the most com-monly reported symptoms， but other symptoms may also occur.

【56】**Pneumonia**

【57】Pneumonia is an inflammation of thelungs and can be caused by(1) aspiration of food， fluids， or vomitus； (2) inhalation of toxic or caustic chemicals， smoke， dust， or gases； or (3) a bacterial， viral， or mycoplasmal infection. It may be primary or secondary(a complication of another disease)； it often follows influenza.

【58】The common feature of all types of pneumonia is an inflammatory pulmonary response to the offending organ-ism or agent. This response may involve one or both lungs at the level of the lobe (lobar pneumonia) or more distally beginning in the terminal bronchioles and alveoli (broncho-pneumonia). Bronchopneumonia is seen more frequently than lobar pneumonia and is common in clients postop-eratively and in clients with chronic bronchitis， particularly when these two situations coexist.

【59】There are three main types of pneumonia： hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP； also known as nosocomial pneumonia)， ven-tilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)， and community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). By definition， HAP occurs 48 hours or more after hospital admission； when HAP develops in a mechanically ventilated patient after endotracheal intubation， it becomes VAP.

【60】**Risk Factors**

【61】Infectious agents responsible for pneumonia are typically present in the upper respiratory tract and cause no harm unless resistance is lowered severely by some other factor such as smoking， a severe cold， disease， alcoholism， or gen-erally poor health (e.g.，poorly controlled diabetes， chronic renal problems， compromised immune function).

【62】Risk factors for developing hospital-acquired pneumonia are age older than 70 years， serious comorbidities， malnutri-tion， impaired consciousness， prolonged hospitalization， and COPD.1’ Older or bedridden clients are particularly at risk because of physical inactivity and immobility. Limited mobil-ity causes normal secretions to pool in the airways and facili-tates bacterial growth. Other risk factors predisposing a client to pneumonia are listed in Box 7.3.

【63】Pneumocystis carinii is a protozoan organism that rarely causes pneumonia in healthy individuals. Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP) has been the most common life-threatening opportunistic infection in persons with acquired immunodefi-ciency syndrome (AIDS). PCP also has been shown to be the first indicator of conversion from human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection to the designation of AIDS.

【55】**Acute Calcific Bursitis and Tendinitis**

【58】Lause

【59】It was once believed that acute bursitis was related to rupture of the bursa due to a calcific process in the tendon. The calcified tendon is visible on a radiograph and was thought to represent a degener-ative process. 【64】An attempt at sling support and palliative physical therapy application may be made， Evidence sug-gests that ultrasound helps in resorption of the caleific deposits." After a nine-month follow-up period， 42% of patients had calcific deposition resolution and 23% had partial resolution if they had been treated with the pulsed ultrasound regimen. 【1】**MARROW INFILTRATE WITH FIBROSIS**

Numerous reactive and malignant disorders are associated with BM fibrosis ， including PMF， CML， PV， acute megakaryoblastic leukemia， systemic mastocytosis， acute panmyelosis with myelofibrosis， infectious disease(granulomas)， MDS with fibrosis， HCL， non-HL， HL， HIV infection， treatment with hematopoietic growth factors fol-lowing bone damage (necrosis， irradiation， fracture)， some metabolic disorders， autoimmune disorders e.g.， systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)\]， HIV infection， and metastatic tumors. The fibrosis is usually composed of reticulin fibers， but may also include collagen. The latter may be accom-panied by osteosclerosis. Special stains that are helpful in|删除0换行|identifying fibrosis include Mallory's， van Gieson’s， Gomori’s， and Masson's.**

【3】**The marrow fibrosis is most often classified into four grades (0-3) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[42\]</u>：**

【4】**1\. Grade 0 corresponds to the normal BM with no intersections (a scattered linear reticulin may be present)**

【5】**2\. Grade 1 shows loose reticulin fibers with intersec-tions， most pronounced around vessels.**

【6】**3\. Grade 2 shows diffuse and dense fibrosis with extensive intersections.**

【7】4\. Grade 3 differs from grade 2 by coarse bundles of collagen often associated with osteosclerosis.

【8】**Some authors use 0-4 grading system (0， no reticulin fibers；1， occasional fine fibers， mostly around vessels； 2， diffuse fine fiber network； 3， diffuse fiber network with scattered thick coarse fibers； 4， diffuse and coarse fiber network with areas of collagen fibrosis) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[43\]</u>. ET at the time of diagnosis is not associated with reticulin fibrosis (its presence excludes the diagnosis of ET)， but similarly to PV， ET may progress into fibrotic stage during the course of the disease. Positive Philadelphia chromosome (BCR-ABLI) confirms CML with fibrosis， and the presence of JAK2 V617F mutation excludes the sec-ondary causes of BM fibrosis. The differential diagnosis of MDS with fibrosis or mixed MDS/MPN with fibrosis (e.g.， RARS-T) with early PMF may be difficult.

【11】**PLASMACYTOSIS**

Increased numbers of plasma cells may be associated with reactive conditions (polyclonal plasmacytosis) and plasma cell neoplasms. The causes of reactive plasmacy-tosis include inflammatory conditions， chronic infections(mostly viral， but also certain bacterial)， autoimmune disor-ders， hypersensitivity states， HL， anemia (megaloblastic and iron deficiency)， cirrhosis， and occasional cases of CML， AML， and metastatic carcinoma. B-cell lymphomas may be accompanied by polyclonal or monoclonal plasmacytosis. Rarely， some T-cell lymphomas (e.g.， AITL) may also be|删除0换行|associated with often prominent plasmacytosis mimicking plasma cell neoplasms. PCM and monoclonal gammopath1yo.f undetermined significance (MGUS) are defined by the presence of monoclonal plasma cell population. The pres-ence of reactive， perivascular plasmacytosis is often seen in secondary polycythemia and helps in differentiating it from PV. The reactive plasmacytosis， although sometimes very prominent， is usually composed of scattered， nonag-gregated plasma cells， which are polytypic by immunohis-tochemistry (or flow cytometry).

【114】**INTRODUCTION**

【115】Flow cytometry (FC) plays a very important role in diagnosis， subclassification， and posttreatment monitoring of hematologic neoplasms 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-26\]</u>. FC results allow to choose the most appro-priate further testing \[such as fluorescence in situ hybridiza-tion (FISH) or polymerase chain reaction (PCR)\] to establish the definite diagnosis and to further characterize the malig-nant process in a timely manner. Multiparameter FC measures simultaneously several surface and/or intracytoplasmic mark-ers on a single cell， allowing for accurate phenotypic charac-terization of analyzed population(s). While no single marker permits a definite lineage assignment， analysis with panels of antibodies allows for separation of hematologic tumors into very precise subtypes with different prognosis and treat-ment requirements， as defined by the current World Health Organization classification of hematopoietic and lymphoid atA tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[27\]</u>. FC analysis can precisely differentiate between B-and T-cell malignancies， and between mature (peripheral) and precursor tumors， and determine the myeloid or lym-phoid lineage among the latter. Availability of new markers(antibodies) and new fluorochromes， and improvement in instrumentation not only increases the accuracy of FC stud-ies and allows for identification of a minute abnormal popula-tion among the majority of benign cells， but also expands FC applications into disorders such as myelodysplastic syndromes(MDSs)， paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)， or myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，18，26，28-34\]</u>.

【116】**FC immunophenotyping includes the evaluation of the expression of specific antigens (markers) along with light scat-tering properties of the cells. The analyzed parameters are compared to those expected in normal (benign) counterpart. Presence of any difference in the pattern of expression-for example， lack of antigen expression， decreased or increased intensity of staining， variable (heterogeneous) expression， or presence of a marker that is not typically seen in normal counterpart (e.g.， lymphoid markers in myeloid cells or pan-myeloid markers in lymphoid cells)-allows for identifica-tion of abnormal population. Once the abnormal population is identified， evaluation of additional markers may be help-ful to further characterize the process and often allow dis-ease monitoring. Based on the immunophenotypic features， possible entities or specific diagnosis (whenever possible) is suggested along with recommendation for additional testing(when applicable)， such as morphology (e.g.， blast enumera-tion； nodular or diffuse pattern of lymph node involvement)， cytogenetics， FISH (e.g.， PML-RARA， IGH-BCL2， MYC)， PCR (e.g.， BCR-ABLI， JAK2 mutation， T-cell clonality)， radiologic imaging studies (e.g.， bone lesions in patients with plasma cell neoplasm)， and laboratory data \[e.g.， serum M protein， serum erythropoietin level， human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1，etc.).**

【117】**FORWARD AND SIDE (ORTHOGONAL) LIGHT SCATTER**

Intrinsic physical properties of the cells， especially their size and cytoplasmic granularity， are measured simultaneously with fluorescence emission as the fluorochrome-tagged cells pass through laser light. The side scatter (SSC； right-angle/orthogonal 11.light scatter) corresponds to the granularity of the cytoplasm 通用删除1(英):<u>(y-axis in Figure 3.1)</u>. 【1】**MARROW INFILTRATE WITH FIBROSIS**

Numerous reactive and malignant disorders are associated with BM fibrosis ， including PMF， CML， PV， acute megakaryoblastic leukemia， systemic mastocytosis， acute panmyelosis with myelofibrosis， infectious disease(granulomas)， MDS with fibrosis， HCL， non-HL， HL， HIV infection， treatment with hematopoietic growth factors fol-lowing bone damage (necrosis， irradiation， fracture)， some metabolic disorders， autoimmune disorders e.g.， systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)\]， HIV infection， and metastatic tumors. The fibrosis is usually composed of reticulin fibers， but may also include collagen. The latter may be accom-panied by osteosclerosis. Special stains that are helpful in|删除0换行|identifying fibrosis include Mallory's， van Gieson’s， Gomori’s， and Masson's.**

【3】**The marrow fibrosis is most often classified into four grades (0-3) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[42\]</u>：**

【4】**1\. Grade 0 corresponds to the normal BM with no intersections (a scattered linear reticulin may be present)**

【5】**2\. Grade 1 shows loose reticulin fibers with intersec-tions， most pronounced around vessels.**

【6】**3\. Grade 2 shows diffuse and dense fibrosis with extensive intersections.**

【7】4\. Grade 3 differs from grade 2 by coarse bundles of collagen often associated with osteosclerosis.

【8】**Some authors use 0-4 grading system (0， no reticulin fibers；1， occasional fine fibers， mostly around vessels； 2， diffuse fine fiber network； 3， diffuse fiber network with scattered thick coarse fibers； 4， diffuse and coarse fiber network with areas of collagen fibrosis) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[43\]</u>. Fibrosis often accompanies**

【10】atypical lymphoid aggregates representing BM involvement by lymphoma. The most pronounced reticulin fibrosis is seen DyISmp in PMF. Advanced stages of PV and CML may also show marrow fibrosis. ET at the time of diagnosis is not associated with reticulin fibrosis (its presence excludes the diagnosis of ET)， but similarly to PV， ET may progress into fibrotic stage during the course of the disease. Positive Philadelphia chromosome (BCR-ABLI) confirms CML with fibrosis， and the presence of JAK2 V617F mutation excludes the sec-ondary causes of BM fibrosis. The differential diagnosis of MDS with fibrosis or mixed MDS/MPN with fibrosis (e.g.， RARS-T) with early PMF may be difficult.

【11】**PLASMACYTOSIS**

Increased numbers of plasma cells may be associated with reactive conditions (polyclonal plasmacytosis) and plasma cell neoplasms. The causes of reactive plasmacy-tosis include inflammatory conditions， chronic infections(mostly viral， but also certain bacterial)， autoimmune disor-ders， hypersensitivity states， HL， anemia (megaloblastic and iron deficiency)， cirrhosis， and occasional cases of CML， AML， and metastatic carcinoma. B-cell lymphomas may be accompanied by polyclonal or monoclonal plasmacytosis. Rarely， some T-cell lymphomas (e.g.， AITL) may also be|删除0换行|associated with often prominent plasmacytosis mimicking plasma cell neoplasms. PCM and monoclonal gammopath1yo.f undetermined significance (MGUS) are defined by the presence of monoclonal plasma cell population. The pres-ence of reactive， perivascular plasmacytosis is often seen in secondary polycythemia and helps in differentiating it from PV. The reactive plasmacytosis， although sometimes very prominent， is usually composed of scattered， nonag-gregated plasma cells， which are polytypic by immunohis-tochemistry (or flow cytometry).

【13】**NONHEMATOPOIETIC TUMORS**

【14】Extrinsic tumors are usually easily discernible . Some cases， however， require confirmatory immunohisto-chemistry staining to identify the metastatic disease and determine the site of origin， especially if marrow findings are the first sign of malignant (metastatic) tumor.

Irregular or bipo-lar cytoplasmic projections may also be seen in splenic lymphoma withvillousSlymphocytes(Figurree 2.26lD Largelymphoidcellss have irregular nuelei， an increased nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio， and occa-sionally prominent nucleoli. T-cell lymphoproliferations are characterized by prominent nuclear contour irregularities， with occasional flower-like cells. T prolymphocytes have prominent nucleoli  and LGLs have coarse azurophilic granules in the cyto-plasm . Lymphoblasts  have a scanty cytoplasm， a medium-sized nucleus with delicate evenly distributed chromatin， and one or more incon-spicuous nucleoli. Monocytosis in the peripheral blood may be associated with numerous reactive conditions and clonal disorders， including acute monoblastic leuke-mia  and CMML. The presence of imma-ture erythroid precursors 通用删除1(英):<u>(erythroblastosis； Figure 2.26L)</u> with prominent dyserythropoiesis may be seen in MDS or AEL. In the pediatric age group， erythroblasts in the peripheral blood may be seen in erythroblastosis fetalis or transient myeloproliferative disorders. In the latter， circulating erythroblasts are accompanied by megakaryocytes and large platelets. A few erythro-blasts may be present normally in the peripheral blood of newborn infants. Circulating erythroid precursors mixed with leftward shifted myeloid cells 通用删除1(英):<u>(leukoerythroblastosis； Figure 2.26N)</u> are seen in a variety of reactive conditions as well as MPN and myelophthisic processes. Neutrophilia with a leftward shift accompanied by eosin-ophilia and basophilia is seen in CML. Plasma cells in the peripheral blood  may indicate an aggressive or advanced PCM； plasma cell leukemia is characterized by a leukocyte differential with >20% plasma cells. The presence of“leukemic” carcinoma in the peripheral blood is rare . Erythrophagocytosis by immature cells is most often seen in acute monoblastic leukemia but can also be seen in other types of acute leukemias.</u>

【114】**INTRODUCTION**

【115】Flow cytometry (FC) plays a very important role in diagnosis， subclassification， and posttreatment monitoring of hematologic neoplasms 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-26\]</u>. FC results allow to choose the most appro-priate further testing \[such as fluorescence in situ hybridiza-tion (FISH) or polymerase chain reaction (PCR)\] to establish the definite diagnosis and to further characterize the malig-nant process in a timely manner. Multiparameter FC measures simultaneously several surface and/or intracytoplasmic mark-ers on a single cell， allowing for accurate phenotypic charac-terization of analyzed population(s). While no single marker permits a definite lineage assignment， analysis with panels of antibodies allows for separation of hematologic tumors into very precise subtypes with different prognosis and treat-ment requirements， as defined by the current World Health Organization classification of hematopoietic and lymphoid atA tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[27\]</u>. FC analysis can precisely differentiate between B-and T-cell malignancies， and between mature (peripheral) and precursor tumors， and determine the myeloid or lym-phoid lineage among the latter. Availability of new markers(antibodies) and new fluorochromes， and improvement in instrumentation not only increases the accuracy of FC stud-ies and allows for identification of a minute abnormal popula-tion among the majority of benign cells， but also expands FC applications into disorders such as myelodysplastic syndromes(MDSs)， paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)， or myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，18，26，28-34\]</u>.

【116】**FC immunophenotyping includes the evaluation of the expression of specific antigens (markers) along with light scat-tering properties of the cells. The analyzed parameters are compared to those expected in normal (benign) counterpart. Presence of any difference in the pattern of expression-for example， lack of antigen expression， decreased or increased intensity of staining， variable (heterogeneous) expression， or presence of a marker that is not typically seen in normal counterpart (e.g.， lymphoid markers in myeloid cells or pan-myeloid markers in lymphoid cells)-allows for identifica-tion of abnormal population. Once the abnormal population is identified， evaluation of additional markers may be help-ful to further characterize the process and often allow dis-ease monitoring. 【129】**2\. CNS involvement：**

**c. Uveitis and bilateral VIIth nerve palsy (Hereford’s syndrome)|删除0换行|d. Myelopathy from involvement of the dura with compression of the spinal cord**

e. CSF； sugar 30-40 mg%； protein 80-150 mg% and lymphocytic pleocytosis|删除0换行|f. Rarely cranial nerve VIII and II are involved B. Clinical presentation：**

【134】**1\. Neuropathy may occur as isolated manifestation or as part of generalized disease**

【151】**A. General features：**

【152】1\. Exact incidence is unknown； appears common in pa-tients that have been in the ICU for greater than four weeks

【153】**2\. Need to distinguish it from concomitant acute myopa-thy (Type II fibers； thick myosin； corticosteroid in-duced myopathy； neuromuscular blocking agents)**

【155】**1\. Occurs in patients with sepsis and multiorgan failure(cardiac， pulmonary，renal，liver)**

【156】**2\. Quadriparesis**

【157】3\. Difficulty weaning from the respirator

【158】**4\. Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes**

【159】**5\. Less clear sensory deficit**

【160】**6\. Often concomitant encephalopathy**

【161】**7\. Residual weakness in distal muscles**

【165】**3\. Denervation**

【167】**1\. Axonal degeneration**

【168】**Neuropathy of Renal Failure**

【169】**A. General features：**

【170】**1\. Present in 80% of severely uremic patients； large per-centage may be asymptomatic but demonstrable by NCV abnormalities**

【171】**2\. Primarily related to the duration and severity of the re-nal failure**

【172】**3\. Males more often affected than females**

【173】**4\. Stable or improves with dialysis**

【174】**5\. Improves following suecessful renal transplantation**

【175】**B. Clinical presentation：**

【176】1\. Insidious onset； rarely acute or subacute

【177】**2\. Sensory neuropathy； painful tingling of the feet； burn-ing； band-like constrictions around the toes**

【178】**3\. Restless legs； muscle cramps**

【179】**d. Impaired position and vibration sensibility； there may be small fiber predominant variant**

【180】**4\. May have marked muscle wasting， concomitant Type II atrophy of proximal muscles**

【181】5\. Distal lower extremity weakness of anterior tibialis， extensors of the toe and eversion

【182】**6\. Decreased or absent deep tendon reflexes**

【183】**7\. Orthostatic hypotension， impotence and constipation are common**

【184】**8\. Increased incidence of CTS**

【185】**9\. Arteriovenous shunt placement in the arm may cause ischemic high median neuropathy**

【186】**10\. CTS may be secondary to deposition of beta2-migroglobulin (systemic amyloidosis as consequence of the renal failure)**

【187】**11\. Ulnar and peroneal compressive neuropathy may oc-cur concomitantly**

【190】**2\. No correlation between NCVs and clinical signs of neuropathy**

【191】**3\. After transplantation there may be rapid improvement of NCV followed by consistent improvement over time**

【192】4\. Progressive reduction of SNAPs and CMAPs

【193】**5\. Prolonged F-wave latencies**

【194】**6\. Denervation and reinvention noted by needle EMG in distal muscles**

【195】**7\. Small parasympathetic fiber abnormalities (R-R vari-ability) greater than sympathetic fiber loss**

【197】**1\. Creatinine clearance of less than 10 ml/minute has de-creased NCV**

【198】**2\. serum PTH inversely correlated with NCV**

【199】**3\. CSF**

【200】**a. Usually normal； may have slight increase in protein E. Pathology：**

【201】**1\. Axonal degeneration**

【202】**2\. Some segmental demyelination and remyelination**

【208】**1\. Rapidly progressive motor and sensory neuropathy**

【234】**1.Raree22. Probable autoimmune etiology**

【260】**Schwannoma**

【261】**A. General features：**

【262】**1\. The most common benign neural sheath tumor**

【263】**2\. Higher incidence in women than men**

【264】3\. May develop with Von Recklinghausen’s disease (neu-rofibroma muscle more common)

【265】**4.Well encapsulated and cause lateral displacement of adjacent fascicles**

【266】**B. Clinical presentation：**

【267】**1\. Positive Tinel’s sign (paresthesias elicited by mechani-cal stimulation) over the tumor in the distribution of the affected nerve**

【268】**2\. Rare presentation as a neurologic deficit of the affected nerye**

【269】**3\. Most common nerves affected：**

【270】**a. Supra greater than infraclavicular components of the brachial plexus**

【271】**b. Axillary and musculocutaneous nerve**

**c. Tibial nerve greater than sciatic nerve in the thigh|删除0换行|d. Median > ulnar > radial nerve； proximal portions of nerve > distal**

【276】**1) Verocay bodies are prominent**

【277】**b. Loose hypocellular regions (Antoni Type B)**

【286】**6\. Females>males**

【287】**7\. R> L side of the body**

【288】8\. Arise from the motor more often than sensory portion of the nerve

【289】**9\. Occur as a localized mass； may involve long segment of the nerve**

【290】**10\. No cleavage plane； total removal requires nerve sec tion**

【294】**b. Axillary nerve greater than deltoid**

【295】c. Pelvic plexus > sciatic nerve in the thigh

**2\. Painful particularly if partially resected|删除0换行|a. Tinel’s sign in the distribution of the nerve D. Pathology：**

【301】**A. General features：**

【302】**1\. Chromosome 17； AD with full penetrance， but variable**

【328】**Differential Diagnosis Points to Delineate Schwannoma from Neurofibroma**

【329】**1\. Neurofibroma is suspected in the face of other stigmata of VRD (rarely Schwannomas can appear in this setting)**

【330】**2\. Neurofibroma more local and radicular pain**

【331】**3\. Tinel’s sign is prominent in both**

【332】4\. Incidence of Schwannoma higher in women than men

【384】**1\. Subeutaneous location**

**2\. Sites； forearm (posterior interosseous nerve compres-|删除0换行|sion； popliteal fossa (peroneal palsy)； supraclavicular**

【6】**◆ Complicated renal cyst of the left upper pole： The water attenuation of the lesion fits for a simple cyst； however， the perceptible wall excludes the diagnosis of a simple cyst. A cyst that is infected or hemorrhagic could have this appearance.**

【7】**◆CCystic renal cell carcinoma (RCC)： Some RCCs are cystic； others can measure in the range of water atten-uation due to extensive necrosis or hemorrhage.**

【8】**◆Renal abscess： An infection within the kidney that has liquefied could have this appearance. It is helpful in these cases to corrclate imaging findings with urinaly-sis， as well as possible clinical symptoms such as py-rexia， leukocytosis， and flank pain.**

【9】**◆Ureteral duplication with obstruction of the upper pole moiety： This diagnosis can be made due to the presence of the fluid attenuation tubular structure adjacent to the left ureter. This tubular structure may be confused with a thrombosed gonadal vein， and therefore its path must be followed. If this tubular structure enters the left renal vcin， a thrombosed gonadal vein can be diagnosed. If this tubular struc-ture is in continuity with the cystic upper pole mass， the diagnosis of an obstruction duplicated system can be made with confidence. This will subsequently be confirmed by cystoscopy， with the identification of two ureteral orificcs on this side.**

【10】**DIAGNOSIS： Obstruction of the upper pole col-lecting system in complete ureteral duplication.**

【11】**KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【12】**Patient with obstruction of the upper pole moiety may present with nonspecific abdominal pain； this is the most common factor leading to clinical evaluation.**

【13】**Alternatively， patients may present with lower tract signs and symptoms related to the ectopic insertion of the duplicated ureter-e.g.， incontinence.**

【14】**◆Other presentations may be related to obstruction of the upper pole moiety and the presence of calculus dis-ease (hematuria) or stages of urine (infection).**

【15】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

**Duplication anomalies of the kidney are common. In patients with a completely duplicated system， both ureters may insert orthotopically； however， the ureter arising from the upper pole moiety frequently inserts ectopically either intravesically or extravesically. Patients most often present with symptoms related to|删除0换行|upper pole obstruction or lower pole reflux.**

【17】**◆1Imaging is useful for documenting the presence of complete duplication and whether the upper polc is obstructed. CT is useful for evaluating the amount of residual parenchyma in the upper pole. Cystography is frequently used to document reflux. Ultrasound can image the obstructed upper pole but usually cannot image the entire ureter.**

【22】**A 48-year-old woman is referred for renal ultrasound following a urinary tract infection.**

【23】通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 4-16A Ultrasound of the left kidney in the transverse plane. There is a 2.5-cm diameter， well-demarcated， uniformly echogenic mass in the posterior mid cortex.**</u>

【24】通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 4-16B Contrast-enhanced CT of the left kidney. There is a corresponding mass that is of mixed soft tissue and fatty attenuation. A region-of-interest measurement obtained from a low-attenuation area of the mass reads -18 Hounsfield units (HU). This suggests the presence of fat.**</u>

【25】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【26】**Renal cell carcinoma (RCC)： Approximately 30% of small RCCs are markedly hypcrcchoic. The presence of either small intratumoral cyst or an anechoic rim can suggest RCC. Thin-section CT must be performed for characterization of a hypcrechoic mass. Fat-containing RCCs with osseous metaplasia have also been report-ed， although they are extremely rare. RCCs can also contain low attenuation of foci due to lipid-producing necrosis. These tumors contain lipid vacuoles and amalgamated cholesterol clefts. An RCC can also grow by extension and entrap perirenal fat. RCCs that behave in this fashion tend to be largc， >5 cm in diam-eter， and have irregular margins.**

【27】**◆ Lipoma： A lipoma is a rare benign tumor of the kid-ney composed of adipose tissue.**

【28】**◆ILiposarcoma： A renal liposarcoma is usually located peripherally， beneath the renal capsulc. The tumor is large and bulky and extends into the perirenal space.**

【29】**Fat-containing renal oncocytoma： Fat may be pre-sent within an oncocytoma that grows sufficiently large to entrap perirenal or sinus fat.**

【30】**◆Adrenal myelolipoma： A full examination of ultra-sound and CT images should help distinguish a fat containing adrenal mass from a fat-containing renal mass. MRI with sagittal and coronal imaging may improve the ability to distinguish a renal angiolipoma from an adrenal myelolipoma.**

【31】**◆Renal angiomyolipoma (AML)： This is the most likely diagnosis for a fat-containing renal mass.**

【32】**◆DIAGNOSIS： Renal angiomyolipoma (AML).**

【33】**KEY FACTS**

【34】**_CLINICAL_**

【35】**AMLs are benign hamartomas composed of fat， smooth muscle， and blood vessels.**

【36】**◆Eighty percent of AMLs are solitary； they occur spo-radically， and they are most common in women 40 to60 years of age.**

【37】**Twenty percent are multiple and bilateral， usually in association with tuberous sclerosis.**

【38】**These tumors are usually an incidental finding.**

【39】**_◆_ Hemorrhage may occur when lesions are large， pro-ducing hematuria， flank pain， and in severe cases， shock.**

【40】**◆Treatment of AMLs includes embolization or resec-tion， especially if the AML is >4 cm in diameter， to avoid the threat of spontaneous hemorrhage.**

【41】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【42】**__ Plain films may reveal subtlc lucencies due to fat con-tent； however， this finding is seen in <10% of cases. Calcifications are seldom scen， and when present， sug gest an RCC.**

【43】**Intravenous urography reveals a nonspecific mass， which is frequently exophytic.**

【44】**Ultrasound demonstrates a well-demarcated， highly echogenic renal mass， although echo-poor areas may be seen due to internal necrosis or hemorrhage， partic-ularly in larger tumors.**

【45】**◆On CT， either with or without contrast material， the presence of fat (<-10 HU) is virtually diagnostic. In some AMLs， however， the fat is microscopic， and because of partial volume averaging， no fatty attenua-tion will be appreciated.**

【46】**With angiography， 95% of the tumors are hypervascu-lar， with dilated arteries. Angiography， however， is rarcly performed unless embolization is anticipated.**

【47】**On MRI， there is variable high signal intensity on Tl-weighted images and intermediate signal intensity on T2-weighted images depending on the fat content.**

【58】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【59】**◆ Renal abscess： One would expect appropriate sympto-matology in a patient with an abscess of this size. A thickened wall that enhances can be seen in a renal abscess. However， lack of inflammatory changes in the perinephric fat may suggest other diagnostic possibili-ties.**

【60】**◆ Hemorrhagic cyst： Over time the attenuation within a hemorrhagic renal cyst may decrease， causing an old hemorrhagic cyst to have a more cystic appearance. The eccentric， lateral wall prominence that enhances， however， prevents one from calling this lesion a hem-orrhagic cyst.**

【61】**◆Cystic RCC： This is the most likely diagnosis for a cystic renal mass with an enhancing mural nodule.**

【62】**DIAGNOSIS： Cystic renal cell carcinoma， Bosniak type 4 lesion.**

【63】**KEY FACTS _CLINICAI_**

【64】**Patients with RCC may present with the classic triad of pain， mass， and hematuria.**

【65】**Other symptoms include fatigue， malaise， anorexia， weight loss， fever， and anemia.**

【66】**_◆_ Men arc most commonly afflicted， with a male-to-female ratio of 2 to 1.**

【67】**◆IPatients are typically in the sixth to seventh decade.**

【68】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

**__ A Bosniak type 4 cyst is one that clearly has malignant features S aass well as large cystic components. Lesions in this category show irregular margins and solid enhanc-|删除0换行|ing elements. They are clearly malignant and should be treated surgically.**

【70】**◆Cysts are sometimes complicated by the presence of calcifications， septations， abnormal attenuation， wall thickening， or nodularity. A solid nodule within a cyst lumen that enhances is a feature that indicates the presence of a malignancy with high reliability. Vascularity within the nodule combined with nodular thickening of a cyst wall is also a clear indication of malignancy.**

【71】**◆This lesion should not be classified as a Bosniak type 3lesion. Type 3 cysts exhibit some of the features of malignant lesions and radiographically cannot be dis-tinguished from malignancy. Resection is necessary to distinguish a benign from a malignant lesion.**

【72】**_◆_ A multilocular cystic nephroma is a benign Bosniak type 3 lesion， while a multicystic RCC is a malignant Bosniak type 3 lcsion. These two tumors may be indis-tinguishable radiographically.**

【81】**A 62-year-old man has a history of chronic urinary tract infections.**

【82】通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 4-18 Anteroposterior view from a left retrograde pyelogram. Multiple small filling defects are present in the left ureter.**</u>

【83】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【84】**Blood clots： Blood clots can causc multiple uretcral filling defects. One would expect that the patient would havc an accompanying history of hematuria. Additional history may be helpful and could include known bleeding disorders or trauma.**

【85】**_◆_ Multiple ureteral stones： Stones can cause multiple filling defects， although typically， due to their calcium content， stones are most often radiopaque. This limits their detectability on contrasted examinations. The fixed nature of the filling defects， as seen in this patient， would make this an unlikely possibility.**

【86】**◆Multiple ureteral transitional cell carcinomas(TCCs)： While TCC has a propensity to be multifocal， this would represent an extremely rare manifestation of urothelial carcinoma. Correlation should be made with findings of urine cytology to establish whether malig-nant cells are present.**

【87】**Ureteritis cystica： This is one of several causes of mul-tiple ureteral filling defects. Ureteritis cystica is often seen in the setting of chronic urinary tract infections.**

【88】**DIAGNOSIS： Ureteritis cystica.**

【89】**KEY FACTS**

【90】**_CLINICAL_**

【91】**◆Ureteritis cystica is associated with chronic mucosal irritation secondary to inflammation.**

【92】**◆These lesions are secondary to degeneration and cavi tation of metaplastic surface urethelium or submucosal Brunn’s cell nests.**

【93】**Patients may bc asymptomatic or have hematuria and symptoms of a urinary tract infection.**

【94】**◆These lesions are not premalignant.**

【95】**The lesions may be unilateral or bilateral.**

【96】**◆Females are affected slightly more with ureteritis cysti-ca than males.**

【97】**_Patients are typically 50 to 60 years old._**

【98】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【99】**◆Lesions arc typically 2 to 3 mm in size， although they can range from l mm to 2 cm in size.**

【100】**Lesions are multiple， smooth， well-rounded or oval filling defects with sharp borders.**

【101】**Lesions are said to predominate in the proximal ureter but may be seen throughout the ureter， in the renal pelvis (pyelitis cystica)， or in the bladder (cystitis cystica).**
